jobs.description: What the Role Does: Transform search engine marketing data into smarter campaigns and high-performing digital marketing strategies. As a Data Analyst - Digital Marketing, you will combine strong analytical skills with hands-on ownership of a large-scale search engine marketing portfolio. You will use campaign performance data, financial results, internal reporting, and AI-enabled tools to uncover opportunities and improve campaign profitability, quality, efficiency, and return on investment. You will also apply creative skills to develop clear, customer-focused advertising that helps more people around the world access modern legal solutions. This is a full-time, permanent position working 37.5 hours per week, with the option to work hybrid from our Edmonton, Alberta office. What You’ll Do: - Plan, implement, and manage a portfolio of paid search campaigns across Google Ads and Microsoft Advertising to increase website traffic and drive conversions - Analyze campaign performance data, financial results, and key performance indicators to uncover actionable campaign change tactics - Optimize and adjust campaign bids to maximize profitability and ensure peak performance - Review campaign structures, budgets, targeting, and other performance levers to improve efficiency and maximize profitability - Utilize AI-enabled tools and workflows to improve campaign management quality, identify optimization opportunities, and make faster data-informed decisions - Monitor data quality and campaign health, investigate variances, and implement solutions that support accurate reporting and dependable campaign management - Conduct keyword, search query, competitor, and market research to identify campaign optimization and growth opportunities - Build product level knowledge to evaluate advertising opportunities and tailor campaign strategies to customer needs - Review user level information to develop relevant audience segments and targeting strategies - Research paid search platforms, AI capabilities, new advertising formats, and industry developments to identify valuable new approaches and stay up to date on best practices - Communicate complex analysis and recommendations clearly to support informed decision-making - Collaborate with cross functional Legal, Product, and Development teams to execute projects - Support creative work by writing compelling advertising copy, crafting brand messaging, contributing to landing page updates, and coordinating image and video assets within the advertising platforms What You Bring: The Essentials - Post-secondary education in Business, Marketing, Finance, Management Information Systems, Operations Management, Data Science, Economics, Math, Computing Science, or another analysis-related program - Experience analyzing large datasets to identify trends, patterns, and actionable insights - Advanced Microsoft Excel skills, including experience with complex formulas, PivotTables, data visualizations, and data analysis - Experience using AI tools to support campaign changes, analysis, reporting, writing, research, and productivity - Excellent time management skills and the ability to balance multiple projects - Strong written English communication skills, with the ability to develop concise, persuasive advertising copy and conversion-focused messaging - Sound judgement and strong data-driven decision-making ability - Ability to communicate findings clearly, synthesize complex analysis, and make actionable recommendations - Natural curiosity and a strong problem-solving mindset, with a track record of fast learning and adapting to new platforms or methodologies - A collaborative working style and the ability to contribute effectively across team projects The Nice to Haves (Great if you have it and we’ll help you learn if you don’t) - Knowledge of PPC / SEM campaign management (Google Ads, Microsoft Advertising) and marketing KPIs - Proficiency with Power BI for data visualization and business intelligence - Experience with Google Analytics, or other marketing analytics tools - Experience with Python, VBA, R, or related analytical and automation tools Why You Should Join the LawDepot Team: - Excellent total compensation package - Comprehensive health and dental benefits, plus an additional Health Care Spending / Personal Spending Account - Great work life balance (37.5 hour work weeks, flexible schedules, ability to bank hours) - Three weeks paid vacation, plus bonus personal days - Continuous learning opportunities, including LinkedIn Learning subscriptions and training budgets - Company share plan - Free catered lunches for the entire office - Monthly social events for team members to enjoy (think axe throwing, rock climbing, board games, food trucks, trivia contests, and charitable activities) - Work alongside talented, driven colleagues in a culture focused on quality, reliability, innovation, and growth - Personal offices for focused work and to have your individual space (plus collaborative workspaces for when you want to meet with the team) - Free and easily accessible parking - Southgate Mall, Whyte Ave, and Calgary Trail restaurants are only minutes away - Hybrid working arrangements for that balance between getting work done at home and engaging with others in the office Who We Are: Join one of the fastest growing companies in Canada! LawDepot is proud to be a seven-time Growth 500 ranked organization and a major player in the Global legal solutions industry. Our mission is to modernize the legal document creation experience by empowering people with fast, easy-to-use, and professional solutions. With over ten million satisfied customers worldwide, over two million monthly website visitors, and billions of dollars saved on legal fees, you will be joining a team that is truly making a difference. At LawDepot, we foster a collaborative and inclusive learning culture that values excellence. Apply today and become a part of our exciting journey! How to Apply: Apply for this job here or submit your application through our Careers page at https://www.lawdepot.ca/career. We thank all applicants; however, only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

The platform delivers integrated multi-device trading across desktop, web, and mobile, with access to thousands of third-party trading apps and add-ons. Breakout is a crypto prop trading program that gives skilled traders access to capital, with up to 90% of profits going to the trader. Since launching, xStocks have surpassed $25 billion in total transaction volume across blockchain ecosystems. CF Benchmarks is the leading regulated cryptocurrency index provider, authorized as a registered benchmark administrator under the UK Benchmarks Regulation. jobs.description: About the Role As a Growth Product Manager, HTS Media, you will own the roadmap for growing advertiser demand across brands: more qualified pipeline, faster campaign launches and higher advertiser spend within Hopper's ecosystem, working closely with engineering leadership, the sales team, Ad Operations and Account Management. This is a builder role: you will start by owning the roadmap for sales pipeline and sales efficiency, using AI-assisted systems to create demand and make every seller faster, then grow into owning the platform roadmap, including the campaign buying interfaces, in partnership with engineering leadership. In your first year, you'll be judged on the pipeline your systems create, how much faster campaigns go from signed to live, and growth in spend per advertiser. What would your day-to-day look like - Own the roadmap for sales pipeline and sales efficiency, with goals and success metrics tied to a revenue target - Build AI-powered systems that generate demand, from account research and signal-based targeting to personalized outreach and follow-up, and measure the pipeline and meetings they produce - Grow into owning the platform roadmap for the campaign buying interfaces with engineering leadership: write the specs and decide what gets built, and in what order - Work with Ad Operations to remove friction between a signed campaign and a live one - Put insights into the buying interface, such as forecasts, benchmarks and media plan recommendations - Use SQL on booking, search and campaign data to size opportunities, find advertiser results and decide what to build next - Run demand experiments across channels such as LinkedIn, email and events, and track results in internal dashboards - Support HTS Media positioning and reusable sales materials (deck templates, one-pagers and case studies), and the HTS Media website and offers site An ideal candidate has - 4+ years of experience in product management or growth at a technology company, ideally in B2B SaaS, marketplaces or ad tech; experience in online advertising or travel is a plus - A track record of owning a roadmap and shipping product with engineering that moved a measurable growth metric, such as pipeline, conversion, time to launch or spend per account - Hands-on experience building AI-assisted or automated workflows that a real sales team used, with tools such as Clay, n8n, Zapier or Make, and LLM APIs (equivalents are fine), and the ability to describe what you built and what it produced - Strong SQL on a cloud data warehouse such as BigQuery, and comfort turning booking, search and ad-serving data into decisions, forecasts and in-product insights - Excellent writing and specification skills, and the ability to work with engineering leadership and communicate clearly with advertisers and internal teams - Self-driven and organized, and comfortable building without a playbook in a fast-growing business Perks and benefits of working with us - Well-funded and proven startup with large ambitions, competitive salary and upsides of pre-IPO equity packages - Hopper covers 100% of the premiums for group insurance plan - Hopper offers life, short term and long term disability coverage - HSA that covers eligible medical and dental expenses - All employees and dependents have access to Dialogue’s telemedicine services, anytime, anywhere - All employees have access to an RRSP plan with automatic pre-tax withdrawals per pay - Please ask us about our very generous parental leave, much above industry standards! - Unlimited PTO - Carrot Cash travel stipend - Access to co-working space on demand through FlexDesk AND Work-from-home stipend - Entrepreneurial culture where pushing limits and taking risks is everyday business - Open communication with management and company leadership - Small, dynamic teams = massive impact About Hopper At Hopper, we're building the leading travel technology platform in the world, and we're doing it by solving real problems for real travelers globally. Our Hopper consumer booking platforms and HTS (Hopper Technology Solutions), our B2B business, work together to give travelers something the industry has never reliably offered: transparency, flexibility, and real savings on every trip. We combine massive amounts of data and AI with proprietary fintech products to make that happen, not just another booking engine, but a fundamentally better way to plan and experience travel for our customers and our partners. We are proof that better-for-the-customer and better-for-the-business can be one in the same And we're continuing to grow fast! The Hopper app has been downloaded over 120 million times, with 70% of our users being Gen Z and Millennials, next-generation travelers. Today, our biggest opportunity is powering travel fintech, commerce, and loyalty for some of the biggest brands in the industry. Our first HTS partnership with Capital One helped launch a dedicated travel portal for a major financial brand's cardholders, and we've since expanded across some of the biggest names in travel and banking, including Air Canada, Uber, Royal Bank of Canada (RBC), and Nubank, powering everything from a single fintech integration to a full end-to-end travel loyalty portal. That's our trajectory: we started as a small, disruptive app within the travel space, and now we're the engine under the hood powering how Travel Tech works. What that looks like in practice: - Billions of dollars in travel and travel fintech move through Hopper and HTS every year - Our fintech products, including Cancel for Any Reason and Disruption Assistance for Any Reason, post exceptionally strong customer satisfaction because the terms are clear and resolutions are instant, no questions asked - Nearly 30% of app customers add a fintech product to their booking, and those customers are 1.6x more likely to book with us again - HTS now drives more than 90% of the business, proof of how fast B2B has scaled - Through HTS, any travel provider (airlines, hotels, banks, travel agencies) can plug the company’s fintech, commerce and AI solutions into their own channels, whether that's a single integration or a full end-to-end travel portal Come take off with us! #LI-Remote At Hopper, we leverage AI-driven tools to assist our team in efficiently reviewing applications. These tools help us assess qualifications fairly and objectively. By submitting your application, you acknowledge the use of these automated screening technologies.

Consumer Growth builds mobile and web experiences that help people become Kraken customers, fund their accounts, invest, earn, access new products, build wealth and stay lifelong clients. Product, engineering, design, data, and lifecycle marketing build together. THE OPPORTUNITY - Choose the right bets. Identify the client segments and problems worth solving. Own the roadmap and allocate effort against expected client value, commercial impact, and engineering cost. Set the baseline, target, and threshold for scaling; stop weak bets. - Build NTU retention. Help newly transacting users build on their first transaction, discover further value, and form repeat investing and financial habits through their first weeks and months. Find where they stall and improve the steps that lead to lasting use. - Retain and bring back established clients. Keep active clients engaged, address signs of lapsing, and reactivate clients who have stopped. Understand how needs change with tenure, holdings, and financial goals, then deepen the client’s relationship with Kraken. - Make the next financial move useful. Test ways to support client intent: recurring deposits and buys, useful portfolio context, timely opportunities, or relevant Earn products. Choose from the evidence. Successful automated investing and Earn can create lasting value without frequent manual activity. Make rewards, access, and risks clear. - Prove the commercial impact. Track retention by cohort and segment, linking behavior to retained balances, net inflows, product adoption, and revenue. Measure active engagement through useful actions, such as reviewing a portfolio or investing, and track successful automated habits separately. Distinguish inflows from asset-price gains, establish incremental impact, account for incentives and costs, and check that gains last after promotions end. - Connect product and lifecycle. Partner with lifecycle marketing on push, email, web, and app journeys, from a relevant message to a useful financial action. Adapt to local payment habits and market requirements. - Build and ship with the team. Turn the chosen problem into prototypes, requirements, and experiments with engineering, design, and data. Bring risk, compliance, and legal partners into design decisions. Balance client impact, reliability, maintainability, and delivery speed; scale what works. WHAT YOU BRING - Evidence that you’ve personally led consumer product changes that beat retention or expansion targets. Be ready to explain the baseline, target, result, timeframe, and your contribution, including the impact on revenue, assets, or retained balances. - A clear account of what changed underneath the result: component behaviors or funnel rates such as repeat deposits, return-to-transaction conversion, successful recurring investments, or reactivation. Show how you established incremental impact and whether it lasted. - Strong client and product judgment. You can choose a segment and problem worth pursuing, understand why clients return, hold, withdraw, or disengage, and turn that insight into a useful experience. - Hands-on analytical depth. You query and validate your own data, diagnose cohorts and funnels, size opportunities, and design experiments that can detect a commercially meaningful effect. - Commercial discipline. You can explain how market conditions, incentives, costs, and client trust affected your results, and use that evidence to decide whether an improvement is worth scaling. - Senior ownership from decision through delivery. You’ve owned a roadmap, made product and technical trade-offs, allocated effort, stopped weak bets, and worked effectively with engineering, design, data, lifecycle marketing, and risk/compliance partners. NICE TO HAVES - Experience with consumer investing, wealth, savings, fintech, or crypto products. Freemium gaming is nice-to-have as well. - Experience building recurring investment, deposit, Earn, portfolio, or goal-based experiences. - Experience adapting client journeys across markets and local financial behaviors. jobs.description: ABOUT CAMBIO Cambio is an AI platform that helps commercial real estate owners plan, prioritize and fund the capital projects that make their buildings more efficient and valuable. Our customers manage large portfolios of buildings, and we turn messy building, utility and equipment data into clear decisions about retrofits, CapEx and sustainability reporting. We're a small, fast-moving team where design sits at the center of product. Our designers shape AI agents, data-heavy workflows and the system that holds them together, working side by side with product, engineering, building science and go-to-market. THE ROLE We're hiring a Product Designer with 4+ years of experience to own major parts of the Cambio product end to end, from framing the problem to shipping it with engineering. You'll design AI agents and data-rich workflows for a complex, high-stakes industry, and you'll help grow the design system that keeps it all coherent. This is a role for a big thinker more than a pixel polisher. We value the judgment to frame the right problem, make the call, and bring the team with you. Reports to: Design Lead WHAT YOU'LL DO - Own product areas end to end. Take core workflows from a rough idea to launch: framing, research, flows, prototypes, specs and QA with engineering. - Define how people and AI work together. Design the interaction patterns for our agents: how they show reasoning, confidence and sources, and where people review, steer or override what the AI does. - Prototype with real behavior. Use design tools to build working prototypes that test real use cases, not just static mocks. - Make complex data usable. Turn building, energy and capital-planning data into clear views and decisions for asset managers, sustainability leads and engineers. - Work in tight loops with product and engineering. No throwing mocks over the wall: you'll shape scope, trade-offs, prompts and data models alongside PMs and engineers. - Navigate without a polished PRD. Find the real problem, propose a direction, test it quickly, and iterate in front of users rather than polishing in private. - Stay close to customers. Run interviews, usability tests and lightweight experiments, and use analytics to learn what's working. - Grow the design system. Define the primitives, patterns and tokens that keep the product coherent, and make them usable by both designers and AI tools. - Wear multiple hats. Pitch in on marketing, sales and brand work when the team needs it, from demo flows to website pages to pitch materials. WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR - 4+ years of product design experience, with a portfolio of end-to-end work on shipped products. - Experience designing B2B SaaS or enterprise software for a complex domain such as healthcare, fintech, legal or another specialized industry. - AI tools support the craft you've already developed: you're fluent in Figma but are able to leverage AI tools to support your workflow (e.g. Claude, Lovable, etc.). - You're at home with ambiguity and have a bias for action: you find direction without a detailed PRD and decide with incomplete information. - Hands-on UX research experience, such as customer interviews, usability testing and A/B testing. - You're a team player with no ego but real opinions: you give direct, critical feedback and take it well. - You can tell the story behind your work and bring product, engineering and leadership along without formal authority. - Systems thinking: you design flows and patterns that hold up across the product, not just single screens. BONUS POINTS - Experience in real estate, climate tech, energy, sustainability, or finance. - You've designed and shipped an AI product, and you have a point of view on what makes AI experiences useful and trustworthy. - You've built or scaled a design system from an early stage. WHY JOIN US - Real impact. Buildings account for a large share of global emissions, and your work helps owners decide what to fix and fund. - Design with a seat at the table. Design shapes product strategy here, not just screens. - AI-native workflow. You'll work with the newest design and prototyping tools and help define how a modern design team works. - A small, senior team. You'll learn fast, ship often and see your work in customers' hands. LOGISTICS - Location: San Francisco, New York City, or Waterloo-Kitchener. Hybrid, 2-3 days in office. - Work authorization: Authorization to work in the United States or Canada. WHAT WE OFFER - Competitive compensation and startup equity - Flexible time off - $1,300 annual learning budget

jobs.description: This posting reflects a current, actively recruited opening at Float. All applications are being reviewed on a rolling basis. ABOUT FLOAT Float is on a mission to simplify finance for Canadian businesses, empowering them to eliminate complexity and unlock new opportunities. Through our innovative platform, Float enables businesses to streamline financial operations and optimize cash flow, so they can focus on what matters most: growth. As one of Canada’s fastest growing companies https://www.theglobeandmail.com/business/rob-magazine/top-growing-companies/article-ranking-canadas-top-growing-companies-of-2024/ and top-rated startups in 2025 https://www.linkedin.com/posts/floatfinancial_were-proud-to-share-that-float-has-been-activity-7387093684720300032-2DDz/, 2024 https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/linkedin-top-startups-2024-15-canadian-companies-rise-linkedin-news-llihe/ and 2023 https://lnkd.in/TSU23CA, Float is customer-obsessed, passionate and entrepreneurial, with a team that includes leaders from Uber, Stripe, Shopify, Top Hat, Ada, Doordash, Snowflake, and Wealthsimple. At Float, everyone is an owner, bringing their unique perspective to our team and product. Your voice is important, and we take having a culture based on feedback seriously. We openly share our thoughts and differing opinions so we can continue to improve. We do our best to keep our decision-making decentralized so that all team members feel ownership in our success. OUR PRODUCT Float is Canada’s intelligent financial operating system, combining modern financial services and software to help businesses spend, save, and grow. Trusted by more than 10,000 Canadian companies, Float provides high-limit corporate cards, automated expense management, next-day bill payments, high-yield accounts, and industry-leading support, all built in Canada, for Canada. Float recently announced our $85 million Series C https://floatfinancial.com/press/float-financial-raises-cad-85-million-series-c, and is backed by world-class investors, including Inovia Capital, Growth Equity at Goldman Sachs Alternatives, OMERS Ventures, and Silicon Valley Bank. Our team is a collection of ambitious, collaborative and mission-driven people from all walks of life but with one goal: helping Canadian companies not just survive but thrive. And we’re looking for bold innovators to help shape the future of business finance in Canada. AI USE IN OUR HIRING PROCESS We use technology, including artificial intelligence (AI), to support parts of our hiring process. This may include AI-assisted scheduling and candidate communications, and AI-generated interview notes, guides or summaries to help our team focus on the conversation. All hiring decisions are made by our hiring team. ABOUT THE ROLE We're hiring a Senior Product Manager to own the rails that move money into, out of and across Float: financial ledgering, financial accounts, payment rails (EFT, wires, ACH, cross-border and FX) and card infrastructure. Reporting to the GM, Banking, you'll work across three engineering squads to build and maintain the infrastructure behind our corporate cards, payments, FX and banking products. You'll think about the whole life of a payment — how it starts, how its status is communicated, what happens when it fails or is returned, and how customers and our teams resolve exceptions. You'll work with a designer, eight engineers and a product operations specialist focused on analytics and go-to-market planning. WHAT YOU'LL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR - Own the Financial Infrastructure roadmap end to end: sizing, sequencing, delivery, launch and iteration. - Make payment health measurable and keep improving it — success rate, processing speed, failure recovery and reconciliation. - Evaluate and manage infrastructure partners with our Product Partnerships team, including partner changes and new rail launches. - Manage dependencies with banks, networks and processors that move on their own timelines. Escalate risks early, with options attached. - Partner closely with Engineering on APIs, data models, ledger interactions, controls and observability. - Make trade-off calls across customer experience, speed, reliability, risk, compliance, operational complexity and commercial impact. - Coordinate across our card, payments and banking products so infrastructure work supports the whole business. - Learn how finance leaders run payroll funding, tax remittance and multi-currency treasury, and work with Design to build accounts, treasury and FX into those workflows. - Work with Risk, Compliance, Operations, Finance and GTM from the start, not as approval steps at the end. - Keep leadership and partner teams clearly informed across many projects at once. - Use AI tools to speed up discovery, analysis, documentation and decision-making. ABOUT YOU HERE'S WHAT SETS YOU UP FOR SUCCESS AT FLOAT: - You Put Customers First, Always. You care deeply about delivering meaningful value. Whether you're building internal systems or customer-facing features, you're always thinking about how to make life better for our users. - You Act Like an Owner. You take responsibility for outcomes, step up to challenges, and seek solutions proactively—doing what's best for the business, not just your role. - You Think Big and Move Fast. You're energized by building from 0 to 1. You're not afraid to challenge the status quo, experiment quickly, and learn as you go. - You Constantly Learn and Grow. You're hungry to improve your craft and open to feedback. You bring a growth mindset to everything you do. - You Raise the Bar. You care about doing things well and efficiently. You balance speed with rigor and always look for ways to improve how we work. - You Win as a Team. You're a generous collaborator who values communication, context, and shared wins. You lift others up and help make the team stronger. WHAT YOU'LL BRING - 5+ years in product management, with hands-on experience building and maintaining financial services infrastructure at a startup or scale-up. - Direct ownership of financial ledgering, money movement or payments products. - Experience leading a major infrastructure change — such as moving volume to a new bank partner or replacing a core system — while keeping customers and compliance whole. - Strong project management across external partners with their own timelines. - Clear, proactive written communication; people know where things stand before they ask. - Comfort with engineering concepts such as APIs, data models, ledgers and observability. - Practical examples of using AI in your product work. - Nice to have: - Canadian or US payments experience, including EFT/ACH, Interac e-Transfer, bill payments and wires. - Experience working directly with sponsor banks, payment processors and payment networks. - Experience building business banking, treasury management, accounts payable or accounts receivable products. THIS MAY NOT BE THE ROLE FOR YOU IF - You prefer executing a roadmap someone else has already sequenced. - You treat Risk, Compliance or Operations as downstream approvers rather than product partners. - You focus on the happy path and leave failures, returns, reconciliation or operational tooling for someone else. - You'd rather run one big launch than keep many improvements moving at once. - You struggle to connect product decisions to measurable customer and business outcomes. - You're resistant to AI-enabled ways of working. WHY YOU SHOULD JOIN - Be part of an award winning company: we're one of Canada’s Top Growing Companies 2026 according to Report on Business, and Deloitte’s Technology Fast50 2026 - Make a real impact in a high-autonomy, high-growth role - Collaborate with an ambitious and supportive team - Competitive compensation, equity options, and benefits - Hybrid work model – we are based in Toronto with in-office days for connection and collaboration - Enjoy catered team lunches every Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday - Bring your pup to our dog-frien

jobs.description: Waabi, founded by AI visionary Raquel Urtasun, is the leader in Physical AI. With a world-class team, we're unlocking the next era of autonomous transportation with technology that's powering commercial autonomous trucks and robotaxis. Waabi is backed by and partners with world leaders in AI, automotive, logistics, and deep tech. With offices in Toronto, San Francisco, Dallas, and Pittsburgh, Waabi is growing quickly and looking for diverse, innovative and collaborative candidates who want to impact the world in a positive way. To learn more visit: www.waabi.ai Robots need to see the world they live in to make informed decisions. The Onboard Sensors Team brings that sight to our robot autonomous vehicles, and cameras are the richest and most demanding sensors on the vehicles. We are looking for an engineer who knows cameras end to end: from the image sensor and serializer, over the GMSL link, through the driver and ISP, to frames arriving on time in our autonomy stack. You will own the camera side of our sensor platform, work with live vehicles every day, and help shape how our camera systems scale from today's fleet to production. Our team is small and hands-on, so you will also set the bar for camera knowledge and mentor engineers who are newer to the domain. You will… Own camera integration on the Waabi Driver: bring-up, configuration, drivers and the path from the image sensor to GMSL link to the autonomy stack. Debug camera issues on real vehicles operating in the field daily — dropped or corrupted frames, link errors, flicker, exposure problems — and trace them to the cable, serializer, deserializer, driver or application. Make camera data trustworthy in time: hardware triggering, frame timestamping and synchronization with the rest of the sensor suite. Tune and validate image quality with our perception and science partners: ISP settings, exposure and HDR control, and performance in hard lighting such as night, glare and tunnels. Evaluate new cameras and vendors, and integrate them into existing and future onboard platforms. Build the diagnostics and observability that tell us which component dropped a frame, and why. Work closely with operations and hardware teams to understand live system behavior and mature our camera platform toward production. Qualifications: 6+ years of industry experience, including hands-on work integrating cameras into fielded systems (automotive, AV, robotics, drones or similar). Deep understanding of the camera hardware pipeline: image sensors, SerDes links (ADI/Maxim GMSL or TI FPD-Link), triggering, and how pixels get from the sensor over the wire into memory. Hands-on SerDes experience: configuring and debugging ADI/Maxim GMSL2/GMSL3 or TI FPD-Link III/IV serializers and deserializers (e.g. MAX9295/MAX9296/MAX96712, DS90UB953/DS90UB960), including link training, I2C passthrough and link-error diagnostics. Experience with Linux camera stacks below the application level: V4L2, kernel drivers, device tree, DMA and buffer management. Proficiency in Rust or C/C++ in real-time, resource-constrained environments (we use Rust). A track record of independently debugging hard camera problems on real hardware, not only in simulation or offline data. Collaborating with large teams that span engineering, hardware and operations. Bonus: Experience with NVIDIA Jetson/DRIVE camera frameworks or similar automotive SoCs. ISP and image-quality tuning: exposure, HDR, white balance, color. Time synchronization in multi-sensor systems (PTP, hardware triggers, frame timestamping). Electronics experience: reading schematics, signal integrity, and using an oscilloscope or protocol analyzer. Experience evaluating camera vendors or working closely with camera suppliers. Familiarity with other sensor modalities (lidar, radar, GNSS/IMU). Passionate about self-driving technology and about efficient, readable, testable code.

And with JunieAI, our purpose-built AI platform, we’re reimagining how private markets operate, embedding intelligence across every workflow. If you’re energized by high standards, rapid growth, and the opportunity to help define a category at a pivotal moment, come join us! Juniper Square offers employees a variety of ways to work, ranging from a fully remote experience to working full-time in one of our physical offices. We invest heavily in digital-first https://blog.junipersquare.com/juniper-square-ponders-future-of-office-with-digital-first-hybrid-workplace-strategy/ operations, allowing our teams to collaborate effectively across 27 U.S. states, 2 Canadian Provinces, India, Luxembourg, and England. We also have physical offices in San Francisco, New York City, Mumbai and Bangalore for employees who prefer to work in an office some or all of the time. ABOUT YOUR ROLE Juniper Square is the system of record for private-capital funds: we move LP capital, hold investor data our customers are legally responsible for, and enforce the boundaries between one fund’s information and another’s. As a Staff Security Operations Engineer, you will be the senior hands-on engineer who builds our Tier 2 detection and response capability and stands up our data loss prevention program. You will report to the Head of Security and work day to day with the Staff Security Engineer who owns our security platform, the Application Security team, GRC, and the CISO. Our stack is modern and already deployed: Google SecOps for SIEM, CrowdStrike for endpoint, Cloudflare Zero Trust, Upwind for cloud posture and runtime, FireCompass for external attack surface, and a managed detection and response provider we are transitioning away from. The job is to make detection and response something we own, measure, and can prove to auditors and customers. WHAT YOU’LL DO - Own Tier 2 detection engineering in Google SecOps: author, test, and tune detection rules and correlation logic, drive down false positives, and maintain a detection catalog mapped to MITRE ATT&CK with documented coverage and gaps. - Build the playbooks, runbooks, and escalation criteria that a Tier 1 analyst desk will operate against, and act as the Tier 2 escalation point for triage decisions and investigations until that desk is staffed. - Lead the technical transition from managed detection and response to in-house operations: inventory what the provider detects today, rebuild or replace those detections in Google SecOps, define cut-over criteria, and validate coverage before each hand-off. - Design, roll out, and maintain the data loss prevention program across Google Workspace, endpoints (CrowdStrike), SaaS applications, cloud storage, and data flowing into AI tools: classify sensitive data (investor PII, fund financials, payment instructions, secrets), write policies, tune them against real business workflows, and build the response process for DLP events. - Automate the operations work: Python and API-driven enrichment, alert triage and response automation, detections-as-code with version control and testing, and integrations between Google SecOps, CrowdStrike, Cloudflare, Upwind, Okta or our identity provider, and Jira. - Run and improve the threat hunting program: hypothesis-driven hunts across endpoint, identity, cloud, and SaaS telemetry that convert into durable detections. - Lead investigations as a senior responder during security incidents, including endpoint and cloud forensics, timeline reconstruction, containment actions, and post-incident write-ups that produce new detections and control changes. - Own telemetry quality: onboard and normalize new log sources, close visibility gaps (for example S3-to-ephemeral-workload activity and SaaS admin events), and define what logs the business must retain for detection and audit. - Harden enterprise controls with IT: enforce least-privilege and zero-trust policies in Cloudflare and identity, review egress and proxy configurations, and turn configuration baselines into monitored controls rather than documents. - Produce evidence and metrics: mean time to detect and respond, detection coverage, false-positive rate, DLP event trends, and control test results for SOC 2 and ISO 27001, 27017, 27018, and 42001 audits and customer security reviews. - Contribute to red and purple team exercises and tabletop scenarios, and use the results to prioritize detection and hardening work. - Mentor Tier 1 analysts and less experienced engineers as the team grows, and set the engineering standards for how detections, playbooks, and automation are written and reviewed. - Participate in an on-call rotation for security escalations. QUALIFICATIONS - 8+ years in information security with at least 4 years in detection engineering, security operations, or incident response roles, including time as the senior or lead engineer on a team. - Hands-on detection engineering in a modern SIEM (Google SecOps / Chronicle strongly preferred; Splunk, Sentinel, or Elastic acceptable), including writing and tuning rules, building correlation logic, and measuring detection quality. - Experience designing and rolling out DLP in a SaaS-heavy, distributed company (Google Workspace, endpoint, and CASB or SaaS DLP tooling), including data classification and policy tuning against real workflows. - Strong EDR depth (CrowdStrike or equivalent) and forensic investigation skills on macOS, Windows, and Linux; comfortable leading an investigation end to end. - Practical programming and automation ability in Python and REST APIs; experience with detections-as-code, CI for security content, or SOAR-style automation. - Working knowledge of cloud security telemetry and identity threats: AWS CloudTrail and GuardDuty, Kubernetes audit logs, identity provider logs, and common attack paths across them. - Familiarity with MITRE ATT&CK, NIST SP 800-61, and the evidence expectations of SOC 2 and ISO 27001 audits. - Experience using AI to accelerate triage, detection development, or investigation, with clear judgment about where it should and should not be trusted. - Ability to explain technical risk to non-security partners in IT, Engineering, Legal, and the business, and to work through disagreements about controls without escalating every one. - Bachelor’s degree in a technical field or equivalent experience. At Juniper Square, we believe building a diverse workforce and an inclusive culture makes us a better company. If you think this job sounds like a fit, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet all the qualifications. jobs.description: Hi, Future Homie! At Homebase, you’ll join a team that’s bold, fast-moving, and obsessed with helping small businesses thrive. We build with empathy, act with urgency, and take big swings that drive real-world impact. Here, every Homie shows up to raise the bar, support one another, and celebrate wins as a team. We’re not just building an app—we’re building unstoppable teams. So what do you say, are you in? 📍Your Impact Starts Here We’re looking for a Full Stack Senior Software Engineer 2 who’s passionate about building AI-powered, high-velocity systems that transform how our Growth, Sales, and Product teams operate. You’ll own greenfield development across GTM tooling, experimentation infrastructure, and intelligent automation that scales our growth engine. This is a unique opportunity to define and implement new capabilities, build supporting tooling, and run experiments that shape the future of Homebase's AI-first platform. If you love zero-to-one execution, collaborating in-person to accelerate innovation, and building systems that meaningfully influence company growth, we want to hear from you. These are the key ways you’ll contribute and create impact in this role: - Lead the technical design and implementation of new GTM (Go-to-Market) tools and platforms that drive scale, automation, and growth. - Partner cross-functionally with Sales, Data, Analytics, and Product to translate business needs into well-scoped technical solutions. - Modernize and contribute to our experimentation infrastructure, helping teams ship faster and learn more efficiently. - Build AI- and LLM-powered capabilities (agents, workflows, embedded intelligence) that unlock new growth opportunities. - Elevate engineering quality through system design leadership, architecture reviews, and mentorship. - Drive technical discovery in ambiguous problem spaces—clarifying requirements, shaping roadmap, and providing direction when paths aren’t obvious. - Collaborate in-office on key hybrid days to align quickly, accelerate iteration, and co-create breakthrough solutions. 🚀 The Foundation for Success - These are the experiences and strengths that will set you up for success in this role: - 5+ years of software engineering experience, including 2+ in technical leadership. - Strong full-stack development skills with Rails + React (or equivalent modern stacks). - Proven ability to lead ambiguity-heavy, greenfield projects from concept → delivery. - Experience designing systems that integrate multiple data sources and support complex workflows. - Hands-on experience building with AI/LLMs (agents, embeddings, orchestrating model calls). - Strong communicator—able to align technical and non-technical teams around shared outcomes. - Track record of pragmatic architectural decisions that balance speed with long-term scalability. 🤝 The Homie Way - These principles guide everything we do—from how we work and make decisions to how we show up for each other. - 💡 Be Customer Obsessed – Solve problems with empathy and creativity. - ⚡ Move Fast, Learn Fast – Experiment, take action, and grow every day. - 🎯 Own Your Impact – Think big, focus on what matters, and make decisions you stand behind. - 🏆 Master Your Craft – Excellence fuels impact—show up, step up, and make your mark. - 🏅 Win Together – Put goals over roles, lead with trust, and connect to our mission and each other. What We Offer - 💰 Ownership & Savings: Stock options + TFSA/RRSP with 4% company match - 🏥 Health & Wellness: Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision for you and your dependents - ⏰ Paid Time Off: Flexible PTO + company holidays + designated focus periods - 🤖 AI access, for real: We invest in builders and believe that curiosity shouldn't have a paywall. That means you'll have access to paid AI tools with minimal restrictions, so you can build, experiment, and level up your craft. - 👶 Family Support: Maternity/Parental Leave EI top-up support offered (after 6 months of service) - 🌟 Work Your Way: Work From Anywhere Month + meeting-free weeks yearly - 🛡️ Protection Plans: Life insurance + short/long-term disability coverage - 🍽️ Workspace Perks: Meals provided, team offsites, and Customer Days - 💼 Our Hybrid Rhythm: We believe collaboration drives impact. That’s why Tuesdays and Wednesdays are our required in-office days—a time to move faster as a team, build deeper connections, make better decisions, and build together. What to Expect During the Interview Process - Meet the Talent Acquisition team, Mavel W. https://www.linkedin.com/in/mavel-wayman-0ab35447/ - Meet the Hiring Manager, Martin R. https://www.linkedin.com/in/martin-ryalen-67482a53/ - Participate in Technical Interviews - Meet Stakeholders - Background Check + Offer Stage - Welcome to the team, Homie 🎉 💜 Belonging at Homebase - We're committed to fostering a welcoming space where every Homie can be their full self. Experience comes in many forms—so if you're excited about this role, even if you don’t meet 100% of the qualifications, we encourage you to apply! 👋 Hey, We’re Homebase Homebase is the everything app for hourly teams—built to simplify the day-to-day and superpower local businesses. With tools for scheduling, time clocks, payroll, communication, HR, and more, we help teams stay connected and in control. Today, over 150,000 small (but mighty) businesses rely on us to make work radically easier. Together, we’ve tracked over a billion hours for 2M+ workers—and we’re just getting started. At Homebase, we celebrate diversity and are proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We welcome all candidates and do not discriminate based on any legally protected status. If you need accommodations during the hiring process, please let us know—we’re committed to ensuring fair and equitable access for all.

jobs.description: Artificial Intelligence. Actual Impact. At Docebo, we’re using AI to change how people learn at work—and we mean actually change it. We’re an AI-powered learning platform that helps organizations create, deliver, and manage training all in one place. But our real mission goes deeper: we help teams move faster, work smarter, and focus on the work that truly matters. Our platform is built with intelligent, time-saving tools that personalize learning, eliminate busywork, and turn training from a checkbox into a superpower. The result? Better experiences for learners and real results for businesses. We’re shaping the future of learning with a team that isn’t afraid to challenge the status quo. If you're excited by the idea of using AI to make work-life better for real people–you’ll feel right at home here. And it’s not just what we build, it’s how we show up. At Docebo, our values aren’t just posters on the wall—they guide how we work every day. We call it the Docebo Heart: trust by default, assume positive intent, and create space for different perspectives to thrive. Want to get a better feel for what it's like to work at Docebo? Check out our Life https://www.linkedin.com/company/docebo/life/0e53ece6-0cc2-41ca-a183-84de0a8c245d/?viewAsMember=true page on our LinkedIn to get a glimpse into our culture, people, and the experiences that make Docebo a great place to grow your career. So… what are you waiting for? Join 900+ Docebians around the world and help us reinvent the way people learn, because learning never stops. 🚀 THE ADVENTURE AHEAD As our Cybersecurity Compliance Analyst, you will be the front-line champion and strategist safeguarding Docebo's security posture and driving customer trust. You will bridge the gap between technical rigor and client confidence, translating complex compliance frameworks (like NIS2, NIST, GDPR, ISO, SOC, and FedRAMP) into competitive advantages. In this role, your work directly accelerates deal cycles, empowers our sales and legal teams, and ensures our global SaaS ecosystem remains fortress-secure. ⚡ THE DAY-TO-DAY - Champion Customer Trust: Respond to prospect and customer security requests, review RFIs/RFQs, and deliver flawless responses regarding Docebo's compliance and security posture. - Drive Compliance & CAPs: Tackle customer security questionnaires head-on and collaborate internally to establish Corrective Action Plans (CAPs) for outstanding requirements. - Power Legal Alignment: Partner with the Docebo legal team to review Customer Agreements, Terms & Conditions, and Data Processing Addendums, seamlessly mapping client requirements to standard processes. - Spearhead Audit Readiness: Lead and support annual customer audits while partnering with the GRC team during SOC2, ISO (27001, 9001, 42001), and NIS2 assessments. - Automate for Efficiency: Leverage AI tools and basic programming capabilities to automate internal processes and optimize compliance workflows. - Publish & Curate Insights: Organize internal compliance documentation and publish up-to-date materials directly to Docebo’s "trust pages" using platforms like Vanta. - Evaluate Vendor Risk: Support third-party vendor risk assessments, monitor security controls, and maintain management reporting dashboards to mitigate external supplier risks. 🦸 YOUR SUPERPOWERS - Proven SaaS Expertise: 4+ years of hands-on experience supporting security activities, audits, and compliance in SaaS environments, backed by a Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or a related field. - Cloud & Privacy Mastery: Solid working knowledge of cloud environments (AWS, Azure, GCloud) alongside data privacy regulations like GDPR, CCPA, and PIPEDA. - Framework Fluent: Deep familiarity with security and compliance standards including ISO/IEC (27001, 27017, 27018, 27701, 9001, 42001), SOC 2, PCI, NIS2, and CFR21 Part 11. - Technical Savvy & Automation Mindset: Basic coding skills and hands-on experience with modern security governance platforms like Vanta and 1UP. - Articulate Communicator: Exceptional written and verbal English communication skills, with a knack for translating complex technical concepts into clear customer answers. - Problem-Solver Extraordinaire: Proactive, adaptable, and deeply passionate about the intersection of technology, business, and enterprise learning. 🌟 BONUS POINTS - Certified Specialist: Holding certifications such as CISA, CIPP (or CIPT), or CompTIA Security+. - FedRAMP Familiarity: Basic understanding and exposure to the FedRAMP framework. - Advanced Academic Background: Specialized degree focus in Information Security or Auditing. 🧭 OUR INTERVIEW PROCESS Step 1: We’ll kick things off with a 30-minute video call with a member of our Talent team. We’ll get to know you, share more about the role and team, and make sure we’re aligned. Step 2: A 60-minute video call with the hiring manager, where they’ll dig deeper into your experience, approach, and what excites you most about this opportunity. Step 3: A 45-minute practical case study/technical discussion with key members of the Compliance & GRC team. Step 4: A final 30-minute chat with our Security Leadership team to discuss long-term vision, growth, and team alignment. OUR HYBRID WORK PHILOSOPHY 🤝 Great work can happen anywhere but coming together helps us go further. Our team spends three days a week in the office (Tuesday-Thursday) to collaborate, solve problems, and learn from each other. With flexibility the rest of the week, it’s a balance designed to help everyone do their best work and keep growing. OUR TOTAL REWARDS PHILOSOPHY 🎉 Our Total Rewards Philosophy centers around three core areas to reward and care for our People: - Rewarding Impact: We lead with competitive pay to reward the impact, skills and traits that fuel our success. - Fostering Holistic Wellbeing: We care deeply about and invest in the whole person with programs that support our people’s physical, mental, and financial well-being. - Empowering Our Talent Culture: We build a culture of trust and empowerment by designing our rewards and benefits with transparency, equity, and flexibility, enabling our people to do their best work and stay for the long haul. OUR PROMISE TO YOU 😍 - Financial Wellness: Own a piece of Docebo through our Employee Share Purchase Plan (ESPP) at a 15% discount, plus a competitive compensation package. - Your Well-Being, Covered: You’ll get access to health benefits, so you can get the care you need when you need it. - Rest, Relax, Repeat: Rest and recharge with paid vacation days, two company-wide Docebo Days, floating holidays for cultural celebrations, and your birthday off! - Family First: We provide coverage offering you time with your little one(s) so you can soak up all those precious moments. Fun fact: we had 30 Docebian babies join the family in 2025! - Connections That Count: Connect with global communities through our Employee Resource Groups (including PRIDE, DWA, BIDOC, and Green Ambassadors) and company-wide events that keep the fun rolling all year long. ABOUT DOCEBO 💙 At Docebo, we create seamless, AI-powered learning experiences for over 3,000 customers worldwide. We have successfully achieved two IPOs (TSX: DCBO & NASDAQ: DCBO https://www.docebo.inc/home/default.aspx), been recognized as a top SaaS e-learning solution, and are growing exponentially in the process. We're a global company, with office across North America, EMEA, APAC, and beyond. Our team is guided by five core values—Grow Together Win Together, Build with Our Customer, Clear is Kind, Own Outcomes, Progress Over Perfection—that shape everything we do. jobs.position: Senior Backend Engineer, Identity and Access Management
jobs.description: At ClickUp, we're building the future of work: the first truly converged AI workspace unifying tasks, docs, chat, calendar, and enterprise search, all supercharged by context-driven AI. We are an AI-native company. Every team member is expected to leverage AI daily, and we evaluate AI fluency as part of our hiring process. Join us and help redefine what's possible. 🚀 Come join the Identity & Access Management Platform team (IAM Platform) and build the layer that decides who can see and do what across all of ClickUp. This team owns the authorization engine, the permission and role model, authentication (SSO, MFA, SCIM, OAuth), sharing primitives, audit logs, and the core hierarchy data model and APIs that every other part of ClickUp is built on. It is backend-heavy, high-blast-radius work: a subtle mistake here is a security incident, not a bug report. We're looking for a Senior Backend Engineer to help design and deliver an enterprise-grade access management platform. Right now that means building fine-grained, location-scoped permission profiles and inherited governance ceilings — a model where a workspace admin can delegate ownership of a Space to a local owner without letting them widen access, invite the wrong people, or delete the container, and where the effective answer is always the intersection of what a principal is granted and what every ancestor policy allows. You'll work on inheritance and resolution semantics across the Workspace → Space → Folder → List → Task tree, on the evaluation path that has to stay correct and fast on every request, and on migrating a live permission model used by millions of users without granting or revoking a single thing by accident. If you want access control to be the problem you work on rather than a checkbox on someone else's roadmap, this is the team. RESPONSIBILITIES - Design and build core services in ClickUp's authorization platform: the permission and role model, capability evaluation, sharing and access-control primitives, and the inheritance semantics that resolve effective access across the Workspace → Space → Folder → List → Task hierarchy. - Extend the authorization engine to support configuration-driven enterprise access models — reusable permission profiles, atomic capability catalogs, delegated grant scopes, and inherited policy ceilings where restriction always wins over grant. - Build and operate authentication and provisioning surfaces: SSO (SAML/OIDC, Okta, Entra, social IdPs), MFA/2FA, session and token lifecycle, OAuth and API token management, and SCIM provisioning and deprovisioning. - Own the correctness of the permission evaluation path end to end — a single authoritative server-side decision that the API, the UI, automations, and agents all resolve against, with no bypass paths. - Make access explainable and auditable: emit the events, reasoning, and audit trail that let an admin answer "why does this user have access here?" and "why was this share blocked?" - Design and execute safe migrations on high-blast-radius data — shadow evaluation, dual reads, backfills, and staged rollout behind feature flags, with a verifiable guarantee that effective access does not silently change. - Hold the performance and reliability bar for services on the hot path of every request in the product, and take part in the shared IAM on-call rotation. - Partner with frontend, product, design, and infosec so the access controls we ship are precise, predictable, and usable by real enterprise admins — and represent your work credibly in enterprise security reviews. - Work AI-natively: use AI tools and agents daily in your engineering workflow, and structure your work so agents can route, roll up, and report on it. We have no status-reporting meetings — reporting is self-serve. REQUIREMENTS - 5+ years of professional backend engineering experience building production SaaS at scale. - Hands-on experience building authorization or access-control systems — permission and role models (RBAC, ReBAC, or ABAC), policy evaluation, access-control lists, or a centralized authorization service — not just consuming one. - Direct experience with hierarchical or inherited permissions: how access is granted, inherited, overridden, and revoked across a tree of resources, and how to resolve effective permissions correctly and quickly. - Strong command of a modern backend stack and of designing APIs and data models that other teams build on. We use TypeScript, Node.js, and NestJS with PostgreSQL, Redis, and Kafka; deep expertise in a comparable stack transfers well. - Practical knowledge of authentication and identity standards: OAuth 2.0, OIDC, SAML, JWTs, session and token lifecycle, MFA, and SCIM provisioning. - Experience operating in a multi-tenant environment where tenant isolation is a hard correctness requirement. - A demonstrated track record of shipping schema and behavior migrations on live, high-traffic systems without breaking existing customers. - A security-conscious mindset: the server is the source of truth, deny-by-default is the starting position, and you reason about blast radius, privilege escalation, and failure modes by default. - Strong debugging and systems-reasoning skills, and the judgment to know when a problem calls for a general abstraction versus a narrow, shippable fix. - Excellent written communication — we are asynchronous by default and push decisions and context into docs and ClickUp rather than meetings. - Daily fluency with AI tools in your engineering workflow. PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS - Experience with Google Zanzibar–style authorization, relationship-based access control, or an open-source engine such as SpiceDB, OpenFGA, Oso, Cerbos, or OPA. - Experience extracting an authorization or identity domain out of a monolith into dedicated services. - Experience building the admin-facing side of access control: custom role builders, permission catalogs, delegated administration, and access-explainability or "view as" tooling. - Familiarity with enterprise compliance requirements and how they shape access control — SOC 2, ISO 27001, audit logging, and separation of duties. - Experience with high-throughput caching and invalidation strategies for permission data. - Experience designing access models for non-human principals — service accounts, API integrations, or AI agents acting on a user's behalf. #LI-REMOTE Equal Opportunity Employer ClickUp is an Equal Opportunity Employer, and qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, or national origin. Visa Sponsorship Please note we are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment visa for roles outside of engineering and product at this time. Sponsorship for engineering and product roles is not guaranteed, but is instead based on the business needs for that specific role at that time. Please reach out to the recruiter with any questions. jobs.description: ABOUT THE ROLE Hi, I'm James https://www.linkedin.com/in/jamesrenaud/, and I help lead the Infrastructure & Enablement group at Jane. Platform Engineering and Developer Experience are career passions of mine, and both are areas critical to our group here. One of the many reasons I joined Jane was to help developers here spend more time helping our helpers and less time worrying about day-to-day development. Jane's product development org grew from 250 to almost 500 staff in about two and a half years. Roughly 350 of us ship software every day leveraging GitHub, Jira, AWS, and more. We've rapidly outgrown the side-of-desk administration of these platforms that are key to our software and product delivery lifecycle. Helping shape the developer experience through settings, security, governance, and implementation in these tools is what the Developer Operations team is all about. That's the job. You'd be a foundational builder as part of a new Developer Operations team, and the first dragon to wrangle is GitHub. GitHub is your platform to own end to end: help drive a more mature baseline, automate it, roll it out, and support the teams already using it. This is taking the tools we already use and making them genuinely delightful to use, so the safe path is also the easy, default path. Our concrete target is every repo at Jane is compliant with a defined operational and security baseline within twelve months. Alongside GitHub, this role continues to grow in scope and breadth taking on administration and integration of all of the key tools in our SDLC, and helping us introduce new ones to fill the gaps as we identify them. You own this with real independence, but with the support and guidance of working groups that have already done the hard thinking on what the baselines should be. Partners in Security, Delivery Engineering, Backend Foundations, Developer Acceleration, and more - already care deeply about the outcome, but you're responsible for taking that guidance and making it a reality. Agentic and AI development raise the value of getting this system humming now, rather than later. The same model continues to streamline our SDLC from end-to-end encompassing Jira, DataDog, and whatever comes next. You're helping shape how this team works before there's even a team to shape. You'd be joining a group that treats developer experience as real work with real leverage. Over 300 people will have their day-to-day lives made better because of the choices you get to make. If you like the idea of taking a sprawling, underserved platform and turning it into something people trust, I'd love to meet you. WHAT IMPACT WE'RE LOOKING FOR YOU TO MAKE - Be the accountable owner of GitHub at Jane. Multiple orgs, 900+ repos, 300+ developers. You set the operational and security baseline, you decide what good looks like, and you're the person the org can escalate to instead of guessing. - Collaborate to build the golden path so the safe path is the default path. Repo creation, branch protections and rulesets, required reviews, secret scanning, least-privilege access - configured so teams get the right setup without having to know the rules, rather than a wiki page nobody reads. These golden paths also help guide teams on discovering technologies already available to them, reducing duplication of efforts, and ultimately helping teams help the helpers faster. - Automate compliance instead of policing it. Configuration drift detection, compliance reporting, and guided enforcement through bots and dashboards, so standards hold without depending on any one engineer remembering them. Partner closely with our Platform Security teams on access controls, secret management, and alerting that actually reaches the right people. - Lead the change management, not just the change. Changing how GitHub works changes how every team ships. Expect entrenched workflows and some pushback, and expect to bring people along collaboratively rather than shipping a policy and hoping. Get us from a defined baseline to 100% of repos compliant within twelve months through a phased rollout - pilot with a few teams, then broaden - with hands-on migration support for the teams that need it. - Prove the model, then extend it. Take what works on GitHub to Jira, Datadog, JFrog and beyond, and help define how this new team operates as it grows. WHAT EXPERIENCE WE NEED - Hands-on administration of developer tooling at organizational scale. A systems administrator profile with a DevOps/DevEx slant. You've owned platforms other engineers depend on, and you're comfortable running them whether they're managed SaaS or something we host ourselves. That includes practical GitHub administration: org and enterprise settings, rulesets and branch protections, GitHub Apps and integrations, Actions, SSO/SCIM and access management, secret scanning and code security, and audit logs. If you've cleaned up a large, drifted GitHub estate before, lead with that. - Configuration as code rather than clicking through settings. Terraform, the GitHub API, and enough scripting - Bash, Python, TypeScript, or similar - to automate config, drift detection, and reporting across hundreds of repos. Comfort hosting and running tools in AWS, ideally including EKS, for the pieces we operate ourselves. - A security-first instinct. Least privilege by default, sound secret management, and a track record of partnering with security teams rather than working around them. - The autonomy and consultative skill this level asks for. You'll be the first person on a team that doesn't exist yet, working across an org that hasn't had an owner here. We need someone who defines the baseline rather than waiting to be handed one, and who's comfortable with the ambiguity that comes with that. Much of this job is influence without authority: getting hundreds of developers to adopt standards they didn't ask for, and making them feel supported rather than governed. - Fluency with AI coding tools (we lean on Claude first, Cursor second), able to direct agents through real automation, reporting, and migration work while staying responsible for correctness and blast radius, and keeping the judgment that org-wide configuration changes deserve. MORE ABOUT JANE Jane is a founder-led, high-growth SaaS company with a remote-first team working across Canada, the US, and the UK, united by our mission to help the helpers. That level of impact means every person at Jane plays an important role in how we show up for our customers. We're all responsible for being deeply connected to their needs, obsessed with improving their experience, and proud of the difference our work makes in their day-to-day lives. jobs.description: Hi 👋🏻 I’m Louis, Head of Security. We’re building out the security function at Ashby. What Ashby gives you in return is the best of both early and growth-stage environments. The agency and no-nonsense approach of a seed startup: you write product specs, make product and design decisions, and build in an almost-no-meeting culture. The product-market fit and scale of a growth-stage startup: 100,000+ weekly active users who depend on your software and eagerly await your next feature. We have notable customers like Notion, Linear, Shopify, and Snowflake. Our growth and retention metrics are best-in-class among our peers: we have tens of millions in ARR, growing >100% year over year, very low churn, and many years of runway. We’ll share more details once we meet. You’ll join our Security team, a single team with multiple specializations overseeing security across the business. I report to Abhik, our Co-Founder and VP of Engineering. We’re bubbling with ideas for how to support Talent Acquisition with software, and we recently launched Talent Management products to expand our total addressable market and become a company worth $60B+. We read every application and aim to respond to yours within 3-4 days (often sooner). ROLE OVERVIEW An employee’s access is increasingly also the access they can delegate to an AI tool. That makes identity and permissions an engineering problem with a practical question behind it: can we understand what someone or their agent can reach, and reconstruct what happened when something goes wrong? We’re looking for someone who can build the systems that answer that question. You’ll automate access management, connect the evidence needed for investigations, and improve the security workflows our team uses every day. You’ll care about how those controls feel to the people using them as well as the risks they address. ABOUT THE ROLE AND HOW WE WORK Your mission is to automate and scale internal security access management while giving us the visibility and response capability to investigate incidents. You’ll own security integrations, identity workflows, operational telemetry, and automation across the internal environment, and incident management for the Security team. You’ll work closely with IT on access management and logging, with Engineering on service and agent identities, with Infrastructure on cloud signals, and with GRC on control requirements and AI governance evidence. GRC will run routine vendor diligence; you’ll provide deeper technical review when data sensitivity, privileged access, integration scope, or service criticality warrants it. You’ll own the security logic and automation connecting these systems and be the Security team’s sole owner for incident management. You’ll lead intake, triage, coordination, escalation, and follow-through. Application Security will own product authorization and AI-feature threat modeling and contribute specialist analysis during incidents. Together, you’ll make internal access decisions and investigations coherent across human, service, and agent activity. In practice, you’ll: - Automate identity lifecycle and access changes, including joiner, mover, and leaver workflows, access reviews, expiring grants, and integrations with internal systems. - Help define prohibited combinations of role, system, action, and data, then implement access controls and monitoring proportionate to the risk. - Evaluate and extend contextual access controls that assess each request using current identity, device posture, and relevant behavioral signals. Compare how Okta and Cloudflare can support those decisions across internal systems. - Centralize useful telemetry from identity, SaaS, infrastructure, repositories, and data systems. Define and maintain detections and escalation rules with our outsourced SOC, improving them through incident learnings. - Evaluate SIEM options through a practical proof of concept, including Datadog Cloud SIEM, Microsoft Sentinel, and Splunk, then recommend an approach based on coverage, investigation quality, effort, and cost. - Build agent attribution: connect the initiating human, acting agent, credentials and permissions, trigger, and resulting actions so activity can be reconstructed. - Deliver useful alerts and permitted response actions through Slack, with access checks, confirmation where needed, and an audit trail. Use AI to help with enrichment and triage while retaining accountability for consequential decisions. - Own incident management from preparation and intake through severity assessment, containment and recovery coordination, stakeholder updates, post-incident review, and tracking follow-up actions to closure. Build the evidence capture, playbooks, and automation that make investigations faster and more reliable. To ground it with examples, you could: - Build an access workflow that grants an appropriate capability for a limited period and automatically removes it, with the reason and owner attached. - Follow an agent’s repository or infrastructure action back to the human who initiated it and show the permissions it used. - Connect identity and SaaS events to an alert that gives an investigator enough context to act, then test whether the detection works without flooding the team with routine activity. WHY YOU SHOULD AND SHOULDN’T APPLY You should apply if: - You’ve built integrations, internal tools, or automation for identity, security operations, or enterprise systems, and you can write maintainable code. - You understand authentication, authorization, least privilege, and how access and delegation work across cloud and SaaS systems. - You’ve worked with logs, detections, and incident investigations, coordinated a security incident through resolution, and know what evidence a responder needs to reconstruct an event. - You care about the experience of employees using security controls, and you can use data to stage changes and find workflows that need a better path. - You’ve applied AI or workflow automation to operational work and can explain the limits, permissions, and review points of what you built. - You collaborate well with IT, Infrastructure, engineers, and nontechnical teams, and can own a problem across those boundaries. You might not enjoy the role if: - You want to spend most of your time administering consoles. We want you to build integrations and automate recurring work. - You believe access should always be blocked or always be monitored. You’ll need to make the tradeoff explicit and implement the appropriate treatment. - You want to collect every log before deciding what to detect. We’ll start with risks and the evidence needed to investigate them. - You want AI agents to make consequential access or response decisions without traceability. Delegation has to preserve accountability. - You only want project work. Incident management, investigations, response, tuning, and maintenance are part of the job. LEVEL AND EXPERIENCE This posting is aimed at Senior engineers, and we’re also open to Staff-level candidates. We care about the systems you’ve built, the judgment you bring, and your ability to own a problem through implementation and operation. At Senior level, we expect you to independently deliver substantial security work and help other engineers use what you build. At Staff level, we expect experience setting technical direction across teams, finding recurring problems, and building approaches that others can extend. YOUR FIRST THREE MONTHS AT ASHBY Your early changes will give you a tour of our codebase, infrastructure, and best practices, increasing in scope and ambiguity as you learn how we work.
