jobs.description: [Quora is a privately held, "remote-first" company https://www.quora.com/q/quora/Remote-First-at-Quora. This position can be performed remotely from anywhere in Canada or the United States. Please visit careers.quora.com/eligible-countries http://careers.quora.com/eligible-countries for details regarding employment eligibility by country.] ABOUT QUORA: Quora’s mission is to grow the world's collective intelligence. To do so, we have two platforms: - Quora http://quora.com: a global knowledge sharing platform with millions of monthly unique visitors, bringing people together to share insights on various topics and providing a unique platform to learn and connect with others. - Poe https://poe.com/: a cloud workspace where millions of users run multiple AI agents on shared context and tools. One subscription, every frontier model, and the collaboration layer that makes them work together. Behind these products are passionate, collaborative, and high-performing global teams. We have a culture rooted in transparency, idea-sharing, and experimentation that allows us to celebrate success and grow together through meaningful work. Join us on this journey to create a positive impact and make a significant change in the world. This role will be supporting both our Quora and Poe products. ABOUT THE TEAM AND ROLE: You will be a key member of the newly created Security Engineering Team, with a mission to keep Quora safe from security problems by building robust protections around our products, infrastructure and people. Our small engineering team works on challenging problems every day. We have a culture that's rooted in constantly learning and improving, and our engineers are encouraged to think big and experiment with new ideas. WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR: - Sweat The Right Details: you thrive in understanding the details but will also know to ruthlessly prioritize the critical issues. - Right-Size The Solution: you recognize guidelines and framework do not always fit the problem and know how to adjust the solution for scalability not always at-scale. - Ownership: you are outcome focused and can deftly navigate obstacles, decompose complexities, manage your time and can communicate your vision to peers and management. AN IDEAL CANDIDATE WOULD... be a capable software engineer while also spiking in at least one of the following domain expertise: - Cloud Infrastructure Security: You have hands-on experience securing large-scale cloud environments, particularly with AWS. You are passionate about building secure infrastructure-as-code (IaC) pipelines using tools like Terraform or CloudFormation. You understand IAM policies, network segmentation, and VPC design and have a thorough grasp of monitoring and logging in cloud-native environments. You are skilled in identifying misconfigurations, mitigating risks, and driving remediation processes. Bonus points if you've implemented security in Kubernetes clusters or serverless architectures. - Automation and Secure Development Practices: You believe in "security as code" and are skilled at automating security processes. You can develop and integrate security tools into CI/CD pipelines to ensure secure code delivery. Tools like SAST, DAST, and dependency scanning are part of your daily toolkit, and you have experience integrating them into workflows to catch vulnerabilities early. You also advocate for secure coding practices and are skilled at mentoring teams to write resilient, secure applications. - Linux/System Security: You are well versed in AWS infrastructure security but also are passionate about scalability, reliability and operational rigor. Beyond that, you know that root does not mean root and are passionate about container security, POSIX Capabilities, SECCOMP and have a favorite flavor of LSM. In your spare time, you love playing around with OSQuery and eBPF. - Product Security (nice-to-have): Not a requirement, but a real plus: experience building secure web applications and APIs, with a working grasp of the OWASP Top 10 and common vulnerabilities such as XSS, CSRF, and SQL injection. It complements the infrastructure security focus of this role and helps when partnering with product teams. RESPONSIBILITIES: - Partner with engineering teams to review cloud and compute architecture design changes - Establish threat models for cloud and compute paved roads to identify security risks - Develop or adopt open-source tools to monitor and harden our cloud Infrastructure, harden our OS, develop security logging pipelines and detect intrusions - Apply your expert knowledge of security best practices for AWS and Kubernetes to inform remediations and the team's control roadmap - Drive the definition and implementation of security policies and monitor in conformance to the policies - Write code for automations that support security requirements like threat detection, incident containment, and network access management. - Conduct initial incident triage; determine scope, urgency, and potential impact of security incidents; participate in the incident response process At Quora, we value diversity and inclusivity and welcome individuals from all backgrounds, including marginalized or underrepresented groups in tech, to apply for our job openings. We encourage all candidates who share a passion for growing the world’s knowledge, even those who may not strictly meet all the preferred requirements, to apply, as we know that a diverse range of perspectives can have a significant impact on our products and our culture. jobs.description: FOUNDING SECURITY ENGINEER You’ll be Firecrawl’s first dedicated security hire, reporting to the Head of Core Platform. You own all of it: the API, the infrastructure behind it, and our internal systems and agents. There’s no security team to manage. You run a fleet of AI agents instead. You direct them, check their output, and keep improving them. One great person plus agents covers what used to take a department. Security has been spread across our engineers, outside pen testers, and internal agents. Nobody owned it full time. That’s you now. Our attack surface is unusual: - A public API that fetches arbitrary URLs for anyone with a key - A large crawling fleet - An open-source codebase people self-host - Internal agents with real access to production We already run regular pen tests and have SOC 2 Type II. You turn that into one program with one owner, moving at the speed of the product. Agents take the repetitive work: alert triage, access reviews, first-pass code and config review. - Salary Range: $241,000–$266,000 USD/year (SF) / $208,000–$226,000 CAD/year (Toronto) - Equity Range: Competitive equity. Details shared during the process. - Location: San Francisco, CA (SF HQ) or Toronto, ON (Toronto Hub). Hybrid, onsite 3+ days a week. - Job Type: Full-Time - Experience: 5+ years in security engineering - Work Authorization: Open to candidates already authorized to work in the US or Canada. In the US, we also support H-1B transfers, F-1 OPT and STEM OPT, TN (Canada and Mexico), and E-3 (Australia). We're not able to sponsor new H-1B visas for candidates outside the US. For Canada, we'll consider work permit sponsorship case by case through our Toronto Hub. ABOUT FIRECRAWL Firecrawl helps AI agents get the data they need through Alexandria (its library of official data providers), its own indexes, and the live web. Developers first turned to us because getting clean data from the web is harder than it looks. Today, Firecrawl has 200k+ stars on GitHub, and more than 1.5 million people build with it, including teams at 67 of the Fortune 100. The open web is only part of what agents need. Much of the most useful knowledge, like company data, financial records and research, sits behind paywalls and private APIs. Firecrawl Alexandria brings that into the same API, and we pay the providers whose data agents use. We believe people who share what they know should be compensated. OUR VALUES - Bias to action: We move fast, ship hard, and don't wait to be told. - Realistic about AI: We're clear-eyed about what AI can and can't do, and we keep pushing to use it where it actually works. - All in: The next few years matter a lot, and we're all in for them. - Human connection: As intelligence gets cheaper, relationships with customers, partners, and each other matter more. WHAT YOU’LL DO - Map the attack surface (API and keys, dashboard auth, data layer, cloud, crawling fleet, SDKs, MCP, CLI, open-source repo). Publish a ranked list of what scares you most, and work it down. Verify every fix. - Own API and platform security end to end: key scoping, leaked-key detection and rotation, tenant isolation, audit logging, egress and SSRF protections, secrets management. - Own operational security: SSO everywhere, least privilege across clouds and SaaS, endpoint and laptop security, instant offboarding, recurring access reviews. - Build detection and response: logging and alerting that catches real attacks, an incident response plan you’ve run as a tabletop, and a working vulnerability disclosure and bug bounty queue. - Secure our agents and the agent-facing product: permissions and credentials for the internal agents that run ops today, prompt injection from scraped content, and the security model for MCP and browser sessions. - Harden the open-source supply chain: dependency review, release signing, GitHub org security. - Run your own fleet of agents for alert triage, access reviews, and first-pass code and config review. Direct them, check their output, keep improving them. - Build the compliance factory. Agents keep SOC 2, and whatever comes next, continuously true for customer security reviews. WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR - You’re an engineer first. You read and write production code and ship fixes yourself. - You’re AI-pilled. You use coding agents daily and have automated real security work with them: triage, detections, code review, evidence collection. You’d rather direct a fleet of agents than manage a team, and you know how to check their work. - You have strong cloud and application security fundamentals: IAM, Kubernetes, auth, and web vulnerabilities, including SSRF. - You’ve led incident response from first alert to postmortem, and built the detections that would have caught it sooner. - You finish what you start. A finding isn’t done when the ticket is filed. It’s done when the fix is verified. People trust your numbers. - You can say no without burning bridges, and explain risk in plain language to a founder or an enterprise CISO. - Bonus: you’ve been the first security hire at a fast-growing company, and can tell us what existed when you arrived and when you left. WHAT WE’RE NOT LOOKING FOR - A policy writer who hands the work to others - Someone whose first move is to ask for headcount and a tool budget, or who wants to build and manage a security team - Someone who thinks the safe answer to AI is to ban it - Someone who measures success by how many findings they filed - Someone who needs a fully-specced ticket to start A NOTE ON PACE We operate at an absurd level of urgency because the window for what we’re building won’t stay open forever. If that excites you, keep reading. If it doesn’t, no hard feelings, but this role probably isn’t for you. BENEFITS & PERKS AVAILABLE TO ALL EMPLOYEES - Own a piece: Gain competitive equity in what you're helping build - Generous PTO: 15 days mandatory, anything after 24 days, just ask (holidays excluded). Take the time you need to recharge - Parental leave: 12 weeks fully paid, for all parents - Wellness stipend: $100 USD/month for the gym, therapy, massages, or whatever keeps you human - Learning & Development: Expense up to $1,000 USD/year toward anything that helps you grow professionally - Team offsites: A change of scenery, minus the trust falls - Sabbatical: 3 paid months off after 4 years, do something fun and new AVAILABLE TO US-BASED FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES - Full coverage, no red tape: Medical, dental, and vision (100% for employees, 50% for partner and kids). No weird loopholes, just care that works - Life & Disability insurance: Employer-paid basic life and AD&D, short-term disability, and long-term disability. Coverage for life's curveballs - Virtual care and a health guide: Teladoc for the couch doctor visit, plus Rightway to answer coverage questions and fight billing errors for you - Mental health: Talkspace, therapy and psychiatry on your schedule - Fertility and family building: Carrot, covering you and your partner - EAP: Free confidential counseling, legal and financial consults, and online will prep through Guardian - 401(k) plan: Retirement might be a ways off, but future-you will thank you - Pre-tax benefits: HSA, FSA, and commuter benefits to help your wallet out a bit - Supplemental options: Extra life and AD&D, accident, critical illness, hospital indemnity, plus pet, legal, and identity protection through MetLife AVAILABLE TO CANADA-BASED FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES - Full coverage, no red tape: Extended health, dental, and vision through Manulife (Diamond, the top tier), 100% employer-paid for you, your partner, and your kids - Life & Disability insurance: Employer-paid life, AD&D, short-term disability, and long-term disability. Coverage for life's curveballs - Virtual care: Dialogue Premium, so you can see a doctor or nurse from your couch, any hour - Mental health: Talkspace Elite, therapy and psychiatry on your schedule - Fertility and family building: Carrot, covering you and your partner - Retirem

jobs.description: WHO ARE WE? Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company. We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems. We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that. We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft. We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us! WHY THIS ROLE? The Data Infrastructure team at Cohere is responsible for the storage and data movement layer underlying every model training run. We're building the unified storage layer that feeds our training workloads at petabyte scale. In this role, you would have the opportunity to architect and lead the design of this system from the ground up, serving petabytes of training data and model checkpoints fast enough to keep thousands of GPUs busy across several training clusters. You'd be a key contributor, leading the effort to solve a problem few teams have tackled at this scale. IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL: - Design, architect, and operate the distributed storage system that feeds model training and evaluation, driving the technical vision from concept through production. - Lead and own the deployment of this system across multiple Kubernetes clusters at petabyte scale, setting standards and best practices for the organization. - Collaborate with researchers and training-infra teams to define how jobs read and write data, translating those patterns into throughput, latency, and durability requirements that shape the platform's roadmap. - Navigate the networking, I/O, and consistency challenges of moving large datasets and checkpoints across regions and backends, with GPU idle time and time-to-insight as the key metrics of success — and drive the solutions that improve them. YOU MAY BE A GOOD FIT IF YOU HAVE: - Strong storage fundamentals, including replication, consistency, caching, and data lifecycle management, with demonstrated architecture and design experience. - Strong coding ability in Python and Go, with the ability to lead implementations and mentor others in either language, and the willingness to contribute to the other. - Proven experience running stateful systems on Kubernetes, including Persistent Volumes, CSI drivers, and StatefulSets, with the capacity to design and execute operational strategies. - Hands-on experience with cloud object storage such as S3 as well as POSIX-style filesystems. IT’S A BONUS IF YOU HAVE: - Experience with parallel or HPC filesystems such as Weka, VAST, or Lustre, and a track record of applying them at scale. - Familiarity with the data-loading and checkpointing patterns used in large-scale model training, with the ability to innovate on them. - An interest in how large models are trained and evaluated, including the trajectory and eval data those runs generate, and a desire to understand the workloads the platform is serving — with the capacity to guide others in that understanding. FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES AT COHERE ENJOY THESE PERKS: - A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch. - Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health. - RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme. - 100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent. - Annual enrichment benefits: Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and a workspace improvement credit. Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching. - 6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days!) - Budget for traveling to other offices if you are remote, plus an annual company offsite. HOW AND WHERE WE WORK: - Cohere is remote-friendly, but we also have offices in Toronto, London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul with more opening soon. - For those in the office: a daily lunch program, plenty of snacks, and regular community and social events. - For those not near an office: a co-working benefit so you can work alongside others in your city. - Everyone receives a $500 home office stipend to set up your workspace properly. If any of the above doesn’t line up exactly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply. We strive to create an inclusive work environment for all; we welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are committed to providing equal opportunities. Should you require any accommodations during the recruitment process, please submit an Accommodations Request Form https://docs.google.com/forms/d/12a6IrLdF3kI2nonKSr4tiFuz18rLQbaeYV-JM9L4o9Q/edit, and we will work together to meet your needs. jobs.description: ABOUT DOCKER Docker is the platform at the center of how intelligent software gets built. For more than a decade, Docker has helped millions of developers and thousands of organizations build, ship, and run software consistently across any environment. Today, Docker extends that same trust to the AI era. Docker Hardened Images https://www.docker.com/resources/containers-are-the-new-supply-chain-attack-vector-on-demand-webinar/?at_exp=DO112.B0 form the foundation agentic code is built on, local and cloud Docker Sandboxes https://www.docker.com/products/docker-sandboxes/?at_exp=DO112.B0 isolate where agents run, and Docker AI Governance https://www.docker.com/products/ai-governance/?at_exp=DO112.B0 sets enterprise-wide policy. Together, they give builders and organizations the confidence to adopt any model, tool, or agent without compromising security, governance, or control. _______________________________________________________________________ THE ROLE The Products Team at Docker is looking for a Principal Product Manager to lead components of Docker Sandboxes. You will own and drive this strategic product area from high-level concept design through delivery, adoption, and operation. You will help shape how developers and AI agents use fast, secure, isolated environments across local and cloud workflows. You will work closely with developers inside and outside of Docker, our customers, and our partners to expand our open ecosystem offering and provide value. As the company and ecosystem grow, you will help foster teams eager to continuously build, measure, and learn. To thrive in this role, you will need experience working with developers, deep technical fluency in systems and developer infrastructure, and prior experience as a software engineer. You will need to understand containers, sandboxes/microVMs, virtualization technologies, hypervisors, the software development lifecycle, and how untrusted or agent-generated code can be safely executed and orchestrated. You will need a relentless drive to try new things and an eye for detail. Your long-term success will depend on your ability to own the product roadmap, earn the trust of the developer community, and scale reliable services. Most importantly, you will need to be comfortable taking ownership of big objectives with big goals, working with a cross-functional team, and maintaining a bias for action. _______________________________________________________________________ RESPONSIBILITIES - You own Docker Sandboxes, its long-term vision, roadmap, revenue, adoption, and results. - You believe in and can succinctly articulate our customers, their workflows, and their pain points. You empathize with the world they live in and the security, performance, compatibility, and cost constraints they work through. - You will engage deeply with developers building AI agents, coding environments, CI and testing systems, and other workloads that require secure, isolated execution, finding solutions for today while optimizing for tomorrow's vision. - You enjoy building infrastructure products that are easy to adopt and use. You will turn complex tradeoffs across isolation, startup time, performance, density, networking, storage, and cost into simple product experiences. - You are comfortable with ambiguity and will guide product definition, feature prioritization, and scope in concert with engineering, design, security, operations, and go-to-market teams. - You are a fan of iterative development, working with customers and cross-functional teams to hypothesize, measure adoption and impact, learn from releases, and continually improve the roadmap. _______________________________________________________________________ QUALIFICATIONS - You have deep empathy for the needs of developers and are obsessed with talking to your users. - You have prior professional experience as a software engineer, ideally in systems, infrastructure, platform engineering, developer tools, or cloud. - You have strong technical familiarity with sandboxes/microVMs, containers, virtualization technologies, and hypervisors, including the isolation and security boundaries each provides. - You understand the building blocks of modern developer infrastructure, including Linux, container runtimes, orchestration, networking, storage, APIs, and cloud services. - You have experience designing, building, or operating systems that execute customer-provided, untrusted, or agent-generated code at scale. - You are comfortable interacting with a command-line interface and discussing APIs, SDKs, and technical architecture with engineers and developers. - You have experience building B2B or SaaS products, or a background in public cloud and developer infrastructure. - You understand software supply chain and software security concerns, including multi-tenant isolation, identity, secrets management, observability, and reliability. - You can break down complex technical problems into small, releasable, user-valuable features. - You can explain complex ideas simply and communicate effectively in writing, verbally, and visually across diverse stakeholders. - You can analyze qualitative and quantitative data to inform decisions, define success metrics, and prioritize investments. - You have a collaborative approach, experience running products from greenfield to scale, and the ability to work with fast-moving, distributed, cross-functional teams. You are a doer as well as a strategist; we are small and need all hands on deck. _______________________________________________________________________ WHAT TO EXPECT FIRST 30 DAYS - Get to know Docker: our vision, mission, and values. - Understand the Docker Sandboxes team's mission, product strategy, and technical architecture. - Meet the team along with peers across the business unit and company. - Work closely with designers, researchers, engineers, security partners, and customers to understand user needs and current pain points. - Work with your manager and team to review and create quarterly goals. - Understand the product roadmap, key technical and business tradeoffs, and the data available to make data-driven decisions. FIRST 90 DAYS - Understand the company's and business unit's product vision and how Docker Sandboxes contributes to it. - Provide clarity on product vision, target users, priority use cases, and how the team contributes to the overall success of Docker. - Develop a deep understanding of our developers and customers, how they use isolated environments, and why they choose Docker. - Shape the team roadmap and product strategy in close collaboration with design, engineering, security, and go-to-market peers. - Lead the definition of team OKRs and success metrics for the quarter, and provide clear progress reports. ONE YEAR OUTLOOK - Lead product initiatives across cross-functional teams that make secure, isolated execution simple and valuable for developers and AI agents. - Drive the long-term direction of Docker Sandboxes, including improvements to adoption, ecosystem integration, reliability, scale, unit economics, and ARR. Visa sponsorship: Not available for this role. _______________________________________________________________________ COMPENSATION & EQUITY All full-time roles include equity. Final compensation is determined on factors including but not limited to experience, skills, qualifications, and location. Canada CA$255,500 - CA$365,000 base United States: $280,000 – $300,000 base ______________________________________________________________________ POSTING INFORMATION - Open vacancy: This posting is for an existing open role. - AI in hiring: Docker may use AI-assisted tools during our recruiting process. - Interview recordings: Candidates will be invited to opt in to interview recordings to support interviewer calibration and consistent evaluations. Recordings are optional and require explicit consent. ______________________________________________________________________ PERKS

We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that. We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft. We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us! ABOUT THE ROLE We're seeking a Senior/Staff Engineer to build and maintain the automation infrastructure that powers the development cycles of our North platform. This engineer will design and implement robust automation systems that enable engineers to efficiently test and validate changes across diverse environments and configurations. This role sits at the intersection of infrastructure and standards. You'll build the systems, frameworks, and culture that allow the rest of engineering to own quality themselves; improving and extending our testing platform by creating the infrastructure that allows engineers to write and execute tests, and enable every engineering team to ship with more confidence. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES - Design and implement automation pipelines that support comprehensive testing across multiple environments with varying feature flags and realistic customer data profiles - Create intelligent testing agents that simulate real user behavior to validate different configuration combinations - Develop and maintain GitHub workflows and actions to automate testing, deployment, and validation processes - Manage and optimize Helm charts for deployment consistency across environments - Implement and maintain ArgoCD workflows for continuous deployment and environment management - Establish best practices for testing methodologies and ensure adoption across engineering teams - Build scalable infrastructure that supports parallel test execution across diverse configurations - Develop infrastructure-as-code templates and configurations for reproducible test environments - Implement containerization strategies for test environments and dependencies - Create benchmarking frameworks to measure performance and reliability across different configurations - Monitor and improve test coverage and reliability metrics - Collaborate with product and engineering teams to understand testing requirements and translate them into automated solutions - Troubleshoot and resolve complex testing infrastructure issues REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS - 5+ years of software engineering experience with a focus on automation and testing infrastructure - Expert proficiency in Python and TypeScript - Extensive experience with GitHub workflows and actions - Generate detailed performance and reliability reports across different cloud environments - Automatically detect and flag regressions in diverse usage scenarios - Scale testing infrastructure to accommodate our growing customer base This is a critical role for ensuring the reliability and scalability of our North platform as we continue to grow our customer base and expand our feature set. ABOUT FLOAT Float is on a mission to simplify finance for Canadian businesses, empowering them to eliminate complexity and unlock new opportunities. Through our innovative platform, Float enables businesses to streamline financial operations and optimize cash flow, so they can focus on what matters most: growth. As one of Canada’s fastest growing companies https://www.theglobeandmail.com/business/rob-magazine/top-growing-companies/article-ranking-canadas-top-growing-companies-of-2024/ and top-rated startups in 2025 https://www.linkedin.com/posts/floatfinancial_were-proud-to-share-that-float-has-been-activity-7387093684720300032-2DDz/, 2024 https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/linkedin-top-startups-2024-15-canadian-companies-rise-linkedin-news-llihe/ and 2023 https://lnkd.in/TSU23CA, Float is customer-obsessed, passionate and entrepreneurial, with a team that includes leaders from Uber, Stripe, Shopify, Top Hat, Ada, Doordash, Snowflake, and Wealthsimple. At Float, everyone is an owner, bringing their unique perspective to our team and product. Your voice is important, and we take having a culture based on feedback seriously. We openly share our thoughts and differing opinions so we can continue to improve. We do our best to keep our decision-making decentralized so that all team members feel ownership in our success. OUR PRODUCT Float is Canada’s intelligent financial operating system, combining modern financial services and software to help businesses spend, save, and grow. Trusted by more than 10,000 Canadian companies, Float provides high-limit corporate cards, automated expense management, next-day bill payments, high-yield accounts, and industry-leading support, all built in Canada, for Canada. Float recently announced our $85 million Series C https://floatfinancial.com/press/float-financial-raises-cad-85-million-series-c, and is backed by world-class investors, including Inovia Capital, Growth Equity at Goldman Sachs Alternatives, OMERS Ventures, and Silicon Valley Bank. Our team is a collection of ambitious, collaborative and mission-driven people from all walks of life but with one goal: helping Canadian companies not just survive but thrive. And we’re looking for bold innovators to help shape the future of business finance in Canada. AI USE IN OUR HIRING PROCESS We use technology, including artificial intelligence (AI), to support parts of our hiring process. This may include AI-assisted scheduling and candidate communications, and AI-generated interview notes, guides or summaries to help our team focus on the conversation. All hiring decisions are made by our hiring team. ABOUT THE ROLE We're hiring Float's first Staff Security Engineer, to own the technical direction of our security platform: application, infrastructure and identity security. Our security team is small and builds more than it buys. We write our own detections, run our own agent platform, and fix things at the root. Float's engineers build quickly and we don't run big security gates, so your job is to make the secure path the easy one. You'll take a complex area of security, own it from end to end, and design the fixes alongside engineering, then drive them through to adoption across product teams. You'll look ahead too, setting up the foundations for new products, and for how we run AI tools safely, well before teams start building. You'll work as a peer to our staff and principal engineers, and explain big architectural changes and the risk behind them in a way that moves everyone toward the outcome. WHAT YOU'LL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR - Own the technical strategy for security platform work: set standards, write down decisions, and explain risk to leadership in business terms. - Own a major area of security end to end, from the risks and the plan through to shipped improvements. - Build security primitives into our core backend (Python and Django), such as default-closed authorization and tenancy scoping, then lead adoption across every product team. - Shape our customer identity platform: passwords, passkeys, SSO/SAML and machine-to-machine authentication. - Threat model and review the architecture and code of new products and large changes, and help redesign things so they are better, not only point out what's wrong. - Secure how we use AI: our internal agent platform, MCP gateways, and the data that flows through them. - Look ahead and put security foundations in place about six months before teams start building in a new area. - Lead multi-quarter efforts across several engineers as the security voice in the room, with minimal drag on engineering delivery, and mentor engineers on and off the security team. - Present significant architectural and engineering changes, with the risks, to engineers and leaders so they understand and act. - Harden our CI/CD and software supply chain, and turn controls into code (infrastructure as code, policy as code) instead of manual work. - Help secure the platform as we move to Kubernetes: workload isolation, network policy, IAM and secrets. - Build in-house tools and capabilities where it makes more sense than buying them as Float grows. - Give timely, practical advice early in the process so teams spend less time waiting on security. - Identify blind spots across the company and help set priorities for where security should invest. - Use AI tools to move faster on threat modelling, reviews, investigation and building. ABOUT YOU Here's what sets you up for success at Float: - You Put Customers First, Always. You care deeply about delivering meaningful value. Whether you're building internal systems or customer-facing features, you're always thinking about how to make life better for our users. - You Act Like an Owner. You take responsibility for outcomes, step up to challenges, and seek solutions proactively—doing what's best for the business, not just your role. - You Think Big and Move Fast. You're energized by building from 0 to 1. You're not afraid to challenge the status quo, experiment quickly, and learn as you go. - You Constantly Learn and Grow. You're hungry to improve your craft and open to feedback. You bring a growth mindset to everything you do. - You Raise the Bar. You care about doing things well and efficiently. You balance speed with rigor and always look for ways to improve how we work. - You Win as a Team. You're a generous collaborator who values communication, context, and shared wins. You lift others up and help make the team stronger. WHAT YOU'LL BRING - 8+ years of experience as a software engineer or security engineer, at a company large enough that you built systems and tools yourself. - Depth in at least one of application security, identity, or cloud and infrastructure security, and credibility across the rest. - You ship production code to fix what you find, in Python and Django or a similar web stack. - Hands-on experience designing and building security controls, tooling or systems, and the engineering depth to be a peer to staff-level engineers. - You've led a multi-quarter, cross-team technical change through influence, not authority. - A real interest in security, shown by what you've built, learned or owned. - Experience owning a complex technical problem and shipping it from start to finish. - Clear, direct writing and communication with engineers and leaders, able to explain architecture and risk in business terms in a way that leads to action. - Practical examples of using AI in your engineering or security work. jobs.description: ARE YOU A DYNAMIC PRODUCT MANAGER WITH A PASSION FOR IMPACTING SMALL BUSINESSES? Then Jobber might be the place for you! We’re looking for a Senior Product Manager to join our New Starts team, helping the next generation of home service businesses make it past their toughest years. Jobber exists to help home service businesses be successful, like your local plumbers, painters, and landscapers, to transform the way service is delivered through technology. With Jobber they can quote, schedule, invoice, and collect payments from their customers while providing an easy and professional customer experience. Running a small business today isn’t like it used to be—the way we consume and deliver service is changing rapidly, technology is evolving, and customers expect more. That’s why we put the power and flexibility in their hands to run their businesses how, where, and when they want! Our culture of transparency, inclusivity, collaboration, and innovation has been recognized by Great Place to Work, Canada’s Most Admired Corporate Cultures, and more. Jobber has also been named on the Globe and Mail’s Canada’s Top Growing Companies list, and Deloitte Canada’s Technology Fast 50™, Enterprise Fast 15, and Technology Fast 500™ lists. With an Executive team that has over thirty years of industry experience of leading the way, we’ve come a long way from our first customer in 2011—but we’ve just scratched the surface of what we want to accomplish for our customers https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EkfZmHrRLx4&list=PLoktA_D-2UEnxMLfCe93bANKXVXd2bdN8&index=24. The team: Every service business starts somewhere: a truck, a trade skill, a handful of first customers, and an owner who has never run a business before. The first years are the hardest, and too many promising businesses don’t make it through them. The New Starts team exists to change those odds. Our mission is to help new service businesses become stable, growing companies. We work across the whole journey: the first trial and the critical early weeks in the product, and the path from “just getting started” to “growing with confidence.” This is an exciting mandate, and it is deliberately different. We are accountable for whether new businesses succeed, not for a single funnel stage or a conversion number. We spend time with new owners, we favour customer-first bets over short-term metric wins, and we work hand in hand with cross-functional teams building Jobber’s AI-powered customer journey. If you want to build something meaningful from a blank page, this is that team. The role: Reporting to the Director of Product Management, the Senior Product Manager will contribute to the product strategy for New Starts and own the roadmap that brings it to life. You will work closely with Engineering, Design, and Go-To-Market stakeholders, alongside fellow Customer Experience Product Managers, to turn that strategy into experiences new owners feel in their first days and in their first year. The Senior Product Manager will: - Contribute to the vision and strategy for New Starts, defining the outcomes that matter for new businesses and the leading indicators that tell us we’re on track, then own the roadmap that gets us there. - Lead discovery with new owners. jobs.position: Senior Security Platform Engineer - Secure Delivery
jobs.description: Hi 👋🏻 I’m Louis, Head of Security. You’ll report directly to me. What Ashby gives you in return is the best of both early and growth-stage environments. The agency and no-nonsense of a seed startup: you contribute to useful projects, make practical decisions, and work in an almost-no-meeting culture. The product-market fit and scale of a growth-stage startup: tens of thousands of daily users who depend on our software, and customers whose trust your work will help us earn. We have notable customers like Notion, Linear, Shopify, and Snowflake. Our growth and retention metrics are best-in-class among our peers: we have tens of millions in ARR, growing >100% year over year, very low churn, and many years of runway. We’ll share more details once we meet. You’ll join our Security team, a single team with multiple specializations overseeing security across the business. I report to Abhik, our Co-Founder and VP of Engineering. We’re bubbling with ideas on how to support Talent Acquisition through software, and we’ve started the journey of building products beyond Talent Acquisition. We read every application and aim to respond to yours within 3-4 days (often sooner). ROLE OVERVIEW We’re looking for a platform engineer to build the secure-delivery capabilities other engineers use every day. You’ll turn security requirements into reliable integrations, useful feedback, and self-service workflows that work across our production repositories. You’ll treat engineers as your users and own the operation of what you ship. You’ll use existing tools where they fit and build the capabilities that materially improve our delivery workflow. ABOUT THE ROLE AND HOW WE WORK We’re also advertising this opening as Senior DevSecOps Engineer. Both titles describe the same position; please apply once using the title that best reflects your experience. Your mission is to make our delivery pipeline secure by default across application code, infrastructure, dependencies, containers, and product configuration. You’ll own the technical implementation and operation of delivery-security tooling and controls, including integration, configuration, tuning, reliability, and coverage. Product Engineering teams own triage and remediation for the features they maintain. Application Security provides specialist analysis and defines product-security test requirements. Infrastructure retains ownership of the underlying cloud platform. You’ll work with those teams to make agreed checks and policies run reliably in the delivery workflow. In practice, you’ll: - Deploy, configure, integrate, and tune static analysis, dependency, secret, container, and Infrastructure as Code scanning in our CI/CD workflows. - Inventory production repositories and delivery paths, including prompts and model configuration. Make scanner coverage distinct from application-specific tests of AI behavior; AppSec defines those tests, and you operate agreed delivery checks. - Start new checks in report-only mode where appropriate, then implement agreed warn and block policies using exploitability, exposure, and compensating controls. - Give engineers self-service exceptions within documented rules, with an owner, justification, expiry, and audit trail. Escalate decisions outside those rules to Security leadership with the relevant specialist analysis. - Build automation and AI-assisted workflows that enrich findings, propose fixes, and support Product Engineering’s triage under documented criteria. Preserve required checks, review, and rollback for automated patch changes. - Make coverage, integration failures, finding age by risk, time to triage and remediate, false blocks, build delay, and bypasses visible. Record mitigations separately from completed fixes and connect useful telemetry to GRC evidence. - Work with Infrastructure on cloud-posture monitoring, useful critical-misconfiguration alerts, and bounded remediation automation. - Extend into shared-image hardening and artifact provenance as the delivery foundations mature. To ground it with examples, you could: - Roll out secret scanning with push protection and make a blocked push understandable and actionable for an engineer. - Turn a repeated scanner-exception request into a PR workflow with a reason, expiry, and evidence for revisiting it. - Reproduce a dependency issue in the application, add a regression check, and build a workflow that proposes a patch with useful evidence. - Show which delivery paths are covered, where checks fail, and whether enforcement is addressing risk while keeping build delays reasonable. WHY YOU SHOULD AND SHOULDN’T APPLY You’ve built and operated CI/CD, developer tooling, or infrastructure automation used by other engineers. You can write maintainable code, explain the failure modes of what you shipped, and use security evidence to make a practical rollout decision. Supply-chain and scanner experience is useful; you can learn individual tools as part of the work. You’ve applied AI in engineering and can explain how you check its outputs and permissions. You enjoy treating engineers as users, making build-versus-buy decisions, and improving adoption and reliability after launch. You might not enjoy the role if: - You prefer to deliver a prototype and hand off its operation. Reliability, tuning, and existing integrations are part of the work. - You prefer a prescribed backlog to investigating an ambiguous problem, writing a proposal, and bringing partners into the work. - You want standalone assessments to be your main output. This role centers on working delivery capabilities and their adoption. INTERVIEW PROCESS If this also sounds exciting to you, please apply. We review every application and aim to get back to candidates within 2-3 days. For candidates who advance to the interview process, here is what you can expect: - Recruiter Screen - 30 mins - Hiring Manager Intro Call - 20 mins - Past Projects Deep Dive - 45 mins - Founder Screening - 45 mins - Take-Home Assessment + Practical Assessment Review - 1 hr (2-3 spent on take-home assignment) - Cross-Functional Stakeholder Interview - 45 mins ROLE-SPECIFIC TECHNOLOGY AND TOOLS For this role, CI/CD and infrastructure automation experience matter more than familiarity with a particular scanner. GitHub Actions or comparable systems, Terraform, containers, and cloud controls are relevant. You should be comfortable writing production automation in TypeScript, Python, Go, or a comparable language. Tool choices and individual scanner integrations are part of the work. YOUR FIRST THREE MONTHS AT ASHBY Your early changes will give you a tour of our codebase, infrastructure, and best practices, increasing in scope and ambiguity as you learn how we work. You’ll pair program with your onboarding peer as you learn the delivery workflows. Your initial focus will be to: - Map production delivery paths and gaps across code, infrastructure, prompts, configuration, and evals, with clear ownership of the different checks. - Deliver a bounded scanning integration, such as secret push protection or report-only static analysis, with a usable finding workflow. - Establish initial warn, block, and self-service exception rules with the relevant partners and make Product Engineering ownership visible. - Baseline coverage, integration failures, false blocks, and build delay so the next rollout has evidence to build on. Early progress means engineers can use the selected checks, act on their findings, and handle routine exceptions. Broader rollout follows the agreed risk policy and what the first integration teaches us. BENEFITS - Competitive salary and equity. - 10-year exercise window for stock options. You shouldn’t feel pressure to purchase stock options if you leave Ashby —do it when you feel financially comfortable. - Unlimited PTO, and we will encourage you to take it. - A minimum of 12 weeks of fully paid parental leave, covered by Ashby. The actual number may increase to satisfy local requirements.

jobs.description: ABOUT THE ROLE Hi, I’m Alexa https://www.linkedin.com/in/alexayiouroukis/, Platform Security Manager at Jane, and I’ve been here for just over a year. IAM, networking, compute, and storage should all be comfortable ground, and you read and write Terraform fluently enough to review other teams’ modules. - Production Kubernetes security depth: you’ve hardened EKS or equivalent in production across RBAC, network policy, admission controllers, runtime detection, and benchmark hardening, and you know which controls hold under real workloads and which only look good in a slide. We’re also embracing the possibilities of AI, using it to work smarter, improve our systems, and create even better experiences for our customers and our team. jobs.description: ABOUT THE TEAM The Integrations Ecosystem org builds the drivers, SDKs, connectors and BI integrations that make ClickHouse feel native in any stack. The Language Clients team maintains the official clients for Python, JavaScript, Java, Go, Rust, C++ and C#, plus the ODBC, JDBC and ADBC drivers. We're small, senior and remote across North America and EMEA. THE ROLE We're looking for a product-minded engineer to own the ClickHouse .NET client. You'll decide what the client should do by talking to the developers who use it, reading the issues and the telemetry, and listening to the community. Then you'll build it, with deep .NET expertise, and measure whether it worked. Your scope is the SDK and what builds on it: ADO.NET http://ADO.NET, Dapper and Entity Framework Core users, and the tools and integrations that depend on your client. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Know who uses the client and what they're trying to do. Define what good looks like (time to first query, error clarity, adoption by key integrations), measure it, and let that drive the roadmap. - Be the voice of ClickHouse for .NET developers. Speak at .NET conferences and meet-ups, and write the posts, tutorials and samples that developers and AI assistants find when they search for how to use ClickHouse from .NET (SEO and GEO). Answer questions where the community asks them. - Own the .NET client and its ecosystem: the client, the EF Core provider and ORM integrations, NuGet releases and support. Evolve it without breaking the people who depend on it. - Review and co-maintain other clients, and take part in cross-client decisions on types, errors and protocol features. - Bring what .NET and Windows users need to the ODBC driver, since that's how many Windows and BI tools reach ClickHouse. If you write C++, contribute to it directly. - Bring written proposals about where we invest next. You set direction rather than wait for it. - Make the client enterprise-ready: TLS and certificate handling, authentication including Microsoft Entra ID, safe credential handling, signed and reproducible packages, and the audit and compliance questions large .NET shops ask before they adopt. - Shape the client for agents as users: an API, docs and error messages an AI coding agent can use correctly on the first try. - Extend our AI development platform, with new workflows for maintaining the clients: consistency checks across languages, issue triage, release checks. ABOUT YOU - Product-minded. You decide what to build from user evidence, measure whether it worked, and can explain what you chose not to build. - 5+ years in software, much of it on data-intensive systems: drivers, SDKs, data access, ingestion or analytics. - Deep C# and .NET expertise: memory management, async and the TPL, Span and pooling, profiling and benchmarking. You reason about throughput and latency down to allocations and bytes on the wire, and you prove it with tests and benchmarks. - Fluent in C#, and productive in at least one more of our client languages (Python, JavaScript, Java, Go, Rust, C++). You'll review and co-own across clients, not only .NET. - You've built or substantially extended a library other engineers depend on, and shipped NuGet packages across .NET Framework and modern .NET. You treat breaking changes accordingly. - Fluent in .NET data access (ADO.NET http://ADO.NET, Dapper, EF Core) and at home in the wider .NET ecosystem: ASP.NET http://ASP.NET Core, Aspire, NuGet. - Security-minded. You've shipped a library into enterprise environments and know what security, compliance and procurement teams look for in a dependency. - Enthusiastic about working in public. You've given talks or written technical content, or you're keen to, and you see it as part of the job rather than a distraction from it. - Thoughtful use of AI development tools, with the judgment to review what comes out. - Clear writing. Most coordination happens in design docs, PRs and RFCs. jobs.description: COMPANY Credit Genie is a mobile-first financial wellness platform designed to help individuals take control of their financial future. We leverage artificial intelligence to provide personalized insights and are building a financial ecosystem by offering tools and services that provide instant access to cash, and building credit. Our goal is to empower every customer to achieve long-term financial stability. Founded in 2019 by Ed Harycki https://www.linkedin.com/in/ed-harycki/, former Swift Capital Founder (acquired by PayPal in 2017 https://techcrunch.com/2017/08/10/paypal-acquires-swift-financial/). Backed by Khosla Ventures and led by industry pioneers from companies such as; PayPal, Square, and Cash App, we are well positioned to build the future of inclusive finance through cutting-edge technology and customer-centric solutions. OVERVIEW The Financial Platform team owns the systems that move money at Credit Genie and the connections that make it possible: cash advances, repayments, refunds, bank account linking, debit card management, and the ledgering and reconciliation that keep every dollar accounted for. When these systems are wrong, customers lose money and trust; when they are right, nobody notices. That is the bar. As the Staff Engineer on this team, you will set the technical direction for our money movement platform and raise the engineering bar for the team around you. You will own the hardest correctness and scale problems we have, make the foundational architecture decisions that the platform will live with for years, and be the engineer the rest of the team looks to for how quality work gets done. This is a rare chance to join a fast-growing fintech startup where your work directly protects and improves the financial well-being of our users. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Set the Technical Direction: Own the architecture and long-term technical roadmap for our money movement systems. Drive the decisions on how we structure payment orchestration, ledgering, and reconciliation as transaction volume grows, and see those decisions through to production. - Build Financial Systems That Are Provably Correct: Design for the properties money movement demands: idempotent operations, exactly-once semantics, auditable state transitions, automated reconciliation, and invariant monitoring that catches discrepancies before customers do. - Design, Build, and Scale: Own backend systems end-to-end, from architecture through deployment and production operation, ensuring high performance, security, and scalability as our financial products grow. - Raise the Bar for the Team: Set the standard for engineering quality across the Financial Platform team. Lead design reviews, mentor senior and mid-level engineers, and establish practices for testing, observability, and operational excellence that outlast any single project. - Own the Bank and Card Integrations: Own the platform's connections to the outside financial world: bank account linking through data aggregators, debit card lifecycle management, and processor integrations. Build abstractions that keep these third-party dependencies reliable, observable, and swappable. - Own Production: Treat reliability of money movement as a first-class engineering problem. Lead incident response for the platform, drive post-incident hardening, and build the monitoring and safeguards that make failures rare and recoverable. - Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with product, compliance, risk, data science, and our banking and processor partners to ship features that balance speed to market with the rigor regulated money movement requires. REQUIREMENTS - 8+ years of experience designing, building, and scaling high-performance backend systems in a fast-paced, high-growth environment. - Direct experience building and operating financial platform systems at scale: payments, money movement, lending, ledgering, billing, or banking infrastructure handling high volumes of real customer funds. - Deep fluency in the correctness patterns financial software demands: idempotency, distributed transactions, double-entry accounting, reconciliation, retry safety, and auditability. - A track record of setting technical direction for a team: you have owned the architecture of a significant system, driven the roadmap to evolve it, and brought other engineers along through design reviews and mentorship. - High ownership as a default. You treat the systems you build as yours end-to-end, from design through incident response, and you raise problems and fix them without waiting to be asked. - Expertise in architecting and productionizing large-scale distributed systems. - Strong understanding of data privacy, compliance, and secure coding practices, with experience designing resilient, reliable systems that meet high security and regulatory standards. - Structured thinking and analytical rigor. You break down intricate systems, identify flaws, and implement scalable, secure, and maintainable solutions. NICE TO HAVE - Hands-on experience with payment rails and partners: ACH, RTP, card networks, push-to-debit, or direct processor and bank integrations. - Experience with bank data aggregators (Plaid, MX, Finicity) or card issuing and debit card management platforms. - Experience in regulated consumer fintech (lending, credit, or banking products). - Experience with event-driven architectures and TypeScript/Node.js services. - Experience leading incident response and building invariant or anomaly monitoring for financial data. - Experience using AI-assisted development tools to raise the quality and velocity of a team, not just your own output. BENEFITS AND PERKS Our goal is to provide a comprehensive offering of benefits and perks that promote better financial, mental, and physical wellness. We believe working alongside each other in person is the best way to build a great product and foster a strong company culture. Our expectation is that employees are in the office five days a week, allowing for optimal collaboration, inclusivity, and productivity. At the same time, we understand that life happens and recognize the importance of flexibility. We are committed to supporting our employees when circumstances arise that require remote work or adjusted schedules. Our goal is to ensure everyone can effectively balance personal and professional responsibilities while maintaining our collaborative and productive environment. Here are some highlights of our benefits and perks offerings, feel free to ask your recruiting partner for more details on our comprehensive offering for employees. - 100% company-paid medical, dental, and vision coverage for you and your dependents on your first day of employment. - Receive up to $100 per month in fitness reimbursement or enjoy a complimentary full membership to LifeTime Fitness or Equinox. - 401(k) with a 3.5% match and immediate vesting - Meal program available for both lunch and dinner - Pre-tax benefits, including a $1,000 HSA match - Life and accidental insurance - Flexible PTO Your actual level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience. Base salary is just one part of your total compensation and rewards package at Credit Genie. You may also be eligible to participate in the bonus and equity programs. You will also have access to comprehensive medical, vision, and dental coverage, a 401(k) retirement plan with company match, short & long term disability insurance, life insurance, and flexible PTO along with many other benefits and perks. Credit Genie is a proud Equal Opportunity Employer where we welcome and celebrate differences. jobs.description: BUILDING THE FUTURE OF OPEN FINANCE Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout, xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system. THE TEAM Founded in 2011, Kraken is one of the world's longest-standing crypto platforms, trusted by over 10 million individuals and institutions across the globe. It offers spot trading, margin, futures, staking, and OTC services, with products built for both individual investors and institutional clients. We are looking for a Security GRC Lead to own security governance, risk, and compliance across Payward's acquisitions. You will be the accountable owner for bringing each acquired company from its own control environment into ours, working with the M&A Technology Team from diligence through to either full platform migration or steady-state coverage under our central program. Payward acquires and integrates companies continuously, across multiple jurisdictions and regulatory regimes. Every target arrives with its own controls, its own maturity level and its own audit history, and every one enters our financial statement audit scope on a timeline set by the deal rather than by readiness. Today that work competes for the same people who run controls for the parent company. This role exists so that it has a dedicated owner. This is a build role to uphold the repeatable process for assessing an acquired company against our security baseline, mapping its controls into our compliance frameworks,and setting remediation milestones a newly acquired team can realistically hit. You will then run it, deal after deal, and you are accountable for the work getting done. THE OPPORTUNITY - Assess each acquisition target against Payward's security baseline, during diligence where deal timelines allow and immediately post-close otherwise - Map the acquired company's existing controls to Payward's control framework, and identify gaps against the external frameworks the entity falls under once in scope - Score control maturity at the entity level and document the basis for each score - Define remediation milestones that are achievable for the acquired team's size and maturity, sequenced by risk reduction rather than by framework order - Track milestones to closure and report status to Security GRC leadership and the M&A Technology Team - Recommend the endpoint for each entity: full migration onto Payward platforms, or uplift to a maturity level the central program can absorb - Load acquired-entity risks into the enterprise risk register and keep them current - Prepare acquired entities for inclusion in external audit scope, including evidence collection and walkthrough support - Act as the Security GRC point of contact for acquired-entity leadership, finance, and internal audit - Maintain policy coverage for acquired entities, including building entity-specific policy libraries where the parent policy set does not apply cleanly - Feed recurring findings back into the diligence process, so later deals are assessed against known patterns - Document the onboarding process so that it is repeatable and not dependent on one person WHAT WILL YOU DO - Target Assessment - Review target security posture during diligence: control environment, identity and access management, infrastructure, third-party dependencies, and prior audit or examination history - Produce a written assessment of each target against the Payward security baseline, separating the risks that matter to the deal from those that matter to steady-state operations - Give the M&A Technology Team and deal sponsors a clear read on what integration will cost in control remediation terms - Control Mapping and Framework Onboarding - Map acquired controls to Payward's framework and to the external frameworks the entity becomes subject to - Identify which parent-company controls extend to the entity as they are, which need an entity-specific variant, and which have no equivalent at all - Build the entity's policy library where the parent policy set does not cover it - Remediation and Milestones - Set milestones the acquired team can meet, each with a date, an owner, and a stated risk reduction - Sequence work so that the highest-risk gaps close first rather than the easiest ones - Run the cadence for tracking remediation and escalating overdue or material risks Prepare proposed risk acceptances, including the rationale and compensating controls, and present them to leadership for decision - Program Integration - Prepare entities for external audit inclusion and support fieldwork - Keep acquired-entity risk visible in the enterprise risk register and in Security GRC reporting - Hand each entity over to central GRC coverage once its maturity supports it, with the handover documented - Integrate 3rd parties and vendors into Payward WHAT YOU BRING - 5-7+ years in security governance, IT risk, or compliance, including regulated financial services, fintech, or virtual asset environments - Direct experience onboarding an acquired company into an existing controls or compliance program. This is the core of the role - Working knowledge of SOX/ICFR IT general controls and what external auditors accept as evidence - Experience with at least two of ISO 27001, SOC 1, SOC 2, and PCI DSS, including mapping controls across frameworks - Ability to assess control maturity and set remediation plans the receiving team completes, including teams below Payward's maturity level - Hands-on delivery: you write the scope, collect the evidence, and close gaps yourself when needed - Sound judgment on priorities with incomplete information, and the sense to escalate decisions that need leadership - Ability to build working relationships with control owners in IAM, infrastructure, and engineering - Ability to translate control gaps into risk language that deal teams and executives can act on - Strong project management across cross-functional, distributed teams - Preferred - CISA, CRISC, CISM, CISSP, or ISO 27001 Lead Implementer - M&A or post-merger technology integration experience - Familiarity with PKM WHY THIS ROLE - You will own a domain end to end rather than supporting someone else's. There is no incumbent process and no one else doing this work today - Acquisitions are one of the fastest-moving parts of the business, and security integration sits on the critical path for each one - You will work directly with deal teams, acquired-company leadership, external auditors, and Security GRC leadership, with visibility into how acquisitions are evaluated and closed - Payward is preparing for public company reporting, which means the controls you put in place at acquired entities are the ones external auditors will test - The scope of this role grows with the acquisition pipeline, across jurisdictions and regulatory regimes - You will join a remote-first, international team Unless a specific application deadline is stated in the job posting, applications are accepted on an ongoing basis. Please note, applicants are permitted to redact or remove information on their resume that identifies age, date of birth, or dates of attendance at or graduation from an educational institution. We consider qualified applicants with criminal histories for employment on our team, assessing candidates in a manner consistent with the requirements of the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance. jobs.description: 1Password is growing. We’ve surpassed $500M in ARR and we’re continuing to accelerate, earning a spot on the Forbes Cloud 100 for four years in a row and teaming up with iconic partners like Oracle Red Bull Racing. About 1Password At 1Password, we’re building the foundation for a safe, productive digital future. Our mission is to unleash employee productivity without compromising security by ensuring every identity is authentic, every application sign-in is secure, and every device is trusted. We innovated the market-leading enterprise password manager and pioneered Unified Access Management, a new cybersecurity category built for the way people and AI agents work today. As one of the most loved brands in cybersecurity, we take a human-centric approach in everything from product strategy to user experience. Over 180,000 businesses, from Fortune 100 leaders to the world’s most innovative AI companies, trust 1Password to help their teams securely adopt the SaaS and AI tools they need to do their best work. If you're excited about the opportunity to contribute to the digital safety of millions, to work alongside a team of curious, driven individuals, and to solve hard problems in a fast-paced, dynamic environment, then we want to hear from you. Come join us and help shape a safer, simpler digital future. 1Password helps people use technology safely. As a Security Engineer on the Corporate Security team, you’ll build and automate practical controls across identity, devices, internal tools, Software as a Service (SaaS), and the safe adoption of artificial intelligence (AI). Reporting to the Manager, Corporate Security, you’ll help protect the company while enabling teams to work securely and move quickly. How we’re using AI today Our Engineering, Product, and Design teams are thoughtfully integrating AI across the full software and product development lifecycle to move faster without sacrificing quality or security. In practice, that looks like engineers using AI-assisted coding tools to accelerate reviews and catch bugs earlier, product managers synthesizing user research at scale, and designers rapidly prototyping and iterating with AI-generated mockups. We approach AI the same way we approach security: with clear principles, human accountability at every consequential decision point, and rigorous evaluation before anything ships to customers. This is a remote opportunity within Canada and the US. What we're looking for: • Bring 3+ years of combined experience in information technology or security engineering, along with a track record of building and shipping your own solutions. • Write strong, maintainable code in Python, Bash, Go, or a similar language, and use application programming interfaces (APIs), webhooks, configuration as code, and continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) to build reliable tooling. • Apply hands-on knowledge across areas such as identity and access—including single sign-on (SSO), Security Assertion Markup Language/OpenID Connect (SAML/OIDC), multifactor authentication (MFA), and role-based access control (RBAC)—as well as endpoint and device security. • Build with AI as well as use it: work comfortably in an integrated development environment (IDE), understand the Model Context Protocol (MCP) and agentic tooling, and create automation or workflows that use AI thoughtfully. • Use tools such as structured query language (SQL) and Amazon Web Services (AWS) infrastructure to support scheduled services, reporting, and security automation. • Balance security goals with business needs, explain technical risks and trade-offs clearly, and collaborate effectively with IT, Engineering, Product, and other security teams. • Bring curiosity, ownership, and a growth mindset to a remote-first environment, with an interest in broadening your scope over time and giving actionable feedback when using security products internally. What you can expect: • Build and automate controls across identity and access, endpoint and device security, internal tools, SaaS, and AI and agentic usage. • Take well-scoped security engineering problems from design through implementation and steady-state operation. • Create integrations, visibility, detection, and reporting that make security work more reliable and reduce manual effort. • Help evaluate and de-risk new AI tools and workflows, including how agents access systems and use tools, then translate those decisions into practical controls. • Contribute to initiatives involving device trust, software authorization, security automation, and other safeguards that protect the company’s systems and data. • Partner with IT, Engineering, Product, vulnerability management, security operations, and other teams to integrate controls into broader initiatives. • Participate in the Corporate Security on-call rotation and security incident response, supporting the operational health of the systems and controls the team owns. Additional compensation is provided for on-call, and you’ll have opportunities to grow into larger areas of ownership over time. USA-based roles only: The annual base salary for this role is between $123,000 USD and $172,000 USD, plus immediate participation in 1Password's benefits program (health, dental, 401k and many others), utilization of our generous paid time off, an equity grant and, where applicable, participation in our incentive programs. Canada-based roles only: The annual base salary for this role is between $111,000 CAD and $175,000 CAD, plus immediate participation in 1Password’s generous benefits program (health, dental, RRSP and many others), utilization of our generous paid time off, an equity grant and, where applicable, participation in our incentive programs. At 1Password, we approach each individual's compensation with a promise of fair market value and internal equity commensurate with experience and specific skill set. This posting is for an existing vacancy. Our culture At 1Password, we prioritize collaboration, clear and transparent communication, receptiveness to feedback, and alignment with our core values: keep it simple, lead with honesty, and put people first. You’ll be part of a team that challenges the status quo, and is excited to experiment and iterate in search of the best solution. That said, 1Password is not for everyone https://blog.1password.com/inside-the-culture-powering-1passwords-next-chapter/. Our work is demanding, we strive for excellence, and the pace is fast. We need people who are keen to take on challenging problems, who seek feedback to grow, and who are driven to make an impact. If you're looking for a place where you can settle into a comfortable routine, this might not be the right fit for you. We’re looking for individuals who are proven experts in their fields, as well as those who are highly adaptable, can thrive in ambiguity and through change, are curious, and above all deliver results.
