jobs.description: Hi 👋🏾, I’m Abhik https://www.linkedin.com/in/abhikpramanik/, Ashby’s Co-Founder and CTO. Ashby is growing fast, which means exponential growth across every product metric: jobs, applications, interviews, you name it. We’re not slowing down, and as a result, keeping Ashby performant and reliable is a company priority. We need your leadership to do that now and in the future. We’ve already assembled a fantastic Platform & Infrastructure team of 11 engineers (all Senior+, >70% Staff), and they’ve done an excellent job handling our growth, but the management and leadership of Platform & Infrastructure have been diffused across our Engineering leaders. As we hit our next level of scale, it’s time for us to hire an Engineering leader responsible for performance and reliability, and for building out the team that ensures those. Hopefully, that’s you! THE ROLE In this role, you will report directly to me, and your responsibilities will include: - Building and maintaining a long-term vision and 6-month roadmap for Platform & Infrastructure. - Growing the Platform & Infrastructure team. You’ll hire ICs, managers, and build out a headcount plan. This will include determining if more specialized roles need to be established (e.g., DB Admin). - Building and maintaining an excellent relationship with Product Engineering. The ideal state is that Product Engineering can move incredibly fast independently without breaking performance or reliability, and Platform & Infrastructure doesn’t feel like they’re always cleaning up someone else’s “mess.” Today, there’s a great relationship, but there’s always room for improvement! - Assessing and improving our monitoring and incident management process. Again, we’re doing relatively well here, but there’s always room to improve. For example, making uptime measurement easier and improving coordination with Support during incidents. - Maintaining vendor relationships and negotiating pricing for our critical hosting and observability infrastructure, including AWS, ClickHouse, Datadog, and Braintrust. They have a meaningful impact on gross margin and need to be kept in check. - You’ve managed managers. Managing other leaders is a very different ball game, and not everyone enjoys it or thrives in it. Within your first 6 months, you’ll most likely have to hire a manager underneath you. - If you have experience managing developer experience and developer tools, building out a dedicated team for DevEx. If you don’t have experience here, DevEx will report into Product Engineering. Happy to discuss once we meet! A big part of our secret sauce is how we run Engineering. We achieve incredible speed and quality by discarding many industry norms and being optimistic about Engineers. We consider what makes exceptional Engineers exceptional, then figure out how to hire them and build an environment that gives them the freedom and agency to be exceptional. You’ll be a key leader in ensuring that continues! THE QUALIFICATIONS We’re entrusting you with a company priority, so we want you to know how to scale products and build the great teams that do that. This means: - You played an important role leading a company through a high-growth period (either as an IC Lead or Engineering Leader). You had to make high-quality decisions under pressure. That often meant striking a balance between short-term fixes to keep the product from falling over and long-term investments to ensure it didn’t happen again. - You have experience hiring and building hiring processes, and enjoy it! You’ve designed interviews, interview loops, and led hiring strategy. - You have a track record of excellent collaboration with other departments. You were a key contributor to company-level initiatives that involved Product Engineering, Product, Sales, or Support. Those departments felt heard and supported, yet positively challenged by you. - You have a background in writing production software (far beyond scripts). Our Platform & Infrastructure team is exclusively made up of strong software engineers, not just folks who scale the systems software runs on. They can jump into any part of our app, understand the code, and modify the underlying logic. We expect you to have similar experience to grow and upskill the team. - You are knowledgeable about platform and infrastructure technologies, networking, and hardware. You know how Kubernetes goes beyond a Container Orchestration Platform, how traffic flows between Load Balancers and Pods, and how the intricacies of the underlying hardware can cause Cloud abstractions to break, etc. - You are a great communicator, particularly in writing. You’ll need to be able to go deep with Infrastructure Engineers in conversations while also communicating those concepts to folks like myself who have much less experience. You should be comfortable managing a team spanning from the Americas West Coast to Europe. You’ll be able to hire managers to focus on specific time zones, but I expect you to have skips with some engineers (and you should want to, too!). jobs.description: Infisical is the open source security infrastructure platform that engineers use for secrets management, certificates, and privileged access management. We help developers and organizations securely manage billions of secrets every month including application configuration, database credentials, certificates, and more. We’ve raised ~$60M from Y Combinator, Google, and Elad Gil, and our customers include Hugging Face, OpenRouter, LG, and NVIDIA. Join us on a mission to make security easier for all developers — starting with secrets management. We’re looking to hire exceptional talent to join us in building the open source security infrastructure stack for the AI era. About the role We’re looking for an exceptional Senior Full Stack Engineer to help us build, optimize, and expand the foundation of the platform. We’ve kept our hiring standards exceptionally high since we expect engineers to tackle a broad range of challenges on a day-to-day basis. Examples of past engineering initiatives include developing strategies for secret rotation and dynamic secrets, a gateway to provide secure access to private resources, protocols like EST https://infisical.com/docs/documentation/platform/pki/est and KMIP https://infisical.com/docs/documentation/platform/kms/kmip#kmip-integration, integrations for syncing secrets across cloud providers, and entire new product lines such as Infisical PKI and Infisical PAM. You’ll be working closely with our CTO and the rest of the engineering team to: - Develop and maintain features whilst communicating directly with enterprise customers. - Expand our newer Infisical PKI https://infisical.com/docs/documentation/platform/pki/overview, Infisical PAM https://infisical.com/docs/documentation/platform/pam/overview, and Infisical KMS https://infisical.com/docs/documentation/platform/kms/overview product lines. - Experiment with novel approaches for applying AI to secrets management and more broadly security infrastructure. Requirements - Deep technical mastery of the JavaScript ecosystem, particularly React.js, Node.js, and TypeScript (3+). - Exceptional attention to detail and eager to learn. - A bias toward action—able to make decisions with incomplete information, iterate quickly, and take calculated risks. - Based in the Americas (US or Canada), Brazil, India, UK, or EU. Must work US hours. Nice to have - Expertise in Go. - Has some understanding of devops/developer tools. - Previous founder or startup experience. - Previous experience building in open source or developer tools in either a professional or personal setting. - Excellent written and oral communication skills to interact with customers directly. Team, values & benefits Our team brings experience from companies like Databricks, AWS, Red Hat, and more. We operate primarily as a remote team, but maintain a strong presence in San Francisco, where we have an office. We also get together in person throughout the year for off-sites, conferences, and team gatherings. At Infisical, we offer competitive compensation, including both salary and equity options. Additional benefits, such as a lunch stipend and a work setup budget, are available with more details to be found on our careers page https://infisical.com/careers.

We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems. We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that. We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft. We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us! ROLE OVERVIEW We're seeking a senior product leader to own Cohere's Inference as a Service business end to end. The product is sovereign, self-serve inference: a mid-market or enterprise buyer picks a model, a region and a GPU size, and is running the same afternoon with no procurement cycle and no infrastructure of their own. You'll decide which open-weights and first-party models we serve, in which regions and on which hardware, set the rate card they sell at, and carry the revenue and margin that follow from those calls. You own the platform around that endpoint as well, from the console and dashboards a customer administers their deployment through to the catalog of first-party and third-party models behind it. You'll set the strategy and run the execution, which means choosing where to spend across serving efficiency, the self-serve console and regional capacity when all three want the same budget, and shipping the deployment framework that removes infrastructure barriers while holding the line on data residency, compliance and operational confidence. You'll do that across engineering, serving, finance, legal and GTM without formal authority over most of it, and you'll be accountable for the outcome rather than for the roadmap. The timing is most of the opportunity. Every serious company is deciding where its models will run and what it costs to keep them running, serving demand is climbing faster than anyone can rack hardware for it, and very few of those buyers are willing to hand their data to an operator who can read it. We are starting this business from a standing start, with the models, the silicon and the encryption already in place and almost no one else able to offer the combination. You would be taking a product to market in the window where that advantage is still ours, building one of Cohere's major revenue lines from its first customer onward, and shaping how a generation of companies buys AI it can actually trust. RESPONSIBILITIES - Own the P&L for Inference as a Service: carry the revenue number, set the rate card, and keep blended margin above the floor as the catalog and the fleet grow. - Own the inference platform itself: the console and dashboards where customers see usage, spend, API keys, access control and attestation, and the value-add tooling that makes a managed endpoint worth more than a raw one. - Own the model inventory across first-party and third-party models: what enters the catalog, how it is grouped by provenance, what it is priced at, and when something is quantised, replaced or retired. - Set the roadmap and the investment case across serving efficiency, the self-serve surface and regional capacity, and make the call when those three compete for the same budget. - Build the commercial motion with GTM from the ground up: self-serve acquisition for the mid-market, a sales-led motion for enterprise, and the partnerships that monetise capacity we would otherwise leave idle. - Stay close to the market: talk to customers and developers about integration friction and unmet needs, track competitor pricing, catalogs and launches, and follow where models and hardware are heading, then turn that into a clear view of where we should place our bets and what it would take to win. - Define the metrics that tell us whether this is a business, including revenue, margin, win rate, time to first token and self-serve share, and lead the work that moves them. - Partner with engineering, research, legal, finance, technical writing and developer relations to ship the platform and clear the licensing, pricing and capacity decisions behind it. - Represent the business to the executive team with a recommendation, the evidence behind it and the trade-off it implies. REQUIREMENTS - 10+ years of product management experience, including meaningful time owning a B2B infrastructure or platform product at the scope of a business rather than a feature area. - Experience operating in a GM-like capacity: you have carried a revenue line or a P&L, set pricing, and been held to margin as well as to shipping. - Background at a neocloud such as Together AI, Baseten or Fireworks, or at a hyperscaler such as AWS, Azure, OCI or Google Cloud, with a working view of how inference capacity is priced, packaged and sold, and a point of view on where the segment goes next. - A track record of thinking about infrastructure as a product, with the ability to translate system-level capabilities into clearly differentiated, customer-facing features. - Entrepreneurial, with experience taking a new product to market and building the commercial motion around it rather than inheriting one. - Experience with deployment models such as multi-tenant and dedicated infrastructure, and ownership across the full product lifecycle, from problem definition through launch, iteration and eventual migration or deprecation. - Analytical by default: you define success metrics before you build, instrument thoughtfully, and use data alongside qualitative feedback to make decisions. - Able to set direction and earn alignment across engineering, infrastructure, finance, legal and GTM without formal authority, and to put a clear recommendation and its trade-offs in front of an executive audience. NICE-TO-HAVES - Experience owning a model serving or inference platform, including self-serve infrastructure and metered inference offerings. - Exposure to data residency, sovereignty, or regional compliance requirements as they apply to AI or cloud infrastructure products, particularly in the inference-as-a-service context. - Familiarity with the AI developer ecosystem and open standards, including orchestration frameworks such as LangChain and LlamaIndex, model serving frameworks such as vLLM, and an awareness of de facto interoperability standards and how they shape developer adoption and integration patterns for inference workloads. - Experience with GPU infrastructure and cloud deployment models across both neocloud and hyperscaler environments. FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES AT COHERE ENJOY THESE PERKS: - A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch. - Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health. - RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme. - 100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent. - Annual enrichment benefits: Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and a workspace improvement credit. Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching. - 6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days!) - Budget for traveling to other offices if you are remote, plus an annual company offsite. HOW AND WHERE WE WORK: - Cohere is remote-friendly, but we also have offices in Toronto, London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul with more opening soon. - For those in the office: a daily lunch program, plenty of snacks, and regular community and social events. - For those not near an office: a co-working benefit so you can work alongside others in your city. - Everyone receives a $500 home office stipend to set up your workspace properly. Datadog experience is strongly preferred. - Significant hands-on development experience and strong technical judgment: you can review the code your team writes and partner with staff engineers on architecture and system design. - Demonstrated success leading a hybrid team that spans infrastructure and application engineering on one roadmap. - A leadership style grounded in empowering the team: you set direction, clear the path, and defer to the engineers closest to the problem, staying calm and structured under pressure. - Excellent communication with technical and non-technical stakeholders, including explaining reliability risk and trade-offs to product and leadership partners. Bonus points for: - Experience with Ruby on Rails applications at scale, or with Go services and agent-based data collection. - Experience with osquery, endpoint telemetry, or other device-data pipelines. - Experience running Kubernetes-based platforms on AWS or another major cloud, including infrastructure-as-code. - Experience managing remote and distributed teams. - Experience building systems that balance rapid iteration with enterprise-grade security and compliance requirements. - Deep experience with Datadog, including APM, log management, custom metrics, and SLO-based monitoring. What you can expect: TEAM LEADERSHIP - Lead, coach, and grow a team of senior and staff engineers who own the platform layer of Device Trust, measuring your success by the team's success rather than your own visibility. - Hire, onboard, and integrate new engineers as the team grows and as Device Security and other 1Password products come to depend on these platforms. - Give engineers room to design the solutions they believe are right for customers, while holding them accountable to outcomes. The team closest to the problem makes the technical call; you make sure they have the context, time, and support to make it well. - Spend your time listening and removing obstacles: unclear priorities, missing context, cross-team dependencies, and process that slows the team down. Advocate for the team's needs with leadership and partner teams. - Support career development through regular feedback, mentorship, and growth planning, including the path from senior to staff. - Foster a culture of ownership, trust, and psychological safety, where incidents produce learning rather than blame, and lead by example on transparency, follow-through, and humility. RELIABILITY AND OPERATIONS - Own the reliability and resiliency of Device Trust applications and the platforms beneath them, against a Tier 0 expectation from customers. - Define and maintain SLOs, error budgets, and the monitoring and alerting that make them meaningful. - Lead the on-call program for the team: rotation design, escalation paths, and runbooks that let any engineer respond with confidence. - Run incident response and blameless postmortems, and drive remediation work to completion. - Plan and execute multi-region failover, disaster recovery, and capacity work, and verify it with regular exercises rather than assumptions. OBSERVABILITY - Own observability for the Device Trust platform as a product in its own right: metrics, logs, traces, and the dashboards, monitors, and SLOs built on them in Datadog, our observability platform. - Continue the work already underway on the team to instrument services end to end, so that latency, throughput, error rates, and data freshness are visible per customer, per region, and per pipeline stage. - Make the health of the platform legible to people outside the team, including support, product, and leadership, through dashboards and status reporting that answer "is it working" without an engineer in the loop. - Treat alert quality as an engineering problem: reduce n

jobs.description: ABOUT CERTN At Certn, we’re changing how trust works with The World’s Easiest Background Check. We’ve raised $127M+, earned Deloitte Fast 50 recognition three years in a row, and we’re still only scratching the surface. Our goal is straightforward: help people move faster - into jobs, homes, and opportunities - by simplifying the path to trust. We’re not a traditional background screening company. We’re a team of curious, collaborative builders who care about solving real problems for real people. We challenge each other, move fast, and have fun doing it. If you want to grow, make an impact, and help shape products used by millions, this is your place. Let’s build what’s next, together. ABOUT THE ROLE The Senior Product Manager (12-month contract) role is responsible for developing and executing product strategies and roadmaps aligned with business goals and market trends. The role drives the product development process through collaboration with cross-functional teams and utilisation of market research to inform product decisions. This role will have a strong external focus, engaging with customers, global stakeholders and industry sources to refine and prioritise the strategic direction of the solution. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES PRODUCT STRATEGY AND PLANNING - Develop and execute product strategies and roadmaps aligned with overall business goals and market trends - Define and prioritise product requirements, user stories, and use cases based on customer needs and business objectives - Conduct market research, competitive analysis, and customer insights to inform product decisions - Collaborate with cross-functional teams to gather input and ensure smooth product development and launch - Identify market opportunities, emerging trends, and customer pain points to drive product innovation - Define and communicate the product vision, roadmap, and strategy to internal and external stakeholders - Discover and validate market problems for both existing and future customers PRODUCT DEVELOPMENT - Drive the product development process from concept to launch, including defining product specifications, collaborating with engineering teams, and overseeing testing and quality assurance - Build and own the product roadmap of incremental improvements and iterative development - Collaborate with marketing and sales teams to develop product collateral, sales enablement tools, and marketing campaigns to drive product adoption and revenue growth - Provide input into go-to-market strategies, product positioning, and messaging for product launches - Analyze customer feedback and user testing to inform product decisions and iterate on features and functionality - Define and track product performance metrics, conduct data analysis, and generate insights to measure product success and identify areas for improvement - Research and evaluate new technologies, industry trends, and competitor offerings to identify opportunities for product differentiation and competitive advantage CROSS-FUNCTIONAL COLLABORATION, COMMUNICATION AND MENTORSHIP - Collaborate with cross-functional teams, including engineering, design, marketing, sales, and customer success, to ensure alignment and smooth execution of product initiatives - Build relationships and maintain open lines of communication within the company and with key external stakeholders - Monitor delivery progress and communicate with stakeholders on delays and launch timeframes so dependencies can be managed PRODUCT PERFORMANCE AND PROFITABILITY ANALYSIS - Develop profitability calculations on the potential or actual success of a proposition using ROI, cost of delay, or other modelling tools to determine which products and features to add, keep, retire, or grow - Define and analyse product success metrics to evaluate the product and any changes or new features launched - Perform data analysis in collaboration with the BI team to extract product usage statistics - Gather and organise market research to develop and articulate the positioning and value of a proposition in various markets - Work with key customers, analysts, and members of the global organisation to gather requirements for future releases based on feedback KEY QUALIFICATIONS - Proven track record of successfully developing and launching software (SaaS) products, preferably in a global or fast-paced startup environment - Deep experience with product development processes, methodologies, and best practices covering the product lifecycle - Demonstrated experience owning and driving product strategy, roadmap planning, and product lifecycle management - Demonstrated ability to collaborate with cross-functional teams, including engineering, design, marketing, sales, support, and customer success, to achieve successful product outcomes - Experience conducting market research, competitive analysis, and customer insights to inform product decisions - Data-driven mindset, with experience analyzing verification performance metrics, running experiments, and leveraging insights to drive product improvements - Excellent communication skills across all mediums - This role involves frequent travel (up to 20%). BONUS - Experience in product management for enterprise-level or B2B SaaS products - Track record of successfully working with global remote teams - Experience with go-to-market strategies and product positioning - Experience with Agile or Scrum methodologies, and familiarity with product management tools such as Jira, Asana, or Trello - Experience with decision engines and billing systems If you meet most, but not all, of the qualifications listed above, we still encourage you to apply. We recognize that strong candidates come from a wide range of backgrounds and experiences, and we value the diversity of perspectives that brings. OUR CULTURE Certn is a remote-first company with a high-performance edge. We value hustle, hunger, and helping each other win - but we also have a strict no-jerk policy. Ambition here is about lifting people up, not stepping on toes. - We think like owners and execute with urgency. - We’re customer-obsessed and always learning. - We give real feedback and hold each other to high standards. AI IN OUR CULTURE We’re AI enthusiasts. From Ops to Legal, Product to People & Culture, we use AI to move faster, make smarter decisions, and build better experiences. We believe in using AI intentionally - ethically, creatively, and always in service of delivering more for our customers and each other. Don’t worry if you’re not an expert; curiosity and a willingness to learn matter most. COME AS YOU ARE We’re committed to building a workplace that’s diverse, inclusive, and empowering for all. If you need accommodations to support any special needs at any stage of the recruitment process, just let us know - we’ve got you. ONE LAST THING… Just so you know, the selected candidate will be required to complete a background check. This means you will get to see first hand what we do, and trust us, we do it REALLY well! jobs.description: About the Role Hopper Technology Solutions (HTS) powers travel for some of the world's largest brands through our APIs, white label products and fintech, and every dataset we hold tells a story our partners need told clearly, repeatedly and fast. As a Senior Data Scientist on HTS you will own the analytical relationship with a portfolio of partners and build the machinery that answers their questions about supply health, pricing competitiveness and performance once, then answers them every week. You will be judged less on the sophistication of your models than on whether the people you work with, inside Hopper and across partner commercial teams, make better decisions because of you. What would your day-to-day look like - Own the analytical relationship with a portfolio of HTS partners, working alongside Partner Success and Commercial to understand what they need, deliver it, and present it directly to their teams - Design and templatize repeatable reporting on supply health, pricing competitiveness and tenant performance that scales across hotels, flights, homes and cars without being rebuilt each time - Use AI assistants, agents and code generation tools as everyday collaborators to automate the repetitive parts of analysis and reporting, and help the broader team adopt the same practices - Frame and run exploratory analyses that deepen our understanding of partner and traveler behavior, and translate what you find into clear recommendations for product, engineering and business leaders - Apply machine learning and statistical methods to large, messy datasets where they move the needle, and recognize when a simple, well explained metric is the better answer - Build dashboards and self serve reporting in BigQuery, Looker, Tableau, Amplitude and Google Sheets, with an eye toward making yourself unnecessary for routine questions - Partner closely with product and engineering so the data we collect supports the questions our partners will ask next An ideal candidate has - A degree in Math, Statistics, Computer Science, Engineering, Economics or another quantitative discipline, or equivalent practical experience - Extremely strong analytical and problem solving skills, with a track record of answering hard questions with data across more than one domain or product line - A proven ability to turn complex technical work into simple, credible narratives for non technical and executive audiences, including external partners - Comfort being partner facing, presenting findings, fielding tough questions live and building trust with commercial counterparts - Deep SQL skills and experience with modern data warehouses such as BigQuery, plus fluency in Python and Pandas or R for large scale data preparation and analysis - Hands on, daily use of LLM based tools such as Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor or Copilot for writing code, SQL, analysis and documentation, and a point of view on where they help and where they fall short - Experience building or deploying automated and agentic workflows, from scheduled pipelines to LLM driven report generation and prompt or skill libraries, that turn one off analyses into repeatable products - Experience with data mining, machine learning and statistical modeling, and the judgment to know when to reach for them - Experience with business reporting and experimentation tools such as Tableau, Looker or Amplitude - A strong bias toward simplifying, templatizing and shipping over polishing - Travel industry experience in lodging, air, vacation rentals or car rental, or in a marketplace, B2B platform or API distribution business, is a plus - Experience with geographic data in search, filtering or recommendation, or working with external customers in a consulting, solutions or customer analytics capacity, is a plus Perks and benefits of working with us - Well-funded and proven startup with large ambitions, competitive salary and upsides of pre-IPO equity packages - Hopper covers 100% of the premiums for group insurance plan - Hopper offers life, short term and long term disability coverage - HSA that covers eligible medical and dental expenses - All employees and dependents have access to Dialogue's telemedicine services, anytime, anywhere - All employees have access to an RRSP plan with automatic pre-tax withdrawals per pay - Please ask us about our very generous parental leave, much above industry standards! - Unlimited PTO - Carrot Cash travel stipend - Access to co-working space on demand through FlexDesk AND Work-from-home stipend - Entrepreneurial culture where pushing limits and taking risks is everyday business - Open communication with management and company leadership - Small, dynamic teams = massive impact About Hopper At Hopper, we're building the leading travel technology platform in the world, and we're doing it by solving real problems for real travelers globally. Our Hopper consumer booking platforms and HTS (Hopper Technology Solutions), our B2B business, work together to give travelers something the industry has never reliably offered: transparency, flexibility, and real savings on every trip. We combine massive amounts of data and AI with proprietary fintech products to make that happen, not just another booking engine, but a fundamentally better way to plan and experience travel for our customers and our partners. We are proof that better-for-the-customer and better-for-the-business can be one in the same And we're continuing to grow fast! The Hopper app has been downloaded over 120 million times, with 70% of our users being Gen Z and Millennials, next-generation travelers. Today, our biggest opportunity is powering travel fintech, commerce, and loyalty for some of the biggest brands in the industry. Our first HTS partnership with Capital One helped launch a dedicated travel portal for a major financial brand's cardholders, and we've since expanded across some of the biggest names in travel and banking, including Air Canada, Uber, Royal Bank of Canada (RBC), and Nubank, powering everything from a single fintech integration to a full end-to-end travel loyalty portal. That's our trajectory: we started as a small, disruptive app within the travel space, and now we're the engine under the hood powering how Travel Tech works. What that looks like in practice: - Billions of dollars in travel and travel fintech move through Hopper and HTS every year. - Our fintech products, including Cancel for Any Reason and Disruption Assistance for Any Reason, post exceptionally strong customer satisfaction because the terms are clear and resolutions are instant, no questions asked. - Nearly 30% of app customers add a fintech product to their booking, and those customers are 1.6x more likely to book with us again. - HTS now drives more than 90% of the business, proof of how fast B2B has scaled. - Through HTS, any travel provider (airlines, hotels, banks, travel agencies) can plug the company's fintech, commerce and AI solutions into their own channels, whether that's a single integration or a full end-to-end travel portal. Come take off with us! #LI-Remote While this role utilizes automated systems to assess candidate suitability, every actionable decision is made by a human member of our team. Under local regulations, you have the right to understand the principal factors used in this assessment, request a correction of your data, or request a human review of any automated decision. To exercise these rights, please contact recruitment@hopper.com

jobs.description: À propos du poste Hopper Technology Solutions (HTS) propulse le voyage pour certaines des plus grandes marques du monde grâce à nos API, nos produits en marque blanche et notre offre fintech, et chaque jeu de données que nous détenons raconte une histoire que nos partenaires ont besoin de voir racontée clairement, régulièrement et rapidement. À titre de scientifique de données principal(e) au sein d’HTS, vous serez responsable de la relation analytique avec un portefeuille de partenaires et vous bâtirez les mécanismes qui répondent une première fois à leurs questions sur la santé de l’inventaire, la compétitivité des prix et la performance, puis y répondent chaque semaine. Vous serez évalué(e) moins sur la sophistication de vos modèles que sur la capacité des personnes avec qui vous travaillez, chez Hopper comme dans les équipes commerciales de nos partenaires, à prendre de meilleures décisions grâce à vous. À quoi ressemblera votre quotidien - Assumer la responsabilité de la relation analytique avec un portefeuille de partenaires HTS, en travaillant aux côtés des équipes Partner Success et Commercial pour comprendre leurs besoins, y répondre et présenter les résultats directement à leurs équipes - Concevoir et standardiser des rapports récurrents sur la santé de l’inventaire, la compétitivité des prix et la performance des locataires, qui s’adaptent aux hôtels, aux vols, aux locations de maisons et aux voitures sans devoir être reconstruits chaque fois - Utiliser les assistants et agents d’intelligence artificielle ainsi que les outils de génération de code comme collaborateurs du quotidien afin d’automatiser les parties répétitives de l’analyse et de la production de rapports, et aider l’ensemble de l’équipe à adopter les mêmes pratiques - Cadrer et mener des analyses exploratoires qui approfondissent notre compréhension du comportement des partenaires et des voyageurs, et traduire vos constats en recommandations claires pour les responsables produit, ingénierie et affaires - Appliquer l’apprentissage automatique et les méthodes statistiques à de vastes ensembles de données désordonnés lorsqu’ils font une réelle différence, et reconnaître quand une mesure simple et bien expliquée constitue la meilleure réponse - Créer des tableaux de bord et des rapports en libre-service dans BigQuery, Looker, Tableau, Amplitude et Google Sheets, avec le souci de vous rendre inutile pour les questions de routine - Collaborer étroitement avec les équipes produit et ingénierie afin que les données que nous recueillons soutiennent les questions que nos partenaires poseront ensuite Le ou la candidat(e) idéal(e) possède - Un diplôme en mathématiques, statistiques, informatique, génie, économie ou dans une autre discipline quantitative, ou une expérience pratique équivalente - D’excellentes compétences en analyse et en résolution de problèmes, avec un historique démontré de réponses à des questions complexes à l’aide des données, dans plus d’un domaine ou d’une gamme de produits - Une capacité démontrée à transformer un travail technique complexe en récits simples et crédibles pour des auditoires non techniques et de direction, y compris des partenaires externes - De l’aisance en contact avec les partenaires, pour présenter des conclusions, répondre à des questions difficiles en direct et établir un lien de confiance avec les interlocuteurs commerciaux - De solides compétences en SQL et de l’expérience avec les entrepôts de données modernes comme BigQuery, ainsi qu’une maîtrise de Python et Pandas ou de R pour la préparation et l’analyse de données à grande échelle - Un usage quotidien et pratique des outils fondés sur les grands modèles de langage, comme Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor ou Copilot, pour écrire du code, du SQL, des analyses et de la documentation, et un point de vue sur leurs forces et leurs limites - De l’expérience dans la conception ou le déploiement de flux de travail automatisés et agentiques, des pipelines planifiés à la génération de rapports par grands modèles de langage en passant par les bibliothèques d’invites ou de compétences, qui transforment des analyses ponctuelles en produits réutilisables - De l’expérience en forage de données, en apprentissage automatique et en modélisation statistique, et le jugement nécessaire pour savoir quand y recourir - De l’expérience avec les outils de rapports d’affaires et d’expérimentation comme Tableau, Looker ou Amplitude - Un fort penchant pour la simplification, la standardisation et la livraison plutôt que le perfectionnement - De l’expérience dans l’industrie du voyage en hébergement, en transport aérien, en location de vacances ou en location de voitures, ou au sein d’une place de marché, d’une plateforme B2B ou d’une entreprise de distribution par API, est un atout - De l’expérience avec les données géographiques en recherche, en filtrage ou en recommandation, ou auprès de clients externes dans un rôle de conseil, de solutions ou d’analytique client, est un atout Avantages sociaux - Une entreprise en démarrage bien financée et éprouvée, avec de grandes ambitions, un salaire compétitif et les avantages d’un régime d’actions pré-IPO - Hopper couvre 100 % des primes du régime d’assurance collective - Hopper offre une couverture vie, invalidité de courte durée et invalidité de longue durée - Un compte de dépenses santé qui couvre les frais médicaux et dentaires admissibles - Tous les employés et leurs personnes à charge ont accès aux services de télémédecine de Dialogue, en tout temps, où que vous soyez - Tous les employés ont accès à un régime REER avec retenues automatiques avant impôt à chaque paie - Renseignez-vous sur notre congé parental très généreux, bien au-delà des normes de l’industrie - Vacances illimitées - Allocation de voyage Carrot Cash - Accès à un espace de cotravail sur demande via FlexDesk, et une allocation pour le télétravail - Une culture entrepreneuriale où repousser les limites et prendre des risques fait partie du quotidien - Communication ouverte avec la direction et les leaders de l’entreprise - Des équipes petites et dynamiques, un impact considérable À propos d’Hopper Chez Hopper, nous bâtissons la principale plateforme technologique de voyage au monde, et nous y parvenons en résolvant de vrais problèmes pour de vrais voyageurs partout sur la planète. Nos plateformes de réservation grand public Hopper et HTS (Hopper Technology Solutions), notre division B2B, travaillent ensemble pour offrir aux voyageurs ce que l’industrie n’a jamais offert de façon fiable : de la transparence, de la flexibilité et de véritables économies sur chaque voyage. Nous combinons d’immenses volumes de données et l’intelligence artificielle à des produits fintech exclusifs pour y arriver, pas simplement un autre moteur de réservation, mais une façon fondamentalement meilleure de planifier et de vivre le voyage, pour nos clients comme pour nos partenaires. Et nous continuons de croître rapidement! L’application Hopper a été téléchargée plus de 120 millions de fois, et 70 % de nos utilisateurs font partie de la génération Z et des milléniaux, les voyageurs de la prochaine génération. Aujourd’hui, notre plus grande occasion consiste à propulser la fintech, le commerce et la fidélisation en voyage pour certaines des plus grandes marques de l’industrie. Notre premier partenariat HTS, avec Capital One, a contribué au lancement d’un portail de voyage dédié aux titulaires de cartes d’une grande marque financière, et nous avons depuis étendu notre présence auprès de certains des plus grands noms du voyage et de la finance, dont Air Canada, Uber, Banque Royale du Canada (RBC) et Nubank, en propulsant aussi bien une simple intégration fintech qu’un portail de fidélisation de voyage complet de bout en bout. Voilà notre trajectoire : nous avons commencé comme une petite application perturbatrice dans l’univers du voyage, et nous sommes aujourd’hui le moteur qui propulse le fonctionnement des technologies de voyage. jobs.description: <p>About a week before Hurricane Sandy made landfall, the two leading forecast models flatly disagreed: the American one carried the storm safely out into the Atlantic, the European one turned it hard left into New Jersey. The European model wasn't running a better simulation, it was running an ensemble. Hundreds of thousands of people were evacuated on the strength of the spread in forecast distribution, days before any single forecast could have justified moving them, and on October 29th, 2012, Sandy came ashore almost exactly where the models had put it.</p> <p>At Mercury, we're building the future of financial infrastructure for startups and growing businesses. We're extending credit to those businesses, and we're doing it with proprietary access to some of the best data for understanding a borrower's business, from bank transactions to financial reporting to payroll. We're looking for a Senior/Staff Data Scientists to turn that record into a lending decision, partnering closely with Credit, Product, and Engineering.</p> <p>In this role, you'll build and own the inference layer behind our small business lending program; you'll ship it into production with the monitoring and documentation that make it trustworthy; and you'll help Credit and Product decide what we should be lending in the first place.</p> <h3>Here Are Some Things You'll Do On The Job:</h3> <ul> <li>Build and own the models behind our lending program - transaction classification, recurring inflow/outflow detection, annual revenue estimation, forecasting with seasonality, anomaly detection, and more</li> <li>Turn messy data streams - bank transactions, storefront sales, and more - into a defensible view of a business's health</li> <li>Deploy models into a production environment with observability, monitoring, and tests</li> <li>Partner with Credit on underwriting policy: what data is asked for, when follow-up information is worth the friction, and how to quantify uncertainty</li> <li>Partner with Product on the shape of the product: from principal sizes and pricing to repayment terms</li> <li>Assess where predictive modeling actually moves the underwriting program</li> <li>Set the technical bar for ML in Credit</li> </ul> <h3>You Should:</h3> <h4>For Staff:</h4> <ul> <li>Have 7+ years building ML models</li> <li>Implemented models that shaped automated decisions with money on the line</li> <li>Write production-grade Python</li> <li>Have depth beyond classification models; for example: time series and forecasting, anomaly detection, and NLP models</li> <li>Be proficient with deep learning, transformers, and LLMs</li> <li>Be strong in SQL and at home in a data warehouse</li> <li>Be able to explain a model to a credit officer, a model validator, a PM, and an engineer</li> <li>Be able to set modeling standards for your data-science colleagues</li> <li>Have a quantitative degree, or the equivalent built some other way</li> </ul> <h4>For Senior:</h4> <ul> <li>Have 3+ years building ML models, and at least 1 year in lending or credit algorithms</li> <li>Be opinionated and thoughtful on where ML can best lift an underwriting program</li> <li>Some exposure to using deep-learning / transformer models in a professional context</li> <li>Be strong in Python, with experience working on production-grade services</li> <li>Be strong in SQL and at home in a data warehouse</li> <li>Be able to explain a model to a credit officer, a model validator, a PM, and an engineer</li> <li>Be able to set modeling standards for your data-science colleagues</li> <li>Have a quantitative degree, or the equivalent built some other way</li> </ul> <h3>Nice To Have:</h3> <ul> <li>Direct experience modeling on bank transaction data</li> <li>Experience in small business lending or business credit cards</li> <li>Experience with revenue-based financing, merchant cash advances, or similar products</li> </ul> <p>*Mercury is a fintech company, not an FDIC-insured bank. jobs.description: WHO ARE WE? Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company. We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems. We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that. We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft. We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us! ABOUT NORTH: North https://cohere.com/north is Cohere's cutting-edge AI workspace platform, designed to revolutionize the way enterprises utilize AI. It offers a secure and customizable environment, allowing companies to deploy AI while maintaining control over sensitive data. North integrates seamlessly with existing workflows, providing a trusted platform that connects AI agents with workplace tools and applications. WHY THIS ROLE? This role offers a unique opportunity to shape how enterprises harness the power of AI in real-world applications. As a bridge between our core North product and our clients’ engineering teams, you’ll be at the forefront of solving complex problems and securely integrating AI into critical sectors such as finance, healthcare, and telecommunications. Our esteemed clients include industry leaders like RBC, Dell, and LG CNS. We are seeking engineers who deeply care about customers and want to work at the cutting edge of Agentic AI. In this role, you will: - Lead end-to-end deployment of North in private cloud and on-premises environments, including planning, configuration, testing, and rollout. - Partner with enterprise IT teams to assess infrastructure, security requirements, and data management practices. - Experiment at a high velocity and with a high level of quality to engage our customers and ultimately deliver solutions that exceed their expectations - Design and implement deployment strategies tailored to client needs, ensuring compliance with data privacy and security standards. - Troubleshoot and resolve deployment-related technical issues, providing timely solutions to minimize downtime. jobs.description: <div class="content-intro"><p>At Affirm, we exist for the moments that matter—giving people a clear, predictable way to pay over time, with no hidden fees, no surprises, and no tradeoffs on what matters most.</p></div><p>We build the experiences that connect a customer's intent to buy with the flexibility of Affirm Card. From making financing options easier to understand to creating intuitive checkout journeys, we turn complex financial capabilities into simple, trustworthy experiences. Our roadmap includes evolving Default Terms, supporting additional cards, and strengthening the mobile experiences customers rely on when deciding how to pay.</p> <p>Our work sits at the intersection of mobile, backend systems, and product innovation. We partner closely with Product, Design, and engineering teams across Affirm to introduce new capabilities while protecting the reliability of our checkout-critical surfaces.</p> <p>As a full-stack Software Engineer II, you'll help bring these experiences to life through customer-facing features and the services behind them. We're looking for a curious, collaborative engineer who cares about the complete customer journey and enjoys turning challenging problems into thoughtful solutions. Together, we'll make Affirm Card easier to use and help customers make financial decisions with greater confidence.</p> <p><strong>What You'll Do</strong></p> <ul> <li>With the support of your team's tech lead and manager, you will break down larger projects into individual tasks, deliver them in multiple phases, and collaborate with others to ensure timely delivery of your work.</li> <li>You will support your peers and stakeholders in the product development lifecycle by collaborating with product management, design &amp; analytics by participating in ideation, articulating technical constraints, and partnering on decisions that properly consider risks and trade-offs.</li> <li>You will support the operations and availability of your team's artifacts by creating and monitoring metrics, escalating when needed, and supporting "keep the lights on" &amp; on-call efforts.</li> <li>You will contribute to a sense of community on your team by engaging in growth and development activities such as participation in the interview process.</li> </ul> <p><strong>What We Look For</strong></p> <ul> <li>You have a total of 1.5+ years of experience as a software engineer.</li> <li>You have experience designing, developing and launching backend systems and are proficient in one of Python or Kotlin.</li> <li>You are familiar with the building blocks of distributed systems, and the technologies like AWS, MySQL and Kubernetes.</li> <li>You have experience shipping web apps using declarative UI frameworks like React or Vue.</li> <li>You have experience designing, developing and launching APIs at scale using languages like Python or Kotlin.</li> <li>You have mastered taking a simple problem or business scenario into a solution that interacts with multiple software components, and executing on it by writing clear, easily understood, well tested and extensible code.</li> <li>You are comfortable navigating a large code base, debugging others' code, and providing feedback to other engineers through code reviews.</li> <li>Your experience demonstrates that you take ownership of your growth, proactively seeking feedback from your team, your manager, and your stakeholders.</li> <li>You have strong verbal and written communication skills that support effective collaboration with our global engineering team.</li> </ul> <p data-pm-slice="1 1 []"><strong>Base Pay Grade</strong> - L</p> <div> <p><strong>Equity Grade</strong> - 5</p> <p>Employees new to Affirm typically come in at the start of the pay range. Affirm focuses on providing a simple and transparent pay structure which is based on a variety of factors, including location, experience and job-related skills.</p> <p>Base pay is part of a total compensation package that may include monthly stipends for health, wellness and tech spending, and benefits (including 100% subsidized medical coverage, dental and vision for you and your dependents). In addition, the employees may be eligible for equity rewards offered by Affirm Holdings, Inc. (parent company).<br><br><strong>CAN base pay range per year: </strong>CAD $133,000 - $183,000.<br><br>This remote role is open only to candidates residing in Alberta, British Columbia, Manitoba, New Brunswick, Newfoundland and Labrador, Nova Scotia, Ontario, Prince Edward Island, or Saskatchewan.</p> </div> <div> <div><strong><span style="font-weight: 400;">#LI-Remote</span></strong></div> </div><div class="content-conclusion"><div> <p><strong>Remote-first with flexibility built in</strong><strong><br></strong>Affirm is proud to be a remote-first company. Most roles can be done from almost anywhere within the country of employment. Some positions may occasionally require in-person work at an Affirm office, and a few are office-based due to the nature of the work. All new hires will be invited to attend an in-person onboarding experience.</p> <p><strong>Benefits designed for you</strong><strong><br></strong>Our benefits reflect our commitment to care, transparency, and flexibility. Here are a few highlights:</p> <ul> <li>Health coverage at no cost: We cover 100% of premiums for employees and their dependents.</li> <li>Spending stipends: Monthly stipends support your tech setup, and the ability to choose health and wellness options that are right for you.</li> <li>Time off to recharge: Flexible time off and generous holiday calendars help you rest when you need to.</li> <li>Own a piece of what you build: Our employee stock purchase plan (ESPP) lets you buy Affirm stock at a discount.</li> </ul> <p>We’re committed to providing an inclusive interview process, including accommodations for candidates with disabilities. If you need support, we’re happy to help.</p> <p>For positions based in San Francisco or Los Angeles: Affirm considers qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records, as required by law.</p> </div> <div> <p>By clicking "Submit Application," you acknowledge that you have read Affirm's&nbsp;<a href="https://www.affirm.com/global-candidate-privacy-notice" target="_blank">Global Candidate Privacy Notice</a> and consent to the use of your personal information as described.</p> </div></div>

jobs.description: ABOUT THE ROLE At Fellow, we’re building a collaborative, agentic assistant that makes the moments before, during, and after meetings more valuable. Behind that simplicity is significant complexity spanning devices, platforms, permissions, and integrations. Design’s role is to make it feel effortless and intuitive. Designers at Fellow have unusually broad ownership. We don’t have a traditional product function where requirements are handed to you to execute. Instead, designers identify problems, propose solutions, guide implementation, and work closely with others to bring their ideas to market. This role is for someone comfortable with ambiguity, responsibility, and owning outcomes from ideation through launch and beyond. If you’ve longed to operate across both design and product, but haven’t had the freedom to do so, read on. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Perform your own research to discover and propose new initiatives. - Design mockups and functioning prototypes with world-class visual polish. - Adapt experiences across web, desktop, mobile, and our Chrome Extension. - Regularly contribute to our design library of tokens, components, and patterns. - Leverage coding tools to ship front-end improvements to production. - Own the roadmap, milestones, timelines, and issues for your team's work WHAT YOU NEED - 7+ years experience designing software that spans many surfaces. - Comfortable leading without authority, owning your team's success. - Ability to identify problems, distill feedback, and advocate for changes. - Mastery of visual design, layout composition, and information hierarchy. - Familiarity with code and experience creating production prototypes. - Effective written and verbal communication skills as we're remote-first. WHAT WE OFFER At Fellow, we care about those that make our mission possible. You can expect: - Fair and competitive compensation $130,000 - $160,000 CAD - Remote-first within Canada on Eastern time - 3 weeks paid vacation, sick leave, and holidays - Company-wide paid end of year break - Health and dental coverage - 12 weeks of paid parental leave at 80% of your salary - Yearly team events and a personal learning budget

The Identity team builds the systems that power secure and seamless access across the MaintainX platform. We design and operate authentication, authorization, and governance services that scale with our enterprise customers and keep user experience frictionless and trusted. What you’ll do: - Develop and enhance IAM features — Implement and maintain authentication, authorization, and user management services across MaintainX, supporting both frontend and backend systems. - On-call duties About you: - You have a minimum of 5+ years of professional experience in full-stack software development. - Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution in Computer Science or related field. - Strong programming skills in C# and/or TypeScript, with experience building production-grade applications. - Familiarity with React and Node.js, and an understanding of modern web authentication patterns. - Interest in Identity and Access Management (IAM) — including authentication, authorization, user provisioning, and permissions systems. - Experience designing and consuming REST or GraphQL APIs. - Proficient at writing understandable, maintainable, and testable code. - Strong communication and collaboration skills; comfortable working in a cross-functional environment. - An expert level of English, both spoken and written, is required, as the individual will need to lead platform engineering managers across multiple teams, present technical priorities to executive stakeholders, and align with engineering leaders outside Québec on a daily basis. Nice to have: - Experience integrating with SSO protocols such as OAuth 2.0, OIDC, or SAML. - Hands-on experience with Okta, Azure AD, or similar identity providers. - Exposure to SCIM or other user provisioning standards. - Understanding of token-based authentication (JWT, PKCE, token exchange). - Knowledge of encryption standards, SSL/TLS, or public/private key infrastructure. - Experience with React Native applications. - Experience with Docker and Kubernetes. - Experience with observability practices, as well as knowledge of observability tools such as Datadog. - Familiarity with cloud providers (AWS, Azure, GCP) and service deployment practices. - Experience with CI/CD pipelines and modern DevOps workflows to streamline testing and deployment. About us: Our mission is to deliver one platform for maintenance, repair & operations teams to keep the physical world running. We believe the greatest asset in any organization is the people. That’s why we built an intuitive, mobile-first solution to help boost productivity and collaboration across teams and locations. MaintainX is committed to creating a diverse environment. jobs.description: Cerebras Systems builds the world's largest AI chip, 56 times larger than GPUs. jobs.description: WHO IS LITMUS Litmus is building the data foundation that powers industrial AI. AI doesn’t work without real-world, contextualized data - Litmus makes that data usable. As AI adoption accelerates, most industrial environments still can’t access or use their operational data. We solve that gap. We’re a growth-stage software company helping manufacturers access, structure, and use real-time data from machines, systems, and sensors at the edge. Our platform sits at the intersection of edge computing, AI, and industrial operations, enabling some of the world’s largest companies to run operations in real time, reduce downtime, and optimize production. Backed by leading investors and trusted by global manufacturers and partners like Google, Microsoft, Dell, Oracle, and Mitsubishi, Litmus is powering the shift toward software-defined manufacturing. WHY JOIN LITMUS BUILD THE INFRASTRUCTURE THAT MAKES INDUSTRIAL AI POSSIBLE AI is moving beyond the cloud and into the physical world. At Litmus, you’ll build the infrastructure that enables real-time data to power AI and machine learning systems in production environments. WORK ON PROBLEMS WHERE SOFTWARE MEETS THE REAL WORLD Most AI systems fail without access to real-world data. You’ll build the layer that makes them viable in production. We solve challenges at the intersection of distributed systems, real-time data, and industrial constraints — where reliability, scale, and performance are non-negotiable. HAVE REAL IMPACT, FAST You’ll work on systems used by real customers in production, with direct impact on product and company trajectory. As a scaling company, we move quickly. You’ll have ownership, visibility, and the ability to shape both product and company as we scale. JOIN A HIGH-PERFORMANCE TEAM We’re building a team that holds a high bar and pushes each other to improve. You’ll work alongside experienced operators, engineers, and leaders who have done this before and are building again at scale. We hire people who take ownership, move quickly, and care about outcomes. No passengers. OUR CULTURE At Litmus, the team is collaborative, curious, and low ego. People are scrappy, take ownership, and look for ways to make an impact. We value empathy just as much as execution, whether that’s in how we build, how we communicate, or how we support each other. We’re a growing company, so things move quickly and not everything is perfectly defined. If you enjoy figuring things out, working closely with others, and making steady progress, you’ll do well here. ABOUT THE ROLE Litmus is seeking a hands-on Senior Product Manager, Product Security to drive product security across Litmus Edge, Litmus Edge Manager, Litmus UNS, and related platform services. This role combines product management, software engineering, cybersecurity, and AI expertise. You will own the product security roadmap, proactively identify vulnerabilities, collaborate with Engineering on remediation, and research secure, scalable architectures for current and future products. We are looking for a technical product leader who can translate security challenges into product improvements while actively participating in technical investigations, prototyping, and security research. WHAT YOU’LL DO PRODUCT SECURITY STRATEGY AND ENGINEERING - Own and drive the product security roadmap across the Litmus product portfolio - Proactively identify security vulnerabilities, architectural weaknesses, and emerging threats - Track relevant CVEs, security advisories, and open-source dependencies. Prioritize remediation based on risk and product impact - Conduct hands-on vulnerability assessments, security investigations, and architecture reviews across applications, APIs, Linux systems, containers, and infrastructure - Reproduce vulnerabilities, investigate root causes, and validate fixes with Engineering - Review source code, configurations, and deployment architectures to identify security risks - Build scripts, proof-of-concepts, and automated tests to evaluate and validate security solutions - Work directly with Engineering to plan security improvements, prioritize releases, and balance immediate fixes with long-term investments SECURITY ARCHITECTURE, AI, AND R&D - Research and evaluate emerging security technologies and architectures for industrial edge and enterprise environments - Design and validate secure, scalable deployment models across edge devices, virtual machines, containers, Kubernetes, and cloud infrastructure - Explore zero-trust principles, workload isolation, sandboxing, authentication, authorization, and secure communication - Evaluate the security implications of AI-powered applications, autonomous agents, and edge AI workloads - Apply AI-assisted tools to vulnerability discovery, code analysis, security testing, and automation - Prototype new security approaches and translate research into product capabilities and roadmap initiatives - Anticipate future enterprise security requirements and proactively improve product architecture SECURE DEVELOPMENT AND CROSS-FUNCTIONAL COLLABORATION - Partner with Engineering, DevOps, and QA to integrate security into product design, development, testing, and releases - Drive secure development practices, automated security testing, dependency management, and software supply chain security - Define security requirements for APIs, OAuth, RBAC, device management, remote access, and software updates - Coordinate product security incident response, vulnerability remediation, and security-related releases - Establish security review processes, technical guidelines, and measurable security objectives SECURITY ASSESSMENTS, COMPLIANCE, AND CUSTOMER ENGAGEMENT - Coordinate third-party penetration testing, security assessments, and product security audits. Drive remediation of findings - Support compliance and certification initiatives, including ISO 27001, SOC 2, IEC 62443, and the EU Cyber Resilience Act, as applicable - Collaborate with IT, DevOps, and leadership on security governance, access controls, and employee security awareness - Participate in enterprise customer security discussions, technical assessments, and security reviews - Translate customer security requirements into product features and roadmap priorities - Develop product security incident response procedures, vulnerability disclosure processes, and customer security communications WHAT YOU’LL BRING MUST HAVE - 7+ years of experience in software engineering, product security, cybersecurity, security architecture, or technical product management - Strong hands-on software engineering experience with the ability to investigate vulnerabilities, review code, and validate technical solutions - Experience defining technical product roadmaps and driving security initiatives with Engineering teams - Strong understanding of Linux, Docker, Kubernetes, networking, and cloud infrastructure - Practical knowledge of vulnerability assessment, penetration testing methodologies, threat modeling, and secure software development - Experience with application and API security, authentication, authorization, encryption, TLS, and certificate management - Familiarity with CVE/CVSS, open-source dependency security, and vulnerability management - Experience with AI-assisted development or security tools, scripting, and automation - Ability to independently research technologies, build prototypes, and collaborate on engineering implementations - Strong communication skills to engage technical teams, leadership, and enterprise customers NICE TO HAVE - Experience with industrial IoT, edge computing, OT security, or enterprise infrastructure software - Knowledge of industrial protocols such as OPC UA and MQTT - Experience with embedded Linux, firmware security, secure boot, and OTA updates - Familiarity with zero-trust architecture, container hardening, virtualization, sandboxing, and microVM technologies - Experience securing AI applications, autonomous agents, or edge AI work

jobs.description: ABOUT KEYCARD At Keycard, we're building identity and access infrastructure for the agent-native era, where software isn't static but a dynamic, constantly changing system of AI agents working on behalf of people and businesses. Keycard gives every agent a verified identity and issues short-lived, task-scoped credentials at runtime, so agents can only do what they were asked to do, and every action is fully auditable. We're backed by a16z, Boldstart, and Acrew, and our founding team built and scaled Snyk, Auth0, HashiCorp, and Heroku. THE ROLE We're hiring two staff-level Software Engineers, Infrastructure to own how Keycard is built, shipped, and run. Keycard is a control plane for agents: identity, credential exchange, delegation, policy, and audit. Many of the enterprises adopting it need that control plane inside their own cloud, behind their network controls, with no standing access for us. Bring-your-own-cloud (BYOC) is a product at Keycard, not a services engagement. It's versioned, documented, and held to the same reliability and security bar as our hosted service. You'll own Keycard's build and release systems, our multi-tenant cloud, dedicated deployments, and deployments in customers' cloud accounts. Build common delivery and operating tools across them, with release safety, reliability, cloud cost, and repeatable installs as priorities. You'll work with founders, engineers, product, and customers, and agree escalation and on-call with engineering. We build on AWS (and later GCP and Azure), EKS, Pulumi, and Helm. WHAT YOU'LL DO - BYOC product. Own what it's like to install, upgrade, and get support for Keycard in a customer's cloud, from what their security team reviews to how each version is documented. - Compatibility. Decide what we support, from clouds, regions, and Kubernetes versions to customer guardrails like SCPs and egress proxies. Set the skew limits and deprecation policy that keep our control plane and customer-hosted deployments compatible. - Deployments. Make a new deployment, ours or a customer's, a configuration change: infrastructure as code, account bootstrap, and network patterns like PrivateLink and certificates that work through customer proxies. For example: take a new customer's AWS account to a running, upgradeable deployment with no standing access from us. - Releases. Own one pipeline from commit to running deployment, wherever it runs, with the control plane kept separate from the data plane. Get releases to many independently versioned deployments with staged promotion, approval gates, and rollback. - Reliability. Set the availability and durability targets we hold ourselves to for the hosted service, with the observability, runbooks, and incident response behind them. Operate customer-hosted deployments without standing access, using audited break-glass. - Agent operations. Build agents for the repetitive work: pre-install checks, installs, failed-upgrade triage, and runbook drafts. They run with scoped credentials, every action is audited, and an engineer approves any change to a customer account. - Cost per install. Keep each install cheap in engineering time and cloud spend. Decide what's standard, what's configurable, and what we decline, so one customer's request doesn't become the roadmap. - Deployment guardrails. Work through reviews with customers' cloud and security teams. With security, set the guardrails for every deployment, from credential scope and isolation to workload identity and PKI, then build and run them. WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR - You build infrastructure as software in Pulumi, Terraform, or CDK, and write the Go or TypeScript tooling around it. You've run Kubernetes and Helm in production. - Deep AWS experience, especially IAM and permission boundaries, Organizations and SCPs, and VPC networking. - You've run software in accounts you don't control, like customer VPCs, on-prem, or regulated networks, and supported it through upgrades. - You've shipped versioned releases that customers upgrade on their own schedule, with a support matrix and deprecations they could plan around. - You debug across layers: a hung request that turns out to be a security group rule, a proxy that breaks a TLS handshake, a certificate challenge that can't reach the internet. - You've worked directly with customers' platform and security teams, and turned down a one-off when a product change was better. - You think in control plane and data plane: you've designed or run systems where the two are separate and upgrade independently. - Agents at work. You already use coding agents in infrastructure work and have a clear view of where they're reliable and where a human has to review. jobs.description: ABOUT KEYCARD At Keycard, we're building identity and access infrastructure for the agent-native era, where software isn't static but a dynamic, constantly changing system of AI agents working on behalf of people and businesses. Keycard gives every agent a verified identity and issues short-lived, task-scoped credentials at runtime, so agents can only do what they were asked to do, and every action is fully auditable. We're backed by a16z, Boldstart, and Acrew, and our founding team built and scaled Snyk, Auth0, HashiCorp, and Heroku. THE ROLE We're hiring a staff-level Software Engineer, SDK to own the libraries developers use to put Keycard in front of their agents and MCP servers. For most teams, the SDK is the first Keycard code they touch: a few lines that add OAuth to an MCP server, then token exchange so a tool can call GitHub or Google as the user. Keycard is a control plane for agents: identity, credential exchange, delegation, policy, and audit. Our SDKs come in two kinds. The REST API clients for Python, TypeScript, and Go are generated from our OpenAPI spec. The agent SDKs are handwritten: OAuth primitives, MCP server and client auth, agent-to-agent (A2A) delegation (in preview), and integrations for frameworks like FastMCP, LangChain, Temporal, and Cloudflare Workers. The hard design work is on the handwritten side. Python is the most complete today. TypeScript is in preview and working toward parity, and Go and Ruby are earlier. Keeping behavior consistent across four languages, while priorities differ and TypeScript comes next, is the core of the job. You'll work with founders, product, and the engineers building the services underneath. WHAT YOU'LL DO - API design. Keep authorization concepts and behavior consistent across languages while making each API idiomatic. Map credential types and error semantics across Python, TypeScript, Go, and Ruby. - Safe defaults. Require the expected issuer and audience for token validation, and handle signing-key outages without accepting unverified tokens. Refresh client-held access tokens when the grant permits it, and return clear errors when fresh authorization is needed. - Track upstream. Our MCP package follows the upstream MCP SDK's major versions, and framework integrations are tested nightly against each upstream's latest release. Ship support for new versions quickly, and decide when an old line moves to security fixes only. - Releases. Each package versions and publishes on its own, to PyPI, npm, and RubyGems, with Go modules released as versioned tags in their repos. Own semver, changelogs, deprecations, and the CI that bumps and publishes on merge. - Generated clients. Own the path from our OpenAPI spec to the generated clients. Fix problems in the spec, not in generated code. - Developer experience. Quick starts, examples, and docs that take someone from install to a protected MCP server, and a loop that turns developer feedback into API changes. - Agents at work. Coding agents already open a good share of our SDK pull requests. Decide what they're trusted to do, and keep tests and review strong enough to catch what they get wrong. WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR - You've shipped libraries or SDKs that other developers depend on, and supported them through breaking changes. - You've kept one API consistent across at least two languages. You write idiomatic Python and TypeScript; Go or Ruby is a plus. - You know OAuth 2.0 and OIDC at the library level: token verification, refresh, PKCE, and token exchange (RFC 8693). - You've managed versioning in the real world: peer dependency ranges, maintenance branches, and deprecations users could plan around. - You've built framework integrations or protocol libraries, and can work through MCP's authorization flows and compatibility changes. STRONG CANDIDATES MAY ALSO HAVE - Code generation for multi-language SDKs: Stainless, Speakeasy, Fern, OpenAPI, or protobuf. - Plugin or integration ecosystems, like Terraform providers, framework adapters, or editor extensions. - Contributions to MCP, the A2A protocol (which we support in preview), or open source agent frameworks. - Edge runtimes like Cloudflare Workers, or durable execution like Temporal. YOUR FIRST 90 DAYS - Close the biggest gaps between the TypeScript and Python SDKs, toward dropping TypeScript's preview label. - Publish a cross-language API guide: names, errors, and credential types, mapped across Python, TypeScript, Go, and Ruby. - Take one upstream breaking change, like a new MCP SDK major or framework release, from nightly failure to released support. - Agree an SDK roadmap with product and engineering, including where generated clients end and handwritten SDKs begin. WHO WILL LOVE THIS JOB - You care about the first ten lines a developer writes with your library. - You'd rather design an API once than explain it four different ways. - You use coding agents every day, and you know which of their changes need a closer look. WHAT WE OFFER - Build at the Frontier: Work every day at the frontier of agent-native systems — shipping, inventing, and iterating on technology that hasn’t been built before. You’ll be given huge autonomy, the opportunity to gain mastery, and the chance to work in a team that holds each other accountable to succeed. - Truly Agent-Native Culture: At Keycard, we don’t just enable others to adopt agents — we use them ourselves to build. You’ll help shape an organization that embeds AI into its foundation as an enduring competitive advantage. - Compensation With Upside: Market-competitive salaries and generous equity packages (4-year vest, 1-year cliff) give you the security to focus on building — and the asymmetric upside of ownership in a company chasing a category-defining mission. - Comprehensive Benefits & Recharge: Health, dental, vision, and paramedical coverage for you and your family, plus 4 weeks vacation, 11 statutory holidays, and 1 volunteer day annually. We encourage at least 2 weeks off each year to fully recharge. - Tools That Keep You Ahead: A new MacBook Pro, a $500 stipend for peripherals, and the best AI tools available so you can work at the forefront of agent-native workflows. - Remote-First Flexibility: We are a remote-first team prioritizing asynchronous collaboration, with hiring focused in North and South America. Work where you’re strongest — we just want the best.
