jobs.description: PLATFORM PARTNERSHIPS LEAD, AI LABS & AGENTS Agents find tools in plugin stores, and the tools that are listed, current, and ranking well get installed. Most of our active teams already find Firecrawl that way, through the AI labs and agent harnesses they build on. This hire protects that channel and grows it. You'll own Firecrawl's place inside the labs and harnesses, so we're the default data provider before a team makes its engineering decision. Labs and harnesses want agents that work on real tasks, and real tasks need live web data. Firecrawl and Alexandria supply it, so better agents mean more runs on their platform. You'll be the person both sides call. That means owning our relationships with the teams that run those stores, getting our MCP and plugin updates through their approval processes, and keeping a two-way line into what they're building next. You'll report to Eric Ciarla, Co-Founder & Chief Growth Officer, and work day to day with our deployment and engineering teams. Salary Range: $220,000–$249,000 USD/year base Equity Range: Competitive equity. Details shared during the process. Location: San Francisco, CA (SF HQ). Hybrid, onsite 3+ days a week. You live where the labs do. We have a strong in-office culture and value in-person collaboration. Job Type: Full-Time Experience: 5+ years in partnerships, platform, developer relations, GTM engineering, or growth roles, or a body of work that makes the case. Either way, you can name the people you'd call at the major labs. Work Authorization: Open to candidates already authorized to work in the US. We also support H-1B transfers, F-1 OPT and STEM OPT, TN (Canada and Mexico), and E-3 (Australia). We're not able to sponsor new H-1B visas for candidates outside the US. ABOUT FIRECRAWL Firecrawl helps AI agents get the data they need through Alexandria (its library of official data providers), its own indexes, and the live web. Developers first turned to us because getting clean data from the web is harder than it looks. Today, Firecrawl has 200k+ stars on GitHub, and more than 1.5 million people build with it, including teams at 67 of the Fortune 100. The open web is only part of what agents need. Much of the most useful knowledge, like company data, financial records and research, sits behind paywalls and private APIs. Firecrawl Alexandria brings that into the same API, and we pay the providers whose data agents use. We believe people who share what they know should be compensated. HOW WE WORK We’re a small team where everyone owns a meaningful part of the product and the company, end to end. In September 2026, we raised a $75M Series B led by Smash Capital, giving us the runway to build for the long haul. We’re based in San Francisco, with an office in Toronto. We build the infrastructure other AI companies run on, and we move fast because the window of opportunity won’t stay open forever. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Get listed and ranking. Get Firecrawl live, up to date, and ranking well on the plugin stores of the leading labs and the harnesses on the rise. - Choose where to aim. Use agents to map the labs and harnesses, then decide where your time and relationship capital go. Back today's leaders and tomorrow's. - Build a two-way channel. Meet regularly with platform and product teams. Learn what they're building and how stores rank plugins, then bring it back to shape our product. - Show up where lab teams are. Host dinners, workshops, and conference side-events in SF. Show up at theirs, whether that's an executive dinner or the pickleball courts. - Turn intel into shipped work. Take what you hear to engineering and get our updates out fast. WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE IN 30 DAYS - Firecrawl is listed and current on every priority store. - You've mapped the landscape and have a ranked target list with a plan for each. - You have a standing cadence with platform teams at the priority labs and harnesses. - At least one update has moved through a store's approval process with you driving it. WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR Relationship capital comes first. Everything else is secondary. - Real relationships at the major labs. You know people at Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Meta, or xAI, and you can name them. Friendships count more than LinkedIn connections. - Based in San Francisco. You live where the labs do. - Relentless. You get the door open, no matter what, and you'd rather make the intro than write the plan. - Technical fluency. You understand how MCPs work, use agents, and happily vibe code. WHAT WE'RE NOT LOOKING FOR - Someone who only knows the formal channel. Enterprise partnerships run on contracts and quarterly reviews. This role also runs on a friend who can get a plugin reviewed this week. - Relationship-only candidates who won't touch the product. You don't need to have been an engineer. You do need to understand MCPs and agents well enough to explain what you're pitching. - People who need a finished playbook. We're mapping the stores as we go. If you need a target list and a plan before you can start, you'll stall here. BONUS POINTS - You've shipped in a store: an integration approved and ranking well on a large platform. A lab or agent harness is ideal. Slack, Shopify, Salesforce, Atlassian, Chrome, VS Code, Cursor, and similar marketplaces count too. - You've built or published an MCP server, plugin, or extension. - You have a network in the SF AI and developer scene: lab teams, accelerators, meetup and dinner organizers. - You've hosted dinners, workshops, or side-events that people kept coming back to. - You've used Firecrawl, or reached it through Claude Code, Cursor, or n8n. OUR VALUES - Bias to action: We move fast, ship hard, and don’t wait to be told. - Realistic about AI: We’re clear-eyed about what AI can and can’t do, and we keep pushing to use it where it actually works. - All in: The next few years matter a lot, and we’re all in for them. - Human connection: As intelligence gets cheaper, relationships with customers, partners, and each other matter more. A NOTE ON PACE We operate at an absurd level of urgency because the window for what we're building won't stay open forever. If that excites you, keep reading. If it doesn't, no hard feelings, but this role probably isn't for you. BENEFITS & PERKS AVAILABLE TO ALL EMPLOYEES - Salary that makes sense: $220,000–$249,000 USD/year base, based on impact, not tenure - Own a piece: Gain competitive equity in what you're helping build - Generous PTO: 15 days mandatory, anything after 24 days, just ask (holidays excluded). Take the time you need to recharge - Parental leave: 12 weeks fully paid, for all parents - Wellness stipend: $100 USD/month for the gym, therapy, massages, or whatever keeps you human - Learning & Development: Expense up to $1,000 USD/year toward anything that helps you grow professionally - Team offsites: A change of scenery, minus the trust falls - Sabbatical: 3 paid months off after 4 years, do something fun and new AVAILABLE TO US-BASED FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES - Full coverage, no red tape: Medical, dental, and vision (100% for employees, 50% for partner and kids). No weird loopholes, just care that works - Life & Disability insurance: Employer-paid basic life and AD&D, short-term disability, and long-term disability. Coverage for life's curveballs - Virtual care and a health guide: Teladoc for the couch doctor visit, plus Rightway to answer coverage questions and fight billing errors for you - Mental health: Talkspace, therapy and psychiatry on your schedule - Fertility and family building: Carrot, covering you and your partner - EAP: Free confidential counseling, legal and financial consults, and online will prep through Guardian - 401(k) plan: Retirement might be a ways off, but future-you will thank you - Pre-tax benefits: HSA, FSA, and commuter benefits to help your wallet out a bit - Supplemental options: Extra life and AD&D, accident, critical illness, hospital indemnity, plus pet, legal, and identity protection thro

jobs.description: Cerebras Systems builds the world's largest AI chip, 56 times larger than GPUs. This architecture allows Cerebras to deliver industry-leading training and inference speeds; over 10 times faster than GPU-based hyperscale cloud inference services. This order of magnitude increase in speed is transforming the user experience of AI applications, unlocking real-time iteration and increasing intelligence via additional agentic computation. Cerebras works with the leading model labs, global enterprises, and cutting-edge AI-native startups. OpenAI recently announced a multi-year partnership https://openai.com/index/cerebras-partnership/ with Cerebras, to deploy 750 megawatts of scale, transforming key workloads with ultra high-speed inference. We are seeking an experienced Hardware Lab Manager to lead the operations and expansion of our system hardware labs. You will own the infrastructure, equipment, team, and processes that enable hardware bring-up, system integration, and validation across multiple generations of AI and high-performance computing systems. This role combines hands-on technical leadership with operational planning and people management. Working closely with hardware, systems, validation, manufacturing, IT, and facilities teams, you will ensure our labs are safe, reliable, and ready to support increasingly complex systems and configurations. Key Responsibilities - Own lab operations and readiness. Manage daily operations across internal system hardware labs and coordinate test capabilities at contract manufacturer (CM) labs, ensuring equipment, infrastructure, and support are available for engineering milestones. - Plan and scale infrastructure. Translate product roadmaps into lab capacity plans covering space, racks, power, cooling, networking, instrumentation, and staffing. Support concurrent development and validation of multiple system generations. - Manage equipment and budgets. Own equipment selection, procurement, installation, calibration, preventive maintenance, repair, and retirement. Plan lab investments, manage vendors, and maintain accurate asset and inventory records. - Lead and develop the team. Manage lab engineers and technicians, establish priorities, balance workloads, and build technical capabilities through coaching, training, and clear operating expectations. - Enable engineering execution. Partner with engineering teams on system deployment, hardware bring-up, troubleshooting, and test setup. Establish reliable provisioning, remote access, and equipment reservation processes. - Build scalable workflows. Develop practical tools, operating procedures, and playbooks for equipment tracking, configuration management, request intake, maintenance, and issue resolution. - Maintain safety and compliance. Establish lab safety and electrostatic discharge (ESD) practices, coordinate training, maintain documentation, and support regulatory inspections and audits with relevant internal partners. - Oversee logistics and hardware handling. Manage receiving, packaging, shipping, storage, and return merchandise authorization (RMA) workflows for prototype systems, components, and equipment. - Deliver lab upgrades and expansion. Coordinate with facilities teams, landlords, contractors, service providers, and vendors on build-outs, repairs, maintenance, and expansion while minimizing disruption to engineering work. Skills and Qualifications - Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related technical discipline, or equivalent practical experience. - 10+ years of relevant experience in hardware engineering labs, system validation environments, or technical lab operations, including substantial ownership of lab infrastructure and operations. - Demonstrated experience leading lab engineers, technicians, or comparable technical teams. - Hands-on experience supporting server hardware, AI accelerators, high-performance computing systems, or enterprise data center platforms, including rack-level deployment and system bring-up. - Practical experience with liquid cooling, power distribution units (PDUs), and high-voltage power delivery, including safe operating and maintenance practices. - Working knowledge of lab networking, including structured cabling, switch configuration, DHCP, DNS, and VLANs. - Experience managing equipment procurement, calibration, maintenance, inventory, vendors, and infrastructure projects. - Familiarity with electrical safety, ESD controls, and applicable environmental, health, safety, and compliance requirements. - Strong organizational and communication skills, with the ability to prioritize competing requests and take operational issues from identification through resolution. - Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced environment, make sound decisions with incomplete information, and adapt processes as the organization grows. Preferred Qualifications - Experience building or expanding hardware labs from initial requirements through commissioning. - Familiarity with Linux, server provisioning, BIOS and firmware configuration, and out-of-band management tools. - Experience coordinating engineering test capabilities with CMs or other external manufacturing partners. - Experience supporting environmental chambers, mechanical prototyping facilities, or cleanroom environments. - Experience developing lightweight automation or implementing lab asset management and infrastructure monitoring tools. Location: Sunnyvale, CA Compensation The annual base salary range for this position is $220,000 - $290,000. Actual base salary will be determined based on relevant experience, skills, and qualifications. Additional compensation may include bonus and equity. Why Join Cerebras People who are serious about software make their own hardware. At Cerebras, we have built a breakthrough architecture that is unlocking new opportunities for the AI industry. With dozens of model releases and rapid growth, we’ve reached an inflection point in our business. Members of our team tell us there are five main reasons they joined Cerebras: 1. Build a breakthrough AI platform beyond the constraints of the GPU. 2. Publish and open source their cutting-edge AI research. 3. Work on one of the fastest AI supercomputers in the world. 4. Enjoy job stability with startup vitality. 5. Our simple, non-corporate work culture that respects individual beliefs. Find out more about what it's like to work at Cerebras here https://www.cerebras.ai/join-us! Apply today and become part of the forefront of groundbreaking advancements in AI! Cerebras Systems is committed to creating an equal and diverse environment and is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate different backgrounds, perspectives, and skills. We believe inclusive teams build better products and companies. We try every day to build a work environment that empowers people to do their best work through continuous learning, growth and support of those around them. jobs.description: Cerebras Systems builds the world's largest AI chip, 56 times larger than GPUs. This architecture allows Cerebras to deliver industry-leading training and inference speeds; over 10 times faster than GPU-based hyperscale cloud inference services. This order of magnitude increase in speed is transforming the user experience of AI applications, unlocking real-time iteration and increasing intelligence via additional agentic computation. Cerebras works with the leading model labs, global enterprises, and cutting-edge AI-native startups. OpenAI recently announced a multi-year partnership https://openai.com/index/cerebras-partnership/ with Cerebras, to deploy 750 megawatts of scale, transforming key workloads with ultra high-speed inference. About the Team The Cerebras Data Center team plans and delivers the infrastructure behind our AI systems. We work across site strategy, power and cooling, hardware, networking, supply chain, deployment, and operations to bring reliable capacity online across multiple locations. About the Role We are seeking a Data Center Capacity Planner to translate business and AI infrastructure demand into an integrated capacity plan. You will determine where capacity is needed, when it must be available, and which constraints could affect delivery. Working with Data Center leadership, infrastructure engineering, delivery program managers, supply chain, finance, and commercial teams, you will connect demand forecasts with available and planned supply. Your analyses will guide site expansion, equipment planning, and capacity allocation decisions. Responsibilities Build and maintain near-term and long-range demand and supply forecasts by site and region, connecting AI compute requirements to system counts, racks, critical power, cooling, and network capacity. Reconcile customer commitments, expected growth, utilization, and engineering plans; distinguish committed demand from forecast opportunities and document planning assumptions. Maintain a clear view of installed, commissioned, allocated, available, and planned capacity. Account for operating reserves, redundancy requirements, and capacity that cannot yet support workloads. Model capacity gaps and expansion scenarios, incorporating utility timelines, construction and commissioning milestones, hardware availability, and supplier lead times. Recommend when to expand, reserve, or rebalance capacity. Partner with Finance to assess capital requirements, operating costs, utilization, and the tradeoffs between earlier availability and unused capacity. Partner with delivery TPMs to translate approved capacity plans into site requirements and milestones; update forecasts when schedules, demand, or infrastructure constraints change. Work with Data & Tooling partners to establish planning datasets, reconciliation checks, and dashboards. Track forecast accuracy, capacity coverage, utilization, and changes in expected availability. Lead recurring capacity reviews, explain material changes, and present decisions and recovery options to leadership with clear assumptions, owners, and dependencies. Required Qualifications - 5+ years of experience in capacity planning, infrastructure planning, operations research, supply and demand planning, or a related analytical role supporting complex infrastructure. - Experience building demand and supply models across multiple locations or infrastructure environments, including scenario analysis and reconciliation of changing assumptions. - Understanding of data center capacity constraints and dependencies across electrical power, cooling, space, hardware, networking, and deployment readiness. - Strong SQL and spreadsheet modeling skills, with the ability to combine operational and financial data, validate results, and explain the limits of incomplete information. - Ability to convert forecasts into specific recommendations and influence decisions across engineering, finance, program management, and operations. - Clear written and verbal communication, including concise leadership updates that explain capacity gaps, timing risks, and decision tradeoffs. - Bachelor’s degree in engineering, computer science, operations research, mathematics, supply chain, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. - Preferred Qualifications - Experience planning capacity for AI, high-performance computing, hyperscale cloud, or colocation environments, including high-density infrastructure. - Proficiency with Python or another analytical language for forecasting, optimization, and repeatable planning workflows. - Experience with business intelligence tools, data center infrastructure management systems, enterprise resource planning systems, or infrastructure inventory platforms. - Familiarity with power delivery timelines, liquid cooling, long-lead electrical and mechanical equipment, or global data center expansion. - Experience connecting workload demand and service requirements to fleet utilization, capacity reservations, and investment planning. Why Join Cerebras People who are serious about software make their own hardware. At Cerebras, we have built a breakthrough architecture that is unlocking new opportunities for the AI industry. With dozens of model releases and rapid growth, we’ve reached an inflection point in our business. Members of our team tell us there are five main reasons they joined Cerebras: 1. Build a breakthrough AI platform beyond the constraints of the GPU. 2. Publish and open source their cutting-edge AI research. 3. Work on one of the fastest AI supercomputers in the world. 4. Enjoy job stability with startup vitality. 5. Our simple, non-corporate work culture that respects individual beliefs. Find out more about what it's like to work at Cerebras here https://www.cerebras.ai/join-us! Apply today and become part of the forefront of groundbreaking advancements in AI! Cerebras Systems is committed to creating an equal and diverse environment and is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate different backgrounds, perspectives, and skills. We believe inclusive teams build better products and companies. We try every day to build a work environment that empowers people to do their best work through continuous learning, growth and support of those around them. jobs.description: BUILDING THE FUTURE OF OPEN FINANCE Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout, xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system. THE TEAM Founded in 2011, Kraken is one of the world's longest-standing crypto platforms, trusted by over 10 million individuals and institutions across the globe. It offers spot trading, margin, futures, staking, and OTC services, with products built for both individual investors and institutional clients. We are looking for a Security GRC Lead to own security governance, risk, and compliance across Payward's acquisitions. You will be the accountable owner for bringing each acquired company from its own control environment into ours, working with the M&A Technology Team from diligence through to either full platform migration or steady-state coverage under our central program. Payward acquires and integrates companies continuously, across multiple jurisdictions and regulatory regimes. Every target arrives with its own controls, its own maturity level and its own audit history, and every one enters our financial statement audit scope on a timeline set by the deal rather than by readiness. Today that work competes for the same people who run controls for the parent company. This role exists so that it has a dedicated owner. This is a build role to uphold the repeatable process for assessing an acquired company against our security baseline, mapping its controls into our compliance frameworks,and setting remediation milestones a newly acquired team can realistically hit. You will then run it, deal after deal, and you are accountable for the work getting done. THE OPPORTUNITY - Assess each acquisition target against Payward's security baseline, during diligence where deal timelines allow and immediately post-close otherwise - Map the acquired company's existing controls to Payward's control framework, and identify gaps against the external frameworks the entity falls under once in scope - Score control maturity at the entity level and document the basis for each score - Define remediation milestones that are achievable for the acquired team's size and maturity, sequenced by risk reduction rather than by framework order - Track milestones to closure and report status to Security GRC leadership and the M&A Technology Team - Recommend the endpoint for each entity: full migration onto Payward platforms, or uplift to a maturity level the central program can absorb - Load acquired-entity risks into the enterprise risk register and keep them current - Prepare acquired entities for inclusion in external audit scope, including evidence collection and walkthrough support - Act as the Security GRC point of contact for acquired-entity leadership, finance, and internal audit - Maintain policy coverage for acquired entities, including building entity-specific policy libraries where the parent policy set does not apply cleanly - Feed recurring findings back into the diligence process, so later deals are assessed against known patterns - Document the onboarding process so that it is repeatable and not dependent on one person WHAT WILL YOU DO - Target Assessment - Review target security posture during diligence: control environment, identity and access management, infrastructure, third-party dependencies, and prior audit or examination history - Produce a written assessment of each target against the Payward security baseline, separating the risks that matter to the deal from those that matter to steady-state operations - Give the M&A Technology Team and deal sponsors a clear read on what integration will cost in control remediation terms - Control Mapping and Framework Onboarding - Map acquired controls to Payward's framework and to the external frameworks the entity becomes subject to - Identify which parent-company controls extend to the entity as they are, which need an entity-specific variant, and which have no equivalent at all - Build the entity's policy library where the parent policy set does not cover it - Remediation and Milestones - Set milestones the acquired team can meet, each with a date, an owner, and a stated risk reduction - Sequence work so that the highest-risk gaps close first rather than the easiest ones - Run the cadence for tracking remediation and escalating overdue or material risks Prepare proposed risk acceptances, including the rationale and compensating controls, and present them to leadership for decision - Program Integration - Prepare entities for external audit inclusion and support fieldwork - Keep acquired-entity risk visible in the enterprise risk register and in Security GRC reporting - Hand each entity over to central GRC coverage once its maturity supports it, with the handover documented - Integrate 3rd parties and vendors into Payward WHAT YOU BRING - 5-7+ years in security governance, IT risk, or compliance, including regulated financial services, fintech, or virtual asset environments - Direct experience onboarding an acquired company into an existing controls or compliance program. This is the core of the role - Working knowledge of SOX/ICFR IT general controls and what external auditors accept as evidence - Experience with at least two of ISO 27001, SOC 1, SOC 2, and PCI DSS, including mapping controls across frameworks - Ability to assess control maturity and set remediation plans the receiving team completes, including teams below Payward's maturity level - Hands-on delivery: you write the scope, collect the evidence, and close gaps yourself when needed - Sound judgment on priorities with incomplete information, and the sense to escalate decisions that need leadership - Ability to build working relationships with control owners in IAM, infrastructure, and engineering - Ability to translate control gaps into risk language that deal teams and executives can act on - Strong project management across cross-functional, distributed teams - Preferred - CISA, CRISC, CISM, CISSP, or ISO 27001 Lead Implementer - M&A or post-merger technology integration experience - Familiarity with PKM WHY THIS ROLE - You will own a domain end to end rather than supporting someone else's. There is no incumbent process and no one else doing this work today - Acquisitions are one of the fastest-moving parts of the business, and security integration sits on the critical path for each one - You will work directly with deal teams, acquired-company leadership, external auditors, and Security GRC leadership, with visibility into how acquisitions are evaluated and closed - Payward is preparing for public company reporting, which means the controls you put in place at acquired entities are the ones external auditors will test - The scope of this role grows with the acquisition pipeline, across jurisdictions and regulatory regimes - You will join a remote-first, international team Unless a specific application deadline is stated in the job posting, applications are accepted on an ongoing basis. Please note, applicants are permitted to redact or remove information on their resume that identifies age, date of birth, or dates of attendance at or graduation from an educational institution. We consider qualified applicants with criminal histories for employment on our team, assessing candidates in a manner consistent with the requirements of the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance. We hire based on merit, seeking out people with the right abilities, knowledge, and skills for the job. With decades of experience creating and deploying real world systems for demanding environments, the Stack team is dedicated to developing an autonomous solution ecosystem tailored to the trucking industry's unique demands.</p> <p>If you are an Internal Candidate, please apply via our Internal Job Board.</p></div><p><strong>About the Role:</strong></p> <p>In the ML Data Understanding team, our mission is to provide trusted and useful data to efficiently power all of Stack's ML applications end-to-end from mining to training to safety evaluation. jobs.position: Staff Software Engineer, Sandbox Secrets (West Coast)
jobs.description: ABOUT DOCKER Docker is the platform at the center of how intelligent software gets built. For more than a decade, Docker has helped millions of developers and thousands of organizations build, ship, and run software consistently across any environment. Today, Docker extends that same trust to the AI era. Docker Hardened Images https://www.docker.com/resources/containers-are-the-new-supply-chain-attack-vector-on-demand-webinar/?at_exp=DO112.B0 form the foundation agentic code is built on, local and cloud Docker Sandboxes https://www.docker.com/products/docker-sandboxes/?at_exp=DO112.B0 isolate where agents run, and Docker AI Governance https://www.docker.com/products/ai-governance/?at_exp=DO112.B0 sets enterprise-wide policy. Together, they give builders and organizations the confidence to adopt any model, tool, or agent without compromising security, governance, or control. _______________________________________________________________________ THE ROLE As AI agents redefine software development, Docker is at the center of that shift, providing the local and cloud sandboxed environments that make interactive and autonomous agentic workflows trustworthy by default. At the heart of our trust model is the fact that user credentials and other sensitive secrets are injected at the sandbox layer and never exposed to an agent. An agent can never leak secrets it never sees. The Secrets team builds the software that makes that possible, from easy-to-use SDKs to secure cloud services to high-performance network proxies. We operate at the intersection of the developer experience, enterprise governance, and security – delivering core security features that make Docker sandboxes the best way to run agents and other workloads safely. As a Staff Software Engineer on the Secrets team, you’ll design and build core security systems that power Docker’s agentic platform and AI governance products. Your work will focus on creating scalable, reliable, and secure software that enables developers to safely run agentic workloads while allowing administrators to confidently manage their organization’s security posture. The successful candidate is a technical, product-minded engineer with deep experience building secure software and scale-out cloud services and a track record of shipping critical infrastructure. They think naturally about isolation and security boundaries, understand the tradeoffs involved in running untrusted or semi-trusted workloads safely, and can reason confidently about a system that spans multiple surface areas. If you thrive on solving security and usability challenges, are enthusiastic about agentic development but conscious of the risks it entails, and want to help shape the future of Docker’s platform, we’d love to hear from you. Please note: this role is currently prioritizing candidates currently located in the Western time zone (US or Canada). _______________________________________________________________________ RESPONSIBILITIES - Design, develop, and lead improvements to the secrets management and credential injection systems. - Investigate and resolve security, correctness, performance, and stability issues across cloud, macOS, Windows, and Linux. - Collaborate with peers, Product, and adjacent teams to evolve the architecture as requirements grow. - Mentor engineers on the team and set the bar in design reviews and code reviews. - Engage with the open source and agentic development community around sandboxing, MCP, and related ecosystems. - Participate in on-call rotations and respond to critical stability issues affecting users. - Document your work clearly and share knowledge with the rest of the team. _______________________________________________________________________ QUALIFICATIONS REQUIRED - 8+ years of software engineering experience, with demonstrated technical leadership on production systems at scale. - Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience - Experience building developer tools, desktop applications, or runtime infrastructure used directly by developers. - Familiarity with the agentic software development ecosystem: how coding agents work and how tools like Claude Code, Codex, or similar agents interact with their environment. - Ability to reason about isolation and security boundaries: what a sandbox should and shouldn't expose, and how to make safe defaults obvious to users. - Experience driving architecture and technical strategy across multiple engineers or teams. - Strong written and verbal communication skills. - Comfortable working with a high degree of autonomy in a remote-first environment. PREFERRED - Strong proficiency in Go, Rust, and/or Java - Experience with cryptographic key management systems and techniques (key wrapping, HSMs, cloud KMSes, etc.) - Familiarity with best practices for protecting credentials and secret material at-rest and in transit - Understanding of networking, TLS, HTTP, and the like. - Understanding of one or more OS-specific credential management capabilities. Visa sponsorship: Docker considers visa sponsorship on a case-by-case basis based on business needs. _______________________________________________________________________ COMPENSATION & EQUITY All full-time roles include equity. Final compensation is determined on factors including but not limited to experience, skills, qualifications, and location. United States: $170,350 – $275,550 base ______________________________________________________________________ POSTING INFORMATION - Open vacancy: This posting is for an existing open role. - AI in hiring: Docker may use AI-assisted tools during our recruiting process. - Interview recordings: Candidates will be invited to opt in to interview recordings to support interviewer calibration and consistent evaluations. Recordings are optional and require explicit consent. ______________________________________________________________________ PERKS & BENEFITS - Remote-first by design – Work from your home, with offices in Seattle and Paris for connection and collaboration. - Flexibility that fits your life – We trust you to manage your schedule while delivering great work. - Time to recharge – Generous PTO, designated quarterly Whaleness Days, and a designated end-of-year Whaleness break. - Home office support – Set up your workspace for comfort and success. - Technology stipend – Equivalent to US$100 net per month to help support your work. - Learning & development – Annual stipend for conferences, courses, certifications, and continued learning. - Parental leave – 16 weeks of paid parental leave after six months of employment. - Equity for all full-time employees – Share in Docker's long-term success as we continue to grow. - Comprehensive benefits – Medical, retirement, and paid holidays vary by country. - Docker swag – Because representing the whale never gets old. We believe diverse teams build better products, make better decisions, and better serve our global community. #LI-REMOTE

jobs.description: At ClickUp, we're building the future of work: the first truly converged AI workspace unifying tasks, docs, chat, calendar, and enterprise search, all supercharged by context-driven AI. We are an AI-native company. Every team member is expected to leverage AI daily, and we evaluate AI fluency as part of our hiring process. Join us and help redefine what's possible. 🚀 Security at ClickUp Security at ClickUp is engineering-focused. We partner with teams across the company to protect our platform, our internal systems and our customers through secure design, defensive controls, detection and response. We build tooling and automation, including AI-powered workflows, to turn what we learn into lasting improvements. About the team Infrastructure Security at ClickUp secures the cloud, compute, network and access layers underneath ClickUp: a multi-account AWS organization, a large Kubernetes fleet, infrastructure managed as code and the identity systems engineers use to reach production. We are a small team that works agentic first, using AI agents we build and maintain ourselves to multiply what a team our size can cover. You will support this mission by thinking like a developer, breaking down a problem that we face, testing a method to approach it with automation, and implementing solutions that yield compounding value. Your skills to uncover threat indicators will be the foundation of this work. The role - Architecture, proposals and reviews. Act as an initial reviewer on infrastructure proposals and designs from engineering and non-engineering teams such as business systems and go-to-market. Write our own security proposals and review the changes that follow. Translate security requirements and agent findings into clear guidance for less-technical partners, and bring their needs back into our designs. - Agentic security tooling and agent infrastructure. Build, evaluate and maintain the agents behind our reviews, triage and investigations, and help run the sandboxed, observable infrastructure they operate on. - Detection, investigation and response. Lead cloud and infrastructure alerts and incidents through to resolution and root cause, working alongside AppSec and incident response on incidents that span both. - Identity, access and least privilege. Move people, CI and services toward least privilege and just-in-time access across our cloud organization and the tooling engineers use to reach production. Deliver fixes as secure building blocks that teams adopt by default. - Compute, network and pipeline security. Harden our container, serverless and virtual machine workloads, our network perimeter and our CI/CD pipelines, and add checks so each class of issue is caught automatically next time. - Continuous review and audit evidence. Move vulnerability, access and attack-surface reviews from point-in-time checks to continuous monitoring that also produces evidence for our infrastructure controls. Qualifications - 5+ years in security engineering, cloud infrastructure or SRE, with at least 2 years securing AWS at organization scale. - At least a year of agentic development experience: building agent skills and tools for real engineering work, and developing and maintaining the development harness they run in, from configuration and permissions to integrations, evaluations and cost controls. You can secure agents against prompt injection, over-privileged tools and unaudited actions, and explain how agents fall into the confused deputy problem and the lethal trifecta. You validate agent output against evidence and decide where human review is required. - Deep AWS IAM experience: IAM Identity Center or an equivalent SSO model, SCPs, permission boundaries, resource and key policies, cross-account trust, and the ability to prove a policy's effect with simulation rather than inference. - Production Kubernetes security on EKS or similar, covering RBAC, workload identity, network policy, admission control and container runtime hardening. - AWS networking for security: VPC design, endpoints and endpoint policies, network and DNS firewalls, egress control, and WAF. - Fluency with infrastructure as code such as Terraform, including reusable patterns, multi-environment rollouts and reading plans for security impact. - Experience with CNAPP, SIEM or runtime security tooling and the cloud detection sources around it, such as CloudTrail, GuardDuty and Access Analyzer. - Experience investigating cloud and infrastructure security events: correlating cloud audit, Kubernetes, identity and network logs to establish what happened, its blast radius and its root cause. - A track record of reviewing architecture and writing design proposals, guiding teams toward secure designs through conversation rather than mandate, mentoring others through reviews, and turning a review into a change another team is glad to make. - Python, Go or TypeScript for security automation. - Clear written and verbal communication, including explaining technical risk to non-technical partners. Most of our work with other teams is asynchronous, so much of the job is a well-evidenced finding, proposal or design note that another team can act on without a meeting. Desirable - Experience using AI agents in a SOC or other incident response workflows. - Sandboxed runtime experience with gVisor, Firecracker or Kata. - Offensive security or red-team experience in cloud and Kubernetes environments. - Policy engines such as OPA or Rego. - Supporting audits like SOC 2 with automated evidence collection. Our stack AWS, Kubernetes, infrastructure as code, CI/CD with federated identity, an enterprise identity provider, observability and cloud security platforms, and AI agent tooling. jobs.description: Hi 👋🏾, I’m Abhik https://www.linkedin.com/in/abhikpramanik/, Ashby’s Co-Founder and CTO. Ashby is growing fast, which means exponential growth across every product metric: jobs, applications, interviews, you name it. We’re not slowing down, and as a result, keeping Ashby performant and reliable is a company priority. We need your leadership to do that now and in the future. We’ve already assembled a fantastic Platform & Infrastructure team of 11 engineers (all Senior+, >70% Staff), and they’ve done an excellent job handling our growth, but the management and leadership of Platform & Infrastructure have been diffused across our Engineering leaders. As we hit our next level of scale, it’s time for us to hire an Engineering leader responsible for performance and reliability, and for building out the team that ensures those. Hopefully, that’s you! THE ROLE In this role, you will report directly to me, and your responsibilities will include: - Building and maintaining a long-term vision and 6-month roadmap for Platform & Infrastructure. - Growing the Platform & Infrastructure team. You’ll hire ICs, managers, and build out a headcount plan. This will include determining if more specialized roles need to be established (e.g., DB Admin). - Building and maintaining an excellent relationship with Product Engineering. The ideal state is that Product Engineering can move incredibly fast independently without breaking performance or reliability, and Platform & Infrastructure doesn’t feel like they’re always cleaning up someone else’s “mess.” Today, there’s a great relationship, but there’s always room for improvement! - Assessing and improving our monitoring and incident management process. Again, we’re doing relatively well here, but there’s always room to improve. For example, making uptime measurement easier and improving coordination with Support during incidents. - Maintaining vendor relationships and negotiating pricing for our critical hosting and observability infrastructure, including AWS, ClickHouse, Datadog, and Braintrust. They have a meaningful impact on gross margin and need to be kept in check. - You’ve managed managers. Managing other leaders is a very different ball game, and not everyone enjoys it or thrives in it. Within your first 6 months, you’ll most likely have to hire a manager underneath you. - If you have experience managing developer experience and developer tools, building out a dedicated team for DevEx. If you don’t have experience here, DevEx will report into Product Engineering. Happy to discuss once we meet! A big part of our secret sauce is how we run Engineering. We achieve incredible speed and quality by discarding many industry norms and being optimistic about Engineers. We consider what makes exceptional Engineers exceptional, then figure out how to hire them and build an environment that gives them the freedom and agency to be exceptional. You’ll be a key leader in ensuring that continues! This means: - You played an important role leading a company through a high-growth period (either as an IC Lead or Engineering Leader). You had to make high-quality decisions under pressure. You’ve designed interviews, interview loops, and led hiring strategy. - You have a track record of excellent collaboration with other departments. Recruiting teams wanted to schedule candidates faster, track interviewer preparation and quality, and do it with half the headcount. A recruiter needed to manually collect availability from the candidate, identify qualified interviewers, perform “Calendar Tetris” to find who is available to interview the candidate, schedule on the earliest date possible, and make any last-minute adjustments as availability changed. They must do this while considering the interview load on each individual and whether interviewers need to be trained and shadowing others. 🥵 TA software didn’t help. As hiring managers, we know TA is a critical function, and as engineers, we know software can do better. So, we built and continue to build Ashby to give TA teams the highest standard of tooling. Software that’s intelligent and powerful. Software that provides insights into where they’re failing and automates or simplifies many of the tasks they’re underwater with. We want other functions and departments to be jealous of what TA teams can do with Ashby, and today they often are! jobs.description: About the Role Hopper Technology Solutions (HTS) powers travel for some of the world's largest brands through our APIs, white label products and fintech, and every dataset we hold tells a story our partners need told clearly, repeatedly and fast. As a Senior Data Scientist on HTS you will own the analytical relationship with a portfolio of partners and build the machinery that answers their questions about supply health, pricing competitiveness and performance once, then answers them every week. You will be judged less on the sophistication of your models than on whether the people you work with, inside Hopper and across partner commercial teams, make better decisions because of you. What would your day-to-day look like - Own the analytical relationship with a portfolio of HTS partners, working alongside Partner Success and Commercial to understand what they need, deliver it, and present it directly to their teams - Design and templatize repeatable reporting on supply health, pricing competitiveness and tenant performance that scales across hotels, flights, homes and cars without being rebuilt each time - Use AI assistants, agents and code generation tools as everyday collaborators to automate the repetitive parts of analysis and reporting, and help the broader team adopt the same practices - Frame and run exploratory analyses that deepen our understanding of partner and traveler behavior, and translate what you find into clear recommendations for product, engineering and business leaders - Apply machine learning and statistical methods to large, messy datasets where they move the needle, and recognize when a simple, well explained metric is the better answer - Build dashboards and self serve reporting in BigQuery, Looker, Tableau, Amplitude and Google Sheets, with an eye toward making yourself unnecessary for routine questions - Partner closely with product and engineering so the data we collect supports the questions our partners will ask next An ideal candidate has - A degree in Math, Statistics, Computer Science, Engineering, Economics or another quantitative discipline, or equivalent practical experience - Extremely strong analytical and problem solving skills, with a track record of answering hard questions with data across more than one domain or product line - A proven ability to turn complex technical work into simple, credible narratives for non technical and executive audiences, including external partners - Comfort being partner facing, presenting findings, fielding tough questions live and building trust with commercial counterparts - Deep SQL skills and experience with modern data warehouses such as BigQuery, plus fluency in Python and Pandas or R for large scale data preparation and analysis - Hands on, daily use of LLM based tools such as Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor or Copilot for writing code, SQL, analysis and documentation, and a point of view on where they help and where they fall short - Experience building or deploying automated and agentic workflows, from scheduled pipelines to LLM driven report generation and prompt or skill libraries, that turn one off analyses into repeatable products - Experience with data mining, machine learning and statistical modeling, and the judgment to know when to reach for them - Experience with business reporting and experimentation tools such as Tableau, Looker or Amplitude - A strong bias toward simplifying, templatizing and shipping over polishing - Travel industry experience in lodging, air, vacation rentals or car rental, or in a marketplace, B2B platform or API distribution business, is a plus - Experience with geographic data in search, filtering or recommendation, or working with external customers in a consulting, solutions or customer analytics capacity, is a plus Perks and benefits of working with us - Well-funded and proven startup with large ambitions, competitive salary and the upsides of pre-IPO equity packages - Unlimited PTO - Carrot Cash travel stipend - Access to co-working space on demand through FlexDesk AND Work-from-home stipend - Please ask us about our very generous parental leave, much above industry standards! - Entrepreneurial culture where pushing limits and taking risks is everyday business - Open communication with management and company leadership - Small, dynamic teams = massive impact - 100% employer paid Medical, Dental and Vision coverage for employees - Access to Disability & Life insurance - Health Reimbursement Account (HRA) - DCA/ FSA and access to 401k plan About Hopper At Hopper, we're building the leading travel technology platform in the world, and we're doing it by solving real problems for real travelers globally. Our Hopper consumer booking platforms and HTS (Hopper Technology Solutions), our B2B business, work together to give travelers something the industry has never reliably offered: transparency, flexibility, and real savings on every trip. We combine massive amounts of data and AI with proprietary fintech products to make that happen, not just another booking engine, but a fundamentally better way to plan and experience travel for our customers and our partners. We are proof that better-for-the-customer and better-for-the-business can be one in the same And we're continuing to grow fast! The Hopper app has been downloaded over 120 million times, with 70% of our users being Gen Z and Millennials, next-generation travelers. Today, our biggest opportunity is powering travel fintech, commerce, and loyalty for some of the biggest brands in the industry. Our first HTS partnership with Capital One helped launch a dedicated travel portal for a major financial brand's cardholders, and we've since expanded across some of the biggest names in travel and banking, including Air Canada, Uber, Royal Bank of Canada (RBC), and Nubank, powering everything from a single fintech integration to a full end-to-end travel loyalty portal. That's our trajectory: we started as a small, disruptive app within the travel space, and now we're the engine under the hood powering how Travel Tech works. What that looks like in practice: - Billions of dollars in travel and travel fintech move through Hopper and HTS every year. - Our fintech products, including Cancel for Any Reason and Disruption Assistance for Any Reason, post exceptionally strong customer satisfaction because the terms are clear and resolutions are instant, no questions asked. - Nearly 30% of app customers add a fintech product to their booking, and those customers are 1.6x more likely to book with us again. - HTS now drives more than 90% of the business, proof of how fast B2B has scaled. - Through HTS, any travel provider (airlines, hotels, banks, travel agencies) can plug the company's fintech, commerce and AI solutions into their own channels, whether that's a single integration or a full end-to-end travel portal. Come take off with us! #LI-Remote While this role utilizes automated systems to assess candidate suitability, every actionable decision is made by a human member of our team. Under local regulations, you have the right to understand the principal factors used in this assessment, request a correction of your data, or request a human review of any automated decision. To exercise these rights, please contact recruitment@hopper.com

jobs.description: Cerebras Systems builds the world's largest AI chip, 56 times larger than GPUs. This architecture allows Cerebras to deliver industry-leading training and inference speeds; over 10 times faster than GPU-based hyperscale cloud inference services. This order of magnitude increase in speed is transforming the user experience of AI applications, unlocking real-time iteration and increasing intelligence via additional agentic computation. Cerebras works with the leading model labs, global enterprises, and cutting-edge AI-native startups. OpenAI recently announced a multi-year partnership https://openai.com/index/cerebras-partnership/ with Cerebras, to deploy 750 megawatts of scale, transforming key workloads with ultra high-speed inference. ABOUT THE ROLE We’re looking for an AI Engineer who loves building with new models, experimenting with developer tools, and writing about what they learn. You’ll create prototypes that demonstrate what fast inference makes possible, optimize the harnesses around models, and turn your findings into technical content that helps other developers build. This is a hands-on role on our DevRel team. Technical writing is a core part of the job. You’ll take projects from an interesting question through implementation, testing, and a clear explanation others can follow. You should be as comfortable debugging an agent workflow or comparing model behavior as you are writing a tutorial or presenting a demo. WHAT YOU’LL OWN - Technical writing: Write blogs, tutorials, walkthroughs, and practical guides grounded in your own experiments. Explain how things work, why implementation choices matter, and how developers can reproduce your results. - Prototypes and demos: Find original ways to showcase Cerebras fast inference. Build sample applications, notebooks, and interactive experiences that make the benefit tangible. - Harness optimization: Build and improve the code and workflows around models, including prompts, tool use, context management, orchestration, and evaluation. Identify bottlenecks and test ways to improve speed, reliability, and output quality. - Model experimentation: Try new models and investigate their capabilities, limitations, and fit for different tasks. Compare behavior on realistic workloads and turn useful findings into examples and recommendations for developers. - Evaluation and reproducibility: Design practical tests, measure results, and validate technical claims. Make your code easy to run and explain the assumptions, tradeoffs, and limitations behind your conclusions. - Launches and developer education: Partner with Product, Engineering, and New Media to create technically accurate launch examples, workshops, and stories. Present your work and help developers understand how to apply it. - Developer feedback: Engage with developers, troubleshoot integrations, and turn recurring questions and friction into improvements to examples, documentation, and the product experience. SKILLS AND QUALIFICATIONS - A strong portfolio of AI applications, prototypes, technical writing, tutorials, or other substantive developer-facing work. - Hands-on experience building with model APIs and debugging AI application workflows. - Excellent technical writing skills. You can turn a complex implementation or experimental result into a clear, useful explanation. - Experience working with agent harnesses or related workflows involving prompting, tool calling, context management, and evaluation. - An informed view of the AI developer ecosystem and curiosity about new models, frameworks, and emerging application patterns. - Strong technical judgment. You can design fair comparisons, verify results, and distinguish observations from assumptions. - Original ideas for demos and developer experiences, with a clear sense of what makes an example useful and engaging. - The ability to scope projects, ship independently, incorporate feedback, and collaborate with technical and creative partners. PREFERRED EXPERIENCE - Experience optimizing latency, responsiveness, or reliability in AI applications. - Contributions to open-source projects, developer tools, or publicly available technical examples. - Experience teaching developers through workshops, talks, or live demonstrations. PORTFOLIO Please include links to code, prototypes, and technical writing you’ve created. Identify what you personally built or wrote, explain the problem you explored, and share the results or lessons learned. Cerebras Systems is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome different backgrounds and perspectives and strive to create an inclusive environment where people can learn, grow, and do their best work. Why Join Cerebras People who are serious about software make their own hardware. At Cerebras, we have built a breakthrough architecture that is unlocking new opportunities for the AI industry. With dozens of model releases and rapid growth, we’ve reached an inflection point in our business. Members of our team tell us there are five main reasons they joined Cerebras: 1. Build a breakthrough AI platform beyond the constraints of the GPU. 2. Publish and open source their cutting-edge AI research. 3. Work on one of the fastest AI supercomputers in the world. 4. Enjoy job stability with startup vitality. 5. Our simple, non-corporate work culture that respects individual beliefs. Find out more about what it's like to work at Cerebras here https://www.cerebras.ai/join-us! Apply today and become part of the forefront of groundbreaking advancements in AI! Cerebras Systems is committed to creating an equal and diverse environment and is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate different backgrounds, perspectives, and skills. We believe inclusive teams build better products and companies. We try every day to build a work environment that empowers people to do their best work through continuous learning, growth and support of those around them. This website or its third-party tools process personal data. For more details, click here https://www.cerebras.net/privacy/ to review our CCPA disclosure notice.

jobs.description: ABOUT DOCKER Docker is the platform at the center of how intelligent software gets built. For more than a decade, Docker has helped millions of developers and thousands of organizations build, ship, and run software consistently across any environment. Today, Docker extends that same trust to the AI era. Docker Hardened Images https://www.docker.com/resources/containers-are-the-new-supply-chain-attack-vector-on-demand-webinar/?at_exp=DO112.B0 form the foundation agentic code is built on, local and cloud Docker Sandboxes https://www.docker.com/products/docker-sandboxes/?at_exp=DO112.B0 isolate where agents run, and Docker AI Governance https://www.docker.com/products/ai-governance/?at_exp=DO112.B0 sets enterprise-wide policy. Together, they give builders and organizations the confidence to adopt any model, tool, or agent without compromising security, governance, or control. _______________________________________________________________________ THE ROLE Docker's Platform Engineering team builds and operates the cloud-native platform behind Docker's products. Inside the company, teams across Engineering and the business rely on a growing set of internal applications, and each one is built, deployed, and run a little differently. We're looking for a Senior Engineer to give those applications a common foundation and then build the custom tools the business needs on top of it. You'll create a framework that makes it easy to build and deploy internal tools, including slack bots, web apps, workflows, etc, with authentication, hosting, observability, and alerting in place. You'll use it to build internally-facing tools to support cross-org efforts: roadmapping, headcount management, business reporting, etc. You'll decide when to build, when to buy, and when to integrate an existing product. You'll help shape how internal systems fit together across the company. This is a hands-on role. You'll own projects from scoping through rollout and adoption, working with platform leads, engineering teams, and business teams such as HR, Finance, Marketing, and Customer Support. _______________________________________________________________________ WHAT YOU'LL DO INTERNAL APP FRAMEWORK - Build and maintain a framework that makes it fast to create and deploy internal applications and services, with defaults for authentication, hosting, CI/CD, logging, observability, and alerting - Provide templates, documentation, and examples so teams can ship their own tools without starting from scratch - jobs.description: BUILDING THE FUTURE OF OPEN FINANCE Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout, xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system. It offers spot trading, margin, futures, staking, and OTC services, with products built for both individual investors and institutional clients. Forget crypto. Fintech/crypto are now one of the same. You’ll have real ownership of the design work: the experiences you shape, and how they look, feel and behave. You’ll work directly with product, engineering and leadership, with no layers of process between you and the work. This is a rare 0→1 opportunity. We’re straight-talking, no-nonsense, and deeply invested in the quality of what we build. We care about craft, we care about our customers, and we care about getting things right. If you’re excited by hard problems, high standards, no egos and the chance to build something genuinely new, climb aboard. THE OPPORTUNITY - Own design end to end: discovery, concept, prototyping, delivery and launch. jobs.description: ABOUT THE TEAM Mural helps teams think, decide, and follow through together. AI made producing content cheap. It did not make agreement, commitment, or follow-through any easier. The AI Workflows team builds the AI and agentic experiences inside Mural that help teams reach decisions and keep them. YOUR MISSION You will own the outcomes for new AI experiences from first idea to proven value. You will partner with the Engineering Manager and the Agentic Design Director for AI Workflows as counterparts, and together you will own the strategy. You will work with a wider team of engineers, ML engineers, designers, and product managers, moving from hypothesis to working prototype to evidence in weeks, not quarters. You will build prototypes yourself and decide what ships, what changes, and what we stop, based on what users do and what the evals tell us. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Set strategy for AI Workflows together with your engineering and design counterparts, own the outcomes and the evidence behind what we build, and engage deeply in the end-to-end user experience - Find the team workflows where AI adds clear value, at the intersection of collaboration, alignment, and decision making. - Build working prototypes with modern AI tools (Claude, Cursor, Codex, or similar) to test ideas with users before committing further investment. - Turn each release into a hypothesis with pass/fail criteria, and make the call on whether to iterate, scale, or kill it. - Define product-quality evals with engineering that measure usefulness, trust, and reliability, and own the call on whether an experience meets the bar to ship. - Decide with engineering and ML when to use frontier models, when to route across models, when to bring in a new model, and when a model of our own is worth building. - Understand the cost to serve each workflow, and work with growth and finance on how usage is metered and what the unit of value is. - Set up the data loops that improve quality, including what we collect, how we label it, and how it feeds evals and model work. - Design agentic experiences that work in real multiplayer sessions, where people need to understand, steer, and correct what the agent does. - Talk with users every week and bring what you learn back into the work. - Work with design, engineering, marketing, sales, legal, and security teams to align on shipping decisions. - Share what you learn across the product organization so other teams can adopt the practices that work. WHAT YOU'LL BRING - 7+ years in product management, including shipping at least one AI product from concept to real users. - Recent hands-on experience building agentic or LLM-based products, including what went wrong and what you changed. - Technical fluency to design and read evals, and to work as a peer with engineers and ML engineers on context management, latency, reliability, and failure modes. - Sound judgment on model decisions: comparing models, routing across them, adopting new ones, and deciding when fine-tuning or a custom model is worth it. - Understanding of AI unit economics, including cost to serve, usage-based metering, and how model choices change margin. - A record of launching, rebuilding, changing direction, and killing ideas based on evidence - Comfort making high-stakes decisions with incomplete information, and being candid about the tradeoffs. - Experience owning outcomes while partnering with expert engineering and design leaders as true counterparts. - Experience creating structure where no playbook exists. - Experience with collaboration or productivity software. - Experience with forward-deployed or customer-embedded product work. - Experience with agent interoperability, including MCP. Please contact us to request accommodation.

THE TEAM Founded in 2011, Kraken is one of the world's longest-standing crypto platforms, trusted by over 10 million individuals and institutions across the globe. It offers spot trading, margin, futures, staking, and OTC services, with products built for both individual investors and institutional clients. We're looking for a Sr. Data Analyst, Compliance to join our team remotely! The primary goal of this role is to elevate decision-making by uncovering emerging trends and root causes, and by driving insights and actions that provide full visibility into business performance and operational efficiency. Beyond technical expertise, success in this role depends on being a true business partner who combines data-driven insights with strategic thinking to deliver actionable recommendations, guide decision-making, and drive measurable impact across the organization. In this role, you'll own end-to-end data management, from building and maintaining datasets and pipelines to designing dashboards and delivering insights for the Compliance team. A core part of this role is owning the logic and rule-setting behind transaction monitoring across deposits and withdrawals. You'll also contribute to experimentation infrastructure, laying the groundwork for future ML and intelligence initiatives. THE OPPORTUNITY - Own the logic and rule-setting behind transaction monitoring across deposits and withdrawals, partnering closely with Compliance to study patterns and refine detection logic - Translate compliance requirements into production detection logic, preserving correctness across alert eligibility, thresholds, customer segmentation, date windows, and deduplication - Develop and maintain Python and SQL pipelines for transaction data preparation, feature engineering, and detection workflows - Evaluate detection rules and analytical models across coverage, alert quality, threshold sensitivity, and the impact of proposed changes - Design reproducible evaluations on historical data that account for limited labels, class imbalance, and shifts in customer behaviour over time - Own testing, deployment, scheduling, monitoring, and operational support for detection workflows, including investigating data quality issues, pipeline failures, and unexpected changes in detection results - Execute historical backfills with clear validation and traceability, and maintain reliable downstream alert delivery and integrations with compliance systems - Be at the forefront of data innovation by experimenting, testing hypotheses, and translating insights into action, while incorporating software engineering best practices into pipelines and dashboards. WHAT YOU BRING - 7+ years of experience in data analysis, data science, and data management within the fintech, crypto, financial services, or gambling industry, gained in a fast-paced, high-growth environment - Experience working with compliance, fraud, funding, finance, and customer support teams and analyzing large datasets, engineering features, and applying statistical methods to practical business problems - Strong Python and SQL skills, with experience building and supporting production data or analytical systems - Hands-on experience using dbt or similar tooling to model and organize high-fidelity data for reporting and decision-making - Experience setting up and managing data pipelines with a strong understanding of workflow orchestration, plus strong software engineering practices including version control, automated testing, code review, and CI/CD - Solid statistical foundation; ML exposure is a strong plus - Proficiency with BI and data visualization tools (e.g., Hex, Tableau, Power BI, or similar) to build executive-facing dashboards - Ability to investigate production issues independently and communicate technical findings and uncertainty to non-technical stakeholders - You believe wholeheartedly in the values outlined in Kraken's Tentaclements document - A degree in a field emphasizing analytical rigor, such as analytics, software engineering, statistics, or economics - Based in Canada, the US, or Brazil, and fluent in English NICE TO HAVES - Fraud detection, AML, anomaly detection, or other risk applications - Experience with Athena, Trino, Kafka, and Kubernetes alongside the core Airflow/dbt/S3 stack - Transaction pattern analysis, customer segmentation, and detection threshold tuning - Developing or productionising machine learning models, including experiment tracking and performance monitoring - Working with sparse or delayed feedback from investigations to evaluate and improve detection - Explainability, auditability, and change control in regulated environments Unless a specific application deadline is stated in the job posting, applications are accepted on an ongoing basis. Please note, applicants are permitted to redact or remove information on their resume that identifies age, date of birth, or dates of attendance at or graduation from an educational institution. We consider qualified applicants with criminal histories for employment on our team, assessing candidates in a manner consistent with the requirements of the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance. OUR COMMITMENT Payward is powered by people from around the world and we celebrate the diverse talents, backgrounds, contributions, and unique perspectives that everyone brings to the table. We hire based on merit, seeking out people with the right abilities, knowledge, and skills for the job. We encourage you to apply for roles where you don't fully meet the listed requirements, especially if you're passionate or knowledgeable about crypto. We may ask candidates to complete job-related skills or work-style assessments as part of our hiring process. These assessments evaluate competencies relevant to the role and are applied consistently across candidates for similar positions. Results are considered alongside experience and interviews, and are not the sole basis for any employment decision. As an equal opportunity employer, we don't tolerate discrimination or harassment of any kind, whether based on race, ethnicity, age, gender identity, citizenship, religion, sexual orientation, disability, pregnancy, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic as outlined by federal, state, or local laws.
